„cancelled" — kein neuerer Push, sondern `timeout-minutes: 60`. Der
Schritt „Build tests (CMake)" brauchte beim letzten vollstaendigen Lauf
(631b3d81) 51 min; danach fiel das MF-667-Tor („der Pruefstand muss
BAUEN"), und Windows lieferte fuer 19408cef kein Testurteil.

Ursache gemessen in build-tests-ci/build.ninja: 74 Testziele
uebersetzen die Format-Schicht jeweils selbst — 29 055 von 31 461
Objekten (92 %); uft_imd_plugin.c allein 80-mal. Die beiden Qt-Tests
aus MF-1350/1351 brachten 794 Objekte dazu (400 + 394).

Das Limit bleibt ein Haengerschutz (MF-432), nur mit Luft. Die
Behebung ist P3-10 (eine Objektbibliothek statt 74 Uebersetzungen);
sie ist mit dieser Entscheidung freigegeben und wird vor dem Bau als
Entwurf vorgelegt. Nachtrag mit den Messzahlen in docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md.

Eigentuemer-Entscheidung 2026-09-26: „Limit auf 90 + P3-10".

events.message:
fix(gui): das Pruefetor vor dem Oeffnen fragt die Registry — 92 statt 19 von 110 Korpusdateien — und oeffnet keine fremde Datei unter einem Ersatznamen (P2-2, MF-1351)

`DiskImageValidator::validate()` steht vor `MainWindow::openFile()`, dem
Explorer, dem Forensik-Reiter und `DecodeJob` und kannte eine feste
Liste von 17 Endungen plus fuenf Kennungen. Eine .imd, .d88, .td0, .woz,
.stx, .atr, .2mg ging mit „Unknown format" nicht auf, obwohl
`uft_disk_open()` sie ueber die Registry oeffnet.

Jetzt fragt es die Registry, wo Liste UND Kennungen ablehnen:
- die Liste bleibt fuer ihre Endungen ZUERST — die 19 vorher gueltigen
  Korpusdateien sind danach zeichengleich, hxcfe_720k.st bleibt
  „Atari ST Image" (Registry zuerst ergaebe MSX)
- Name „Beschreibung (Plugin)", Geometrie aus der geoeffneten Scheibe
  (0 -> -1, nichts aus der Groesse geraten), Fluss aus
  UFT_FORMAT_CAP_FLUX, keine Plattform
- Endungsentscheid und reiner Groessentreffer (Band 30..49) stehen im

P0-17: `DecodeJob` meldete bei Flussdateien Sektoren als gut, die niemand
gelesen hatte, und zaehlte bei Sektorabbildern ueber einen flachen
Versatz. Seit MF-1350 oeffnet er ueber `uft_disk_open()` (derselbe Weg
wie der Analysator), speist per `uft_d2_from_disk()` ins Modell und
leitet den Status JE SEKTOR aus `uft_d2_sector_t` ab:

  CRC_BAD / ID_CRC_BAD, WEAK, DELETED, MISSING
  UNCHECKED  Daten ohne Pruefsummenangabe (IMG, D64, ADF ...) — weder
             gut noch schlecht
  REJECTED   vom Modell abgewiesen — genannt, nicht verschluckt,

schlecht; Fluss ohne Sektorzerlegung endet mit „Lauf beendet — keine
Sektoraussage", ohne Haken im Status-Reiter. `sectorUpdate` traegt den
Kopf; vorher kamen Seite 0 und 1 eines Zylinders als dasselbe Paar an.

Teilergebnis". Gemessen daran, dass die Bruecke weniger Spuren fragte,
als die Geometrie hat — NICHT am Rueckgabewert von `uft_d2_from_disk()`:

events.message:
fix(imd): jede Sektor-ID war um eins zu hoch — und "data unavailable" kam als guter Sektor heraus (P0-18, MF-1348)

Eigentuemer-Freigabe 2026-09-26: "ja, P0-18 IMD beheben".

Das IMD-Plugin reichte die ECHTEN Sektor-IDs der Nummernkarte an
uft_format_add_sector(), das laut include/uft/uft_format_common.h einen
0-basierten INDEX nimmt und 1 addiert. Jede ID jeder IMD-Datei kam damit
um eins zu hoch heraus. Gemessen an der FREMD erzeugten
tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_pc160.imd: die Datei traegt die Karte 1..8,
gemeldet wurden 2..9 — 0 von 320 IDs richtig. Dazu, im selben Leseweg und
derselben Klasse "ID-Feld falsch gemeldet": die Zylinder- und Kopfkarte
(Bits 0x80/0x40) wurden uebersprungen, die ID nannte die physische Lage
statt des Sektorkopfs. Und ein Sektor mit dtype 0 ("data unavailable")
kam als GUTER Sektor voller 0xE5 heraus (status 0, crc_ok 1).

Warum kein Test es sah, obwohl imd auf T1 steht: die IMD-Tests finden
Sektoren ueber ein Kennbyte im INHALT, und MF-1068 hat an zwei echten
Aufnahmen die ZAHL der Sektoren abgeglichen (26 + 76 x 8 = 634), nie
ihre IDs.

Referenz (im Dateikopf): MAME src/lib/formats/imd_dsk.cpp,
imd_format::load() — sects[i].sector = snum[i]; track/head aus tnum/hnum,
wenn die Karte da ist; stype 0 ohne Daten. Dieselbe Quelle, die
docs/spec_verification.json fuer imd nennt.

Jetzt: uft_format_add_sector_with_id() mit der ID aus der Karte;
Zylinder und Kopf aus ihren Karten, sonst die Lage; "data unavailable"
behaelt die Fuellung, ist aber mit uft_format_mark_last_missing()
gekennzeichnet (MF-980); die Karten werden nur gelesen, wenn der
Satzkopf in die Datei passt (vorher las der Code die Nummernkarte ohne
diese Pruefung).

Rotbeweis zuerst: tests/test_imd_sektor_ids.c — eigener Zerleger fuer
die fremde Datei (befragt nicht dieselbe Quelle wie der Pruefling),
dazu synthetische Faelle mit IDs 0/0xC1/7/3, dtype 0 und den Karten.
Vorher 6 rot, danach 14 von 14. Mutationsmatrix 6 von 6 — im ersten
Lauf 5 von 6: "Kopfkarte statt Zylinderkarte" entkam, weil mein Fall
immer BEIDE Karten trug; die Einzelfaelle (nur Zylinder-, nur
Kopfkarte) sind ergaenzt. ASan+UBSan+bounds-strict (WSL, gcc 15.2):
test_imd_sektor_ids 14/0, test_imd_error_marks 2/0. Volle Suite im
Hauptbau: 553 von 553 gruen (1 benannter Skip, test_freezer) — keine
andere Stelle im Baum verliess sich auf die falschen IDs.

"imd steht auf T1b", richtig ist T1.

NICHT behoben, benannt (im Dateikopf und in P0-18): eine abgeschnittene
Datei verliert ihre letzten Sektoren ohne Kennzeichnung, und ein
Groessencode ueber 6 wird als 512 gelesen (MAME: 8192).

events.title: fix(883): nothing ships that nothing can reach
events.message:
fix(883): nothing ships that nothing can reach

Socket's scan of 0.1.2 reported SQL in dist/analysis/regression.js, which
nothing could run. It was the visible end of a shape: two tools absent from
DEFAULT_TOOLS whose handlers returned a sentence pointing at an unshipped
script, in front of an entry that always throws — and package.json allowlisted
dist/ wholesale, so it shipped.

An audit found the shape throughout:
- The TypeScript trace stack (query-events, taint, follow-path, loader-profile,
  trace-events, trace/store/*) shipped long after the daemon took its job. Its
  smokes were green, testing implementations no tool used.
- runtime_bookmark_add/_list failed on every store the live system writes
  ("Table with name trace_bookmarks does not exist"); their one green test
  used the dead store as its fixture. Deleting them orphaned the TS indexer
  chain, which trace-store.ts already said had moved to the daemon (802).
- ws-handlers and ingress-request served the deleted ws-server; a barrel
  nobody imported; four dead pipeline modules; buildD64FromGCR, writeback for
  the deleted TS 1541.
- Visible tools named tools that do not exist (runtime_session_undump,
  snapshot_dump) or that a session cannot see — ten redirects, including the
  steering project_init seeds and the snippet c64re setup writes.
- Hints that assume a checkout, in text a package user reads.

The rule: a module ships only if an entry a user can start reaches it.
check:dist-reachable walks the BUILT dist/ — where `import type` is erased,
which is how the trace stack looked alive — from the bin, the workbench and the
pipeline child; it fails on a shipped orphan and on a stale !dist/ exclusion,
both proved red before it went in. npm run build clears dist/ first: tsc never
deletes an output, so a deleted source's .js kept shipping from any machine
that was not a fresh clone.

Reduced to their types: flow-focus, trace-definition, asset-join-knowledge.
Excluded from the tarball by name: build-time platform-kb and fingerprint
extractor, the disk fixture builders, three modules the UI bundle compiles.

Fixing one hint exposed one that could not be followed: c64ref_lookup's
auto_build acted only on a missing file while its own note told a ROM-only
snapshot to rebuild. It rebuilds that too now — proved on a trimmed copy of
the real snapshot, the original restored byte-identical.

Also: smoke:input asserted the pre-BUG-026 mapping (Escape → RUN_STOP); it
now checks Escape → ← and Tab → RUN_STOP, 11/11. Spec 882 opened for the
backwards Exomizer depack the server can pack but not unpack; Spec 884 for

events.title: fix(diag): der Oberflaechen-Scan sagt ab statt hinter sector_status[36] zu schreiben, fragt nach den Nummern der Diskette — und bekommt einen Leseweg ueber den Greaseweazle (Tuerstufe 4, MF-1346)
events.message:
fix(diag): der Oberflaechen-Scan sagt ab statt hinter sector_status[36] zu schreiben, fragt nach den Nummern der Diskette — und bekommt einen Leseweg ueber den Greaseweazle (Tuerstufe 4, MF-1346)

Stufe 4 der vom Eigentuemer am 2026-09-26 freigegebenen Tuer fuer den
Oberflaechen-Scan (Folge von H-18). Umgesetzt in einem isolierten
Worktree, von einem Gegenpruefer zweimal geprueft (Runde 1 "nachbessern",
Runde 2 "annehmen"), vor diesem Commit SELBST nachgebaut und gemessen.

Teil A — Grenzen. uft_diag_init und uft_diag_surface_scan prueften
nichts. Gemessen gegen den Vorzustand:
  sectors = 37          UBSan (bounds-strict) "index 36 out of bounds for
                        type 'uint8_t [36]'" — reines ASan/UBSan schweigt
                        (Index 36 liegt in der Polsterung des letzten
                        Mitglieds; P3-550)
  sectors 64 nach init  ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE, nativ 0xC0000374
  sectors = 0           UBSan "division by zero", nativ 0xC0000094
  retries = 0           18 BAD bei 0 Lesungen
  tracks 85 / sides 3   angenommen (MAX_TRACKS 84 stand da, unbenutzt)
Seither: tracks 1..84, sides 1..2, sectors 1..36, sector_size >= 1,
retries >= 1, sonst -1 vor dem ersten Lesen; der Scan prueft tracks x
sides zusaetzlich gegen die in init angelegte Zahl, und die Grenze ist
EXAKT abgenommen (angelegt + 1 sagt ab, genau angelegt wird gelesen).

Teil A — Nummern. Der Scan fragte fest 1..n; eine CPC-Datendiskette
(0xC1..0xC9) war damit 72 von 72 BAD. An uft_diag_config_t angehaengt:
sector_ids[36] + sector_id_count (0 = altes Verhalten).

Teil B — Leseweg. src/diag/uft_diag_gw.c: ein uft_diag_read_fn ueber
uft_gw_read_track -> flux_decode_track -> Suche nach Nummer, C/H, beiden
CRCs und exakter Groesse. Jede Wiederholung ist eine NEUE Erfassung, nie
der Zwischenspeicher. Kein Schreibparameter, kein uft_gw_write*/erase*.
Den Takt fragt der Adapter per GET_INFO, weil uft_gw_open_stream()
dev->info nie fuellt (P3-551, geschuetzte Datei unveraendert).
Drahtbruecke des Emulators (MF-848): READ_FLUX stroemt, Write/Erase
werden gezaehlt, /TRK0 folgt dem Zylinder auf Wunsch (Vorgabe aus).

ABI, bewusst und im Kopf benannt: uft_diag_config_t 24 -> 64 Byte, alte
Versaetze unveraendert; uft_diag_ctx_t 88 -> 136 (die 40 der Konfiguration
plus das neue 8-Byte-Feld track_results_count), weil ctx config als Wert
einbettet. Uebersetzte Nutzer ausserhalb src/diag, include/uft/diag und
tests: 0. Im Adapterkopf: bei revolutions > 1 gewinnt die erste gute
Kopie (GOOD statt WEAK); kein Doppelschritt (fuer t > 0 BAD, Spur 0 GOOD).

Selbst nachgemessen im Hauptbau: ctest diag/entscheidet/gw_ 14 von 14
(einschliesslich der sechs Greaseweazle-Emulator-Tests, deren Bruecke
der Patch erweitert). Eigene Stichprobe der beiden Mutanten, die Runde 1
entkamen: ID-CRC-Pruefung gestrichen -> test_diag_gw_emulator 25 gruen /
4 rot; Anlage um eins zu gross -> test_diag_grenzen Absturz 0xC0000374;
Grundfassung danach wieder 29/0 und 24/0. Umsetzer und Gegenpruefer:
ASan+UBSan+bounds-strict (WSL, gcc 15.2) 7/7 ohne Befund; Mutationsmatrix
Teil A 14/14, Teil B 13/15 (entkommen und benannt ungetestet: FM-Weg,
Aufsummieren der Indexzeiten).

NICHT gemacht, benannt: eine Tuer im Produkt (Scan und Adapter haben 0
produktive Aufrufer; die Oberflaeche wartet auf Phase 6 des
GUI-Plans), FM-Weg, Zonenformate (eine Nummernliste fuer alle Spuren),
das doppelte free in greaseweazle_backend.c (P3-547).

events.title: floppy: refuse high-density tracks in UAE extended ADFs
events.message:
floppy: refuse high-density tracks in UAE extended ADFs

Every emulated drive is a double-density unit: it answers the drive-ID
poll as DD and turns at the DD rate, so at most 11 AmigaDOS sectors pass
under the head per revolution. A plain 1,802,240-byte HD ADF, an HD DMS
archive and an IPF recorded at the HD cell rate were already refused,
but the UAE-1ADF and legacy UAE--ADF decoders took a type-0 (sync 0)
AmigaDOS track of 22 sectors without a density check. The track was
then encoded into one DD revolution, a track no DD drive can read: a
bootable OFS HD disk in the extended container ended Kickstart 1.3's
boot in Guru Meditation #30010000, while the same disk at DD density
reached the CLI.

Both decoders now refuse an AmigaDOS track carrying more sectors than a
DD track holds, naming high density as the DMS and IPF paths do. Raw MFM
tracks carry their own timing and are left alone, as are the all-zero
raw-length blank tracks exporters pad extra cylinders with. The
configuration guide lists the high-density images that are refused.

events.title: fix: no hand-written SQL literals in the two stores that still had them
events.message:
fix: no hand-written SQL literals in the two stores that still had them

Socket's scanner flagged @trex64/c64re 0.1.2 with five "AI-detected code
anomaly" instances. Three do not hold against the code — id-path's baseRelative
is a constant at both call sites, effective-segments needs a segment end of 9e15
in the project's own analysis JSON, and service.ts's shell:true is a build step
the project owner typed. Two do.

trace-run-store.writeTraceRunHeader interpolated overheadMs raw while every
neighbouring value in the same INSERT went through num(). num() itself used
Math.trunc, which turns NaN into the bare word NaN and the statement into a
syntax error — verified against DuckDB: "Binder Error: Referenced column NaN was
not found". Both helpers now return NULL for a non-finite number, and overheadMs
takes a real() that keeps its fraction instead of a num() that would truncate it.

analysis/regression wrote payloadHash unquoted between a family that was escaped
and a cycle that was not. That is the shape this defect always has: not the value
nobody considered, but the one neighbour in a row of identical-looking ones. The
file now has the same two helpers and no hand-written literal anywhere — the
read paths were already correct and were converted too, because one literal left
by hand is how the next one gets missed.

Reachability, stated rather than implied: insertBaselineRun sits behind
runScenarioById, which always throws (scenario execution needs the runtime's
scenario_run). So the regression half is hardening of code that cannot currently
run, and no test covers it. The trace-store half is live and is proved: NaN lands
as NULL, 12.5 stays 12.5, and a quote in a name round-trips.

The README and Getting started told Linux users to run
`flatpak install flathub dev.copperline.Copperline`, but Copperline is
not on Flathub: the submission (flathub/flathub#9401) closed unmerged,
the AppStream API returns 404, and releases attach no .flatpak bundle.

  The Flatpak section becomes "build it yourself" from
  packaging/flatpak, with prerequisites, the build commands and the
  clean-checkout caveat. The lavapipe note, the command-line tools
  table and the VS Code chapter now refer to a self-built Flatpak.
- README.md: the Linux section is AppImage only, with a pointer to the
  Flatpak build instructions.
- packaging/flatpak: the local build recipe ran
  `flatpak run org.flatpak.Builder` without installing it and assumed
  a flathub remote. It now adds a user flathub remote and installs
  org.flatpak.Builder, as Flathub's own docs do;
  --install-deps-from=flathub already fetches the runtime, SDK and Rust
  extension. The README notes the Flathub status.

events.title: feat(881): the graph before the listing — a door and a measure
events.message:
feat(881): the graph before the listing — a door and a measure

The server's own instructions say the graph tools ARE the static analysis,
indexed, and that they come before opening a full listing. Nothing enforced it
and nothing measured it. Across the supervised runs of 2026-09-24/25 there were
103 reads of the rendered listing against 5 disasm calls, spread 25/19/17/16/14/12
over six participants.

D1, a door: read_artifact refuses a listing at >= 1500 lines until one of
graph_find / graph_node / graph_edges / graph_path / graph_overview was called
this session. Session, not process: the ledger is a file under knowledge/,
re-armed by agent_onboard the way 877 D4 re-arms the alias notices. The refusal
names the file, its size and the calls that open it, and does not come back for
that file.

D2, a measure: the ratio rides the contract footer, reports and never refuses,
and speaks only on a delta — run 7 of the unattended series moved model_assert
0 -> 12 by carrying its blockers back as a delta where run 6, without it, moved
nothing. It counts tool reads and says so; the 103 were shell reads an MCP
server cannot see.

The counter went into withGraph first and e2e:823 refused it — that spec draws
an import boundary around graph-tools.ts. The server's footer wrapper already
sees every tool by name and is the better home.

Also: the gate note now records the state captured at the START of the run, not
at the end, so an edit while the gate runs can no longer leave a note claiming a
tree the gate never saw.

Version 0.2.0, a minor and not a patch: D1 refuses a call that used to succeed.

Gates: e2e:881-graph-first 14/0, wired into gates.yml; full gate 83/83.

fix(716): identify a package positively, and cover the packaged launcher

smoke:ui-launcher went red, and it was right to. It hands ensureUiLauncher a
synthetic repo path — to exercise a directory with a space and an apostrophe —
which contains no scripts/workspace.mjs, so "no scripts/workspace.mjs means

A package is now identified positively: the built orchestrator present AND the
source entry absent. A checkout has both, a package has one, an empty directory
has neither and is treated as a checkout, which is the old behaviour.

The fix left the packaged variant uncovered, which is how the defect it exists
for got shipped in the first place, so the smoke now builds a synthetic installed
package and asserts the launchers it gets: no npm run workspace in either script,
the workbench started through the package, a c64re on PATH preferred over npx,
the package named rather than a path baked, and build-ui saying the bundle
already shipped.

events.title: fix(716): the workbench starts from the package, and the gate proves it starts
events.message:
fix(716): the workbench starts from the package, and the gate proves it starts

0.1.1 shipped a workbench that could not be started. The launchers project_init
writes ran `npm run workspace`, which is `tsc -p tsconfig.json && node
scripts/workspace.mjs`; an installed package has no tsconfig, no scripts/ and no
TypeScript, and `scripts/` is not in the tarball. Reported by a reader of the
published package. Every gate here was green.

The orchestration moved from scripts/workspace.mjs into
src/workspace-ui/launch.ts, so it compiles into dist/ and ships. Two doors reach
one implementation: scripts/workspace.mjs for a checkout, `c64re ui` for an
install. The package root is computed from the module, not from a caller's cwd
or a baked path.

The launchers now branch on what they were written beside. In a package they
invoke `c64re` if it is on PATH and `npx -y @trex64/c64re` otherwise, with no
build step and — the third defect reported — nothing baked: under npx the
package sits in a cache directory that changes every version and can be evicted,
so a path written into a project's launcher goes stale silently. The name is
stable; the path is not. build-ui says there is nothing to rebuild.

Also corrects `--help`: `setup` writes the process-discipline block into an agent
config (Spec 044), not "an MCP host configuration". Written two hours ago without
opening the file it describes.

THE RULE, recorded in the spec as §6a: every shipped component gets an acceptance
criterion that says it STARTS, not that it is PRESENT.

An earlier draft of this spec asked whether the UI belonged in the package. The
rewrite deleted that question and answered it silently. When that was corrected,
ui/dist went in and the gate learned to check the files were there — and §7 was
not extended, so nothing asked what starts it. Presence is not function, which is
this spec's own founding argument, missed one layer up.

The gate now starts the workbench from the installed package and fetches its
page: 705 bytes of the built bundle. It also asserts the launchers carry no
`npm run workspace` and no absolute path into the package.

events.title: SDL_mixer chunks on the voice mixer, and a ring device that costs 2%
events.message:
SDL_mixer chunks on the voice mixer, and a ring device that costs 2%

The ring device's refill stepped its source with
`while (acc >= frames) { acc -= frames; f += frame_bytes; }`, and
gcc 4.6 folded that into a closed form with a __mulsi3 call on every
output frame: 37% of an 8MHz STE with a callback that did nothing,
73% at 12517Hz. The converter (stdl_audio_convert, now in src/wav.c
with the WAV loader) steps a byte pointer and a 16-bit fraction, set
up with divu.w and mulu.w, one loop per layout. A callback in the
hardware's format - signed 8-bit at a DMA rate - now writes straight
into the ring. An empty callback costs 2% at either rate; converted,
13% for unsigned 8-bit mono at 12517 and 48% for 16-bit stereo at
22050, which plays at 25033 in stereo.

The SDL_mixer compatibility layer's chunks play on STDL_Voice, mixed
from the VBL, instead of in C over the ring device. On an 8MHz STE
one to four chunks at 6258Hz take 9/15/20/26%, where they took
58/83/99% and four overloaded it; at 12517, 18/29/40/51%, all of
which overloaded it before. A Mega STE takes about half. For ports:
- Mix_OpenAudio mixes at 6258 or 12517, whichever is nearer the rate
  asked for; a PC game's 22050 gets 12517.
- A chunk at full volume plays at half scale, the voice mixer's room
  for two loud sounds: 6dB quieter than before, so balances held
  against the music want re-checking.
- Chunks are converted to the device rate as they load, at most
  65535 frames (about five seconds at 12517); a longer WAV is cut.
- Mix_PlayChannel's loop count is exact, counted by the voice mixer
  through an internal stdl_voice_start; Mix_Playing reads the voice.

audio.c is split three ways: the DMA primitives and STDL_PlaySample
stay, the ring device moves to src/ring.c and the WAV code to
src/wav.c, so a program that plays only voices or one-shots links
neither. An example using voices alone is 12.5KB smaller.

Tests: tests/host/test_wav.c (each format, stereo kept and mixed,
rates up and down, a long source), test_mixer.c (the layer through
its own API), test_ring.c (the direct and converted refills, pumped
by hand) and a loop-count case in test_voice.c; the sound tests share
their fake-DMA helpers in ymtest.h. tests/hatari/mixbench.c measures
the ring device and the chunks. On target, voicechk.c still matches
the C twin at the same speed, loopwave's same-rate and resampled
stereo recordings match v1.12.0's, and examples/playmus.c plays every
other beep three times with a loop count. AGENTS.md records the
multiply no loop asked for; the headers, limits, porting guide, skill
and README carry the new figures.

events.message:
fix(716.2): read the tarball, not npm's stdout

The release run failed at the first gate with the same parse error this gate had
once before: Unexpected token 'P', "Pipeline ...".

`npm pack --json` does not silence the lifecycle scripts it runs, and prepack is
a full build that prints, so the report is never the only thing on stdout. The
first fix sliced for the last JSON array; the release job installs npm@latest,
whose array is formatted differently, and the slice found nothing and parsed the
build output.

Parsing a tool's chatter was the mistake both times. The tarball is the artifact
under test, so the gate now packs without --json, finds the .tgz it produced, and
reads the contents with tar -tzf — one answer, the same on every platform and
every npm.

Nothing was published: the tag check passed, this failed, and every step after it
including Publish was skipped. That is the ordering working as intended.

events.title: fix(879): the gate leaves a note, and the push does not prove it twice
events.message:
fix(879): the gate leaves a note, and the push does not prove it twice

Two problems, one push.

First, every master push ran the full 82 steps even when they had just been run
by hand a minute earlier — twenty minutes spent on ten minutes of answer. The
gate now leaves a note naming the tier it proved and the state it proved it on:
the commit, plus a digest of the working tree's dirty state. When that matches
what is being pushed, the hook says so and skips. An all note satisfies a docs
push; a docs note never satisfies an all one. No expiry, on purpose — the note is
keyed to the code, not the clock, and touching a file moves the digest, which is
exactly when the gate should run again.

Second, and the reason master is still not pushed: git connects to the remote
and fetches the ref list BEFORE it runs pre-push, so the SSH connection sits
open and idle for however long the hook takes. After ten minutes the server
closes it, and git dies of SIGPIPE writing the pack — exit 141, after the hook
has printed "push allowed". It happened at 370s and again at 599s, and never on
a five-second docs push. A repo-local core.sshCommand with ServerAliveInterval
keeps the connection warm; the global ssh config is untouched.

The first fix makes the second rare, but both are real: a gate that has to run
still takes ten minutes, and the connection still has to survive it.

events.message:
merge: Spec 716 — C64RE as an npm package, with the runtime beside it

The package is @trex64/c64re: packed, installed into an empty directory and
answering MCP on Linux, Windows and WSL2, started three ways — node, npm's own
shim, and npx. 1373 files and 23.2 MB of source tree became 642 files and 1.8 MB
that start; runtime dependencies went 13 to 4.

The runtime is fetched on first use rather than at install time, checksum-verified
against the release, into a per-version cache that the resolution chain now knows
about along with PATH. The pin is cross-checked against the sibling checkout and
the daemon's own protocol string, because two hand-maintained numbers that can
silently disagree only surface on someone else's machine.

Eight defects came out of it, and every one was found by leaving this machine:
c64ref_lookup needed a 27 MB derived file that is in no package and whose builder
fetches from the network; the Node floor turned out to be node:sqlite rather than
a version anyone could name; TRX64 built no Intel Mac while the installer claimed
to serve one; and five POSIX assumptions in the gate itself that only a Windows
runner could see.

Publishing is 716.6 and stays a human act.

The chapters were written by several models over time. Every chapter,
the custom-register reference and copperline.example.toml were checked
against the code:

- Prose: filler and repetition cut, run-on sentences split, terminology
  made consistent, British spelling with -ize endings throughout, ASCII
  only, and menu paths written with "->" everywhere.
- Accuracy: wrong flag defaults, menu labels, register offsets, file
  names, stale architecture descriptions and features wrongly listed as
  missing were corrected against the source. The example config no
  longer breaks when its extended_rom/fmv lines are uncommented.
- Coverage: undocumented flags, config keys, control-protocol methods
  and parameters, GDB monitor commands, console commands, launcher pages,
  menu entries and environment variables are documented, along with a
  table of the built-in expansion boards, the WASM plugin socket ABI,

events.title: cli: refuse flag combinations a run would silently drop
events.message:
cli: refuse flag combinations a run would silently drop

--benchmark-until, --gdb and --control each take over the run loop
before the App that fires scheduled work is built, so some flags were
accepted and then ignored:

- --control with --expect-screenshot never compared anything.
- --insert-cd-after was dropped by all three modes (only floppy
  inserts were refused).
- --exit-on-return under --gdb or --control never saw the program's
  return code, since neither watches the --run completion marker.

Each combination is now refused with an error naming the flag. Netplay
also refuses --pen-after, as it already did the other scripted pointer
input that only the local machine would see.

A lone --run PROG --exit-on-return now runs windowless and unthrottled,
like a lone --coverage: run_headless already accepted it as a capture
trigger and docs/guide/run.md already described it that way, but the
windowless check never included it, so it opened a window instead. With
--control-gui or --gdb-gui the session stays windowed as before.

events.title: ci(716.6): a version already on the registry is not an error
events.message:
ci(716.6): a version already on the registry is not an error

Two ordinary things land on the publish step with nothing to do: re-running a
release job whose publish already succeeded, and tagging a version that was
published by hand. The second is not an edge case — it is the FIRST release by
necessity, because a trusted publisher is configured on a package and cannot be
configured on one that does not exist yet.

Neither should paint the run red, and neither can be answered by publishing over
something, which npm forbids regardless. The job now asks the registry first and
skips the publish when the version is already there, while still running both
gates — which turns the v0.1.0 tag into a free end-to-end test of the pipeline
rather than a guaranteed failure.

events.title: debugger: decode ADKCON, BPLCON2 and DDF bits at their hardware positions
events.message:
debugger: decode ADKCON, BPLCON2 and DDF bits at their hardware positions

The IO Map and console CUSTOM decode tables had drifted from the chips:

- ADKCON/ADKCONR named WORDSYNC, MSBSYNC and FAST one bit high. Bit 11
  is UARTBRK, 10 WORDSYNC, 9 MSBSYNC, 8 FAST, as Paula and the disk
  controller already use them.
- BPLCON2 put KILLEHB on bit 10, which is ZDCTEN; KILLEHB is bit 9. The
  table now also names ZDBPEN, ZDCTEN, RDRAM and SOGEN, and shows
  ZDBPSEL as a field beside PF1P/PF2P.
- DDFSTRT/DDFSTOP were always masked to $FC, hiding the bit-1 comparator
  precision ECS and AGA Agnus honour. The decode now takes the fitted
  Agnus revision and uses the same ddf_register_mask the fetch sequencer
  does; BPLCON0 bit 4 likewise counts as BPU3 only on AGA.

New tests pin every ADKCON bit one at a time, the BPLCON2 names and
fields, and the per-revision DDF and BPU views.

events.title: feat(716): the package is @trex64/c64re, and a tag will publish it
events.message:
feat(716): the package is @trex64/c64re, and a tag will publish it

Name decided. Scoped, though not for the usual reason — there are no npm
siblings and probably will not be, because TRX64 and the U64 work are Rust and
801 settled that they ship as release binaries and a tap, never crates.io and
never npm. The scope is taken because it cannot be retrofitted: a name written
into somebody's MCP config is permanent, packages can be added to a scope
forever, and c64re-mcp could not have been moved under @trex64 later without
breaking every config naming it. The npm scope need not match the GitHub org and
does not — trex64-dev is the org, @trex64 the scope.

c64re rather than mcp inside the scope, because MCP is how the thing is reached
and not what it is; a TRX64-side server would otherwise find its name spent. The
executable follows and is now plain `c64re`, which is what the CLI has always
called itself in every subcommand — `c64re graph`, `c64re doc`, `c64re setup` —
with the bin name the one place it said otherwise.

Manifest completed for a registry: author, repository, homepage (the org's Pages
site, which is live), bugs, keywords, private:false, and publishConfig pinning
access public and registry npmjs. That last one matters: a scoped package is
restricted by default, and without it a publish is either refused or silently
private.

release-npm.yml publishes on a v* tag and nothing else, with no stored token —
npm trusted publishing over GitHub OIDC, which also generates provenance
attestations automatically, so the package carries a verifiable link back to the
commit and run that produced it. That is worth more here than for most packages,
because the thing being shipped runs inside somebody's agent. The workflow
refuses a tag that disagrees with the manifest version, and runs both 716 gates
against the artifact about to leave.

What it cannot do is the first publish: a trusted publisher is configured ON a
package, so the package has to exist first. Step one stays a human act, and it is
irreversible after 72 hours. Recorded as such in 716.6.

Gate green under the new name: 29 pass, 0 fail.

events.title: fix(st): eine Luecke in der Sektorfolge ist keine kleinere Geometrie — und der Seitenfehler war nie mit zwei Seiten geprueft (H-18, MF-1339)
events.message:
fix(st): eine Luecke in der Sektorfolge ist keine kleinere Geometrie — und der Seitenfehler war nie mit zwei Seiten geprueft (H-18, MF-1339)

H-18 verlangt, die beiden Fehler von CERTIFY 1.0 (Moore/Small, Antic
1988, certify.lzh!CERTIFY.C Z. 173-194; gesichtet in
docs/research/ATARI_COPY_TOOLS_2026-09-23.md) als Regression aufzunehmen:
der Fehlerzweig von Seite 1 liest erneut Seite 0, und EIN Leseversuch
auf Sektor 10 entscheidet 9 oder 10 Sektoren je Spur.

Gemessen, welche Stellen im Baum in dieser Klasse stehen:

1. uft_st_order_messen() setzte `spt = sector_count`. Fehlte auf der Spur
   ein Sektor MITTEN in der Folge (1..8,10), meldete sie `gemessen` und
   spt 9 — aus einer 10-Sektor-Spur wurde eine 9-Sektor-Spur, und
   Interleave und Spiralfaktor liefen ueber Feldpositionen, die keine
   physischen Plaetze mehr sind. Eine doppelte Nummer (Phantomsektor)
   ergab ebenso eine Messung. Jetzt: traegt die Spur nicht jede Nummer
   1..n genau einmal, bleibt `gemessen` false. Rotbeweis 3 von 5 rot,
   danach 5 von 5; test_st_spiralfaktor weiter 10 von 10.
   GRENZE, festgenagelt statt verschwiegen: fehlt der LETZTE Sektor ganz,
   zeigt die Spur es nicht — spt ist, was diese Spur traegt, nicht die
   Geometrie der Diskette. Das steht jetzt im Header.

2. uft_diag_surface_scan() nimmt die Geometrie aus der Konfiguration und
   wiederholt auf derselben Seite — richtig. Aber jeder vorhandene Test
   lief mit `sides = 1`, die Seitenlokalisierung war also ungeprueft.
   Neuer Test mit zwei Seiten (Seite 0 gut, Seite 1 Spur 5 kaputt) und
   einem Sektor 10, der erst beim zweiten Versuch liest: 10 von 10 gruen.
   Dass er rot werden KANN, ist gemessen: Mutation "immer Seite 0 lesen"
   (die CERTIFY-Gestalt) -> 5 rot; Mutation "nicht wiederholen" -> 3 rot.

Zwei Testdateien statt einer, weil uft_disc_diagnostics.h ein eigenes
uft_sector_status_t definiert, das mit uft_types.h kollidiert — beide
Header gehen nicht in eine Uebersetzungseinheit (Nebenbefund, nicht
behoben).

Produktive Aufrufer beider Funktionen: 0 (nur Tests). Keine der vier
Kennzahlen bewegt sich; die Einheiten sind richtig, bevor jemand sie
verdrahtet. Struct und Signaturen unveraendert.

Nicht gelaufen: ASan (keine Allokation im geaenderten Pfad).
Vorbestehend rot und unberuehrt: test_dms_loch_ist_kein_guter_sektor
(Windows-Wegwerfdatei, siehe CLAUDE.md).

events.title: fix(geos): 00/00 beendet die VLIR-Tafel, 00/FF ist ein leerer Platz — und einen Loeschvermerk gibt es nicht (H-12, MF-1338)
events.message:
fix(geos): 00/00 beendet die VLIR-Tafel, 00/FF ist ein leerer Platz — und einen Loeschvermerk gibt es nicht (H-12, MF-1338)

geos_parse_vlir_index() las den Record-Block eines GEOS-VLIR-Files gegen
drei Belege falsch:

- 00/00 galt als "Empty record", und der Lauf ging WEITER. Er ist das
  Ende der Tafel (GEOS.TXT:170-182; GEOS-2.0-Kernal _OpenRecordFile zaehlt
  bis zum ersten 00/00). Nichtnull-Bytes dahinter wurden als Records
  gezaehlt.
- 00/xx galt als "letzter Sektor, Byte ist Groesse" -> 00/FF bekam
  size 255. 00/FF ist der LEERE Record (Kernal _WriteRecord mit Laenge 0).
- Spur 0xFF galt als "geloescht". GEOS kennt keinen Loeschvermerk,
  _DeleteRecord schiebt die Tafel zusammen (MoveBackVLIRTab). Erfunden.
- num_records zaehlte nur "gueltige" Records statt der Plaetze; damit
  verschob jede Luecke alle folgenden Recordnummern, und der Rundlauf
  parse -> write schrieb nur 85 von 127 Plaetzen zurueck.

Belege: docs/format_specs/commodore/GEOS.TXT und CVT.TXT (eine Hand,
dieselbe Sammlung) und als FREMDE Hand der rekonstruierte GEOS-2.0-Kernal
von Michael Steil, github mist64/geos, kernal/files/files10.s — nur
gelesen, keine Zeile uebernommen (Kanal Spec).

Rotbeweis zuerst: tests/test_geos_vlir_gegen_kernal.c, 9 von 14 Zusagen
rot gegen den Vorzustand, danach 14 von 14 gruen. ctest -R geos: 5 von 5.

Jetzt: Lauf bis zum ersten 00/00, num_records = Plaetze (00/FF zaehlt
mit), records[] hinter dem Ende genullt, Rueckgabe 1 wenn hinter dem Ende
Nichtnull-Bytes stehen (forensischer Hinweis statt stillem Verwerfen).
geos_vlir_record_empty(): Spur 0. geos_vlir_record_deleted() bleibt als
API stehen und sagt immer false, mit Begruendung (MF-1077: umschreiben,
nicht loeschen). Header nennt den 254-Byte-Vertrag (Sektor + 2).

tests/test_geos.c hatte die falsche Deutung festgeschrieben (00/00 mitten
in der Tafel als "empty", FF/00 als "deleted"); die Zusagen sind
umgeschrieben, die alte Aussage steht zitiert daneben.

Produktive Aufrufer: 0 (gemessen, nur die zwei Tests). Die Korrektur
bewegt deshalb keine der vier Kennzahlen; sie haelt die Einheit richtig,
bevor jemand sie verdrahtet. Struct-Layout und Signaturen unveraendert.

Nicht gelaufen: ASan (die Einheit alloziert nicht).

events.title: YM effects: per-step noise, and steps that keep their length at 60Hz
events.message:
YM effects: per-step noise, and steps that keep their length at 60Hz

STDL_Sfx gains an optional `noises` array, one noise period per step.
With it, tone and noise are separate each step on the same voice:
periods[i] sounds the tone, noises[i] the noise generator at that
period, both together when both are set. A gunshot is a crack of
noise over a thump of tone on one voice, not two; an explosion a
noise whose period climbs as it fades, where before the noise period
was fixed for a whole effect. Without `noises` an effect reads
exactly as it did - tone throughout, or noise throughout with period
0 a rest - and initialisers written for the old struct compile
unchanged, though -Wextra now asks for the missing field.

Wanted by a port that approximates its sampled effects on the YM for
machines without DMA sound, where gunfire and explosions are most of
what matters.

Step timing: the tick counted 20ms a VBL, so after STDL_SetRefresh(60)
every effect ran 20% fast. It now counts in thousandths of a tick
against stdl_vbl_hz, as STDL_Music and the voice tick already do, so
a step lasts its step_ms at either rate. The headers, porting guide
and skill said effects could not compensate; they now list them with
the ones that do.

tests/host/test_sfx.c: the old tone and noise forms unchanged, per-step
noise sounding alone, with tone and handing the generator back, and an
80ms effect taking four ticks at 50Hz and five at 60Hz (four without
the change - the test fails on the old timing). examples/sfxdemo.c
adds three gunshots and a sinking explosion; recorded on an emulated
plain ST, the explosion's spectral centroid falls from 7.8kHz to
4.0kHz as it fades.

P3-545. src/formats/c64/uft_d64_g64.c las die G64-Geschwindigkeitstafel mit data[0x15C + i] — Schrittweite 1 statt 4 und fester Versatz statt 12 + 4 * n — und schrieb spiegelbildlich buf[0x15C + i]. Referenz: docs/format_specs/commodore/G64.TXT (je Halbspur ein 4-Byte-Eintrag LO/HI ab $015C). Gemessen an tests/corpus_free/vice_c1541_35trk.g64: 28 von 84 Eintraegen falsch, 26 von 35 Vollspuren in der falschen Zone. Produktiv: g64_load_buffer speist die Wandlung (uft_format_convert_bitstream.c, uft_format_convert_sector.c). Weil Leser und Schreiber denselben Fehler trugen, war jeder Rundlauf gruen; das Plugin src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c las die Tafel die ganze Zeit richtig.

Berichtigt: 4-Byte-Eintraege ab 12 + 4 * n; ein Eintrag ueber 3 ist laut G64.TXT der Versatz einer Zonentafel je Byte und passt nicht in das 8-Bit-Feld speed — abgesagt mit -4 statt gekuerzt; ein Kopf mit weniger als 84 Eintraegen wird nicht mehr an der festen Groesse 0x2AC abgewiesen, verlangt wird 12 + 8 * n; und die zwei Laengenbytes einer Spur muessen im Puffer liegen (offset + 2 <= size statt offset < size, vorher ein Lesezugriff hinter das Ende bei offset == size - 1).

events.title: grm-as0m: constantRegisterValue becomes a location + operation evaluator
events.message:
grm-as0m: constantRegisterValue becomes a location + operation evaluator

The all-or-nothing constant evaluator now walks backward over a location
(A, X, Y or C), stops at the last instruction that writes it, and asks a
ConstantSemantics implementation what that instruction leaves there; each
input it reads is another walk under the same guards. carryValueBefore --
a second walk that duplicated every guard of the first -- is gone: carry is
just another location.

Mos6502ConstantSemantics is the table implementation (design (a)). New over
the old mnemonic list: SBC, ROL/ROR A, carry out of ASL/LSR/ADC/SBC and
CMP/CPX/CPY, and the memory-operand forms of AND/ORA/EOR/ADC/SBC/CMP over a
load the scanner resolves. writes() is the union of the mnemonic modifier
tables and the instruction's p-code result objects, so an undocumented
writer (LAX) now stops the walk instead of being stepped over.

StoredValueScanner.semanticsFor(program) is the seam for design (b), a
p-code evaluator selectable per program (grm-4wqd).

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK. realrom-test.sh check nes
pass=32 fail=2 (dodge = grm-q1bi stale golden, lwings = known bistable
ede6/ee2e/ee8d), patched decompiler; no row moved.

Merge pull request #23 from vibecodekun/feat/cycle-accurate-mode

Add the opt-in cycle-accurate compiler and separate NES runtime, including review fixes for MMC1 bank folding, ordinary-ROM startup, verifier failure handling, and Linux libm linkage.

Independent validation: AccuracyCoin 144/144 at alignment 0 and 143/141/143 at alignments 1-3, with native/interpreter/oracle trace parity; 12,000-frame stress and 3,000-frame SMB3 World 1-1 route parity at all four alignments; nine audio checks; Windows and Linux builds, CPU helper checks and synthetic MMC1/startup regressions; eleven verifier tests. Default output from the combined tree is byte-identical to current master for SMB3, Mega Man and AccuracyCoin (180 files).

The nonzero-alignment AccuracyCoin failures and remaining hardware/host limitations are documented. Trace parity is distinct from hardware correctness. Review corrections: d2c125de914cec5e53ff3b2270cc6df998503641.

events.title: The voice mixer's loops run four samples to a pass
events.message:
The voice mixer's loops run four samples to a pass

Each voice-sample paid a dbra, 12 of its 68 cycles, just to go round
the loop. The body is now written out four times with .rept, so the
dbra comes once in four samples. A run that is not a multiple of four
enters its first pass part-way in: every instruction in the body is a
fixed size, 16 bytes in all, and a jmp (d8,PC,Xn) skips (-run & 3)
bodies. The source still holds one body, in a macro shared by the
store variant for a block's first voice and the add variant for the
rest. The clamp pass is unrolled the same way; a block is 128 frames,
a whole number of passes, so it needs no part-way entry.

tests/hatari/voicechk.c: all 120 random mixes identical to the C
twin, and 400 four-voice blocks in 2065ms against 2305ms before - 10%
off the mixing. Four busy voices at 6258Hz now take 25% of an 8MHz
STE, down from 28%; the header, limits, skill and voice.c quote the
new figure. The C twin is unchanged. ovvoice.c still reads no border
misses.

events.title: Put the modules in MUSIC as well, for the STE to play
events.message:
Put the modules in MUSIC as well, for the STE to play

The port now plays the original ProTracker modules on an STE or Mega
STE, on its DMA sound, and keeps the YM streams for every other ST. So
each module goes into MUSIC unchanged as <NAME>.MOD, beside the
<NAME>.STM converted from it - the same 8.3 name, which is how the game
asks for both and plays whichever the machine can.

A track whose YM conversion fails still ships its module, and the
note about it now says a plain ST will be quiet there while an STE
plays the original. The summary counts tracks rather than files, so
it still reads 21 rather than 42. About 720KB more in the download.

The fixture test compares every module against the port's own copy
from tools/make-music.sh, byte for byte, as it already did for the
streams: 21 of 21. The page, the README and the zip's header comment
say what MUSIC holds now; the README's source map also said "deflated"
for the zip, which has been stored since 614086b.

events.title: SetVoice masks the stores, not the arithmetic
events.message:
SetVoice masks the stores, not the arithmetic

STDL_SetVoice worked out the voice's step inside stdl_int_off(), and
that division is a __udivsi3 call, about a scanline on an 8MHz
machine. A module player calls SetVoice from the voice tick, around
2ms into the frame - where an open top border's Timer A lands, with a
line and a quarter of grace - and on an STE the border was lost every
few seconds while the music played. Never on a Mega STE, whose tick is
done before line 32.

Found by breaking on the miss path in Hatari's debugger and reading
the interrupted PC off the ISR's stack: every miss had interrupted the
move to SR that ended SetVoice's masked section. The step, table row
and 16.16 bounds are now computed first and only the stores are
masked.

tests/hatari/ovvoice.c opens the top border and counts misses for
20 seconds each with the device idle, with four voices looping, and
with all four retriggered from the tick after a delay that sweeps the
calls across Timer A's window: 18 misses on the last before the change,
none after; the port that found it went from 55 to none over the same
scene. AGENTS.md records the rule: a call a tick or ISR may make does
its arithmetic first and masks only the stores.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: The voice mixer accumulates in 16 bits, in 68000 assembly
events.message:
The voice mixer accumulates in 16 bits, in 68000 assembly

Four voices at 6258Hz took 45% of an 8MHz STE, measured under a port
playing four-channel modules: gcc 4.6 compiled the per-voice loop,
which clamped every sample with two compares, to about 170 cycles a
voice-sample. Each voice now adds into a block of 16-bit sums and the
block goes to the ring through one clamp table. The inner loop is a
byte fetch, a table fetch and an add, hand-written, with the 16.16
step split so add.w/addx.w carry the fraction into the index. Each
voice works out once per stretch how many frames it can run, with a
divu.w rather than __udivsi3, so the loop has no end test. Four
voices now mix a block in 5.8ms: 28% of the machine.

The C loop stays beside the assembly (voice_run_c) as the twin
tests/host exercises. tests/hatari/voicechk.c runs 120 random mixes
of one to four voices - short samples and one-frame loops included -
through both on target and compares them byte for byte, then times
them: all 120 identical, 400 four-voice blocks in 2305ms against
3505ms for the C.

Two behaviour changes come with it, both fixes:

- Clamping once is the sum. Clamped per voice, three loud voices
  saturated at +127 before a fourth negative one came back down.
  A host test sums 3 x 63 - 64 and wants 125; the old mixer gave 63.
- A loop carries its overshoot. The wrap restarted on the loop's
  first frame and dropped the fraction, so a loop a few frames long
  came back late every time round and played flat - measurably, for
  the 8- and 16-byte loops modules use. The fraction now carries in,
  as Paula's period counter does. A host test of an eight-frame loop
  at a step of 1.5 fails on the old wrap and passes.

stdl_voice.h, docs/limits.md and the skill carry the measured cost;
AGENTS.md points at voicechk.c for anyone touching either loop.

grm-x5g2: publish iNES Mapper / NES Board as top-level Program Info properties

ProgramDB.getMetadata(), which the About/Info program dialogs display, skips
every Program Information option whose name contains '.', so grm-3ppn's
"Retro Machines.iNES Mapper" / "Retro Machines.Board Name" were written at
import but never shown. Rename the two human-facing keys; nothing in code reads
them, and the machine-read Retro Machines.* keys stay second-tier on purpose.
A JUnit guard pins the names as delimiter-free.

Also retires two owner-answered table extents in human-research-todo
(dragonpower $8F00 = 31, rcransom 9352 = 25), which makes the
lowest-target bound exact on six of six hand-read tables.

events.title: docs(open-items): P3-542 war doppelt vergeben — und zwei Baum-Befunde aus der Paketmessung (MF-1336)
events.message:
docs(open-items): P3-542 war doppelt vergeben — und zwei Baum-Befunde aus der Paketmessung (MF-1336)

In e60d3e7d trugen docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md:656 (0x4489) und :658 (Rezept-Maschine) beide P3-542: beim Zusammenfuehren rueckten die GEOS-Posten von 538/539 auf 540/541, zwei der drei Rezept-Kit-Posten auf 542/543, der dritte blieb auf 542. Die Rezept-Zeile ist jetzt P3-544; der eine Verweis in docs/neue_ideen_urteile.json zieht mit.

Neu: P3-545 — uft_d64_g64.c:551 liest die G64-Geschwindigkeitstafel byteweise ab festem 0x15C und :661 schreibt spiegelbildlich; G64.TXT fuehrt 4-Byte-Eintraege, uft_g64.c:344 liest sie mit read_le32. An einer echten VICE-G64: 28 von 84 Eintraegen falsch, im PRODUKTIVEN Wandlungspfad, und jeder Rundlauf ist gruen, weil Schreiber und Leser denselben Fehler tragen. P3-546 — uft_pll.c rechnet DD/HD mit der Datenbit-Periode (4000/2000 ns), uft_flux_pll.h:345 mit der MFM-Zelle (2 us); an synthetischem 250-kbps-MFM 3998 von 3999 Laeufen falsch, aber ohne Produktivaufrufer (Bestand). Beides Decoder-/Formatschicht: eingetragen, nicht still umgestellt.

Das Belegtor wies die erste Fassung zurecht ab: P3-546 nannte kein MF, und ein Beleg ohne die Nummer, unter der er entstand, ist nach MF-843 keiner. STAND.md zuletzt erzeugt.

events.title: netplay: pin recomp-net bdc58b6 (observers), host finishes the SRAM transfer, fresh session per harness run
events.message:
netplay: pin recomp-net bdc58b6 (observers), host finishes the SRAM transfer, fresh session per harness run

- lib/recomp-net -> RetroPortingToolKit feat/nes-spectator bdc58b6 (03ee1b1 +
  an observer never predicts, opens, follows or NACKs an episode). A
  spectator now keeps up (4 seats + 1 spectator online x2 rounds: sim 1208
  vs host 1203, 0 invents, 0 episodes, same confirmed digest, survives the
  rematch).
- Host-authoritative SRAM barrier: the host takes the finished transfer back
  and FINISHES it, as the guest does (measured with NES_NET_SRAM_SYNC=1: 8192
  bytes delivered before boot in 1-13 ms, match then runs; 4/4 runs PASS).
- rb_loopback.sh: a fresh session id per run. Every run used id 1 on the
  same ports, so the previous run's parting BYE ended the next match as
  'peer gone' (1 in 3 back-to-back runs, SRAM or not; 8/8 after).
- rb_lobby.sh: spectators join after the players are seated; the headless
  room lingers after the last match so every peer can report the room.
- 'peer gone' says whether it was a BYE or 1.5 s of silence.

events.title: fix(tests): 27 Tests gaben ihre Spuren nie frei — und fuenf davon mit einem Aufraeumer, der nur die Haelfte kannte (MF-1335)
events.message:
fix(tests): 27 Tests gaben ihre Spuren nie frei — und fuenf davon mit einem Aufraeumer, der nur die Haelfte kannte (MF-1335)

Der Sanitizer-Lauf zu e60d3e7d war rot, und zwar nur im Schritt
"ASan-Rueckstand gegen fallende Grundlinie": seit diesem Commit ist das
Tor scharf, ohne dass `docs/asan_baseline.txt` existiert, also zaehlt
jeder Leck-Fehler. Gemessen waren es 27 Tests (CI-Lauf 35813314830),
alle "Subprocess aborted" durch LeakSanitizer — und KEINER davon durch
eine Aenderung am Produktivcode: `uft_format_plugin.c`, `atari_check.c`
und `uft_kryoflux_stream.c` sind in e60d3e7d unveraendert. Der Rueckstand
war alt; neu war nur, dass er zaehlt.

Behoben statt eingefroren. Die Grundlinie zu saeen haette die 27 fuer
immer erlaubt; die Kennzahl heisst "leckende Tests null halten".

Die Ursachen, gemessen an den Stapeln (84 von 108 Meldungen aus
`uft_track_add_sector`):

  * 5 Tests: wortgleicher Nachbau von uft_track_cleanup(), der nur
    `t->sectors` freigab, nicht `t->sectors[i].data`. Jetzt ruft der
    Helfer den kanonischen Aufraeumer (MF-1177, eine Rechnung).
  * 8 Tests: `free(X.sectors); free(X.raw_data);` von Hand — dieselbe
    Luecke, 37 Stellen. Ersetzt durch uft_track_cleanup(&X), nur wo X
    nachweislich ein uft_track_t ist.
  * 10 Tests: Spur gelesen und nie freigegeben, der Lesefehlerzweig
    sprang mit `continue` heraus. Aufraeumen hinter der letzten
    Verwendung und vor jedem solchen `continue`.
  * atari: `check_result_t` auf dem Stapel, `r.issues` nie frei
    (check_free() gibt auch die Struktur frei, passt also nicht).
  * kryoflux: `uft_kf_init()` ohne `uft_kf_free()`.
  * d64: `zurueck` und `orig` nur im Fehlerzweig freigegeben.
  * td0: die IMD aus uft_td0_to_imd() nie freigegeben; uft_imd_free()
    ist die passende Freigabe (der Wandler ruft sie selbst, und sie
    gibt die Struktur nicht frei, die hier auf dem Stapel liegt).

Der Produktivcode macht es richtig: 22 Aufrufe von uft_track_cleanup()
in src/, zwoelf Tests ebenfalls. Die Lecks lagen alle in Tests.

Abnahme, lokal gemessen statt auf CI gewartet:
  * Unter MinGW gibt es kein ASan. Die genaue Quelliste je Test kommt
    aus build-tests-ci/build.ninja und wurde unter WSL (Ubuntu, gcc 15.2)
    mit -fsanitize=address und den ASAN_OPTIONS des CI-Auftrags gebaut.
  * Rotbeweis: 27 von 27 rot mit Lecks — derselbe Befund wie CI
    (z. B. dms 6 Lecks, CI 6).
  * Nach der Korrektur: 27 von 27 gruen, 0 Lecks.
  * Windows-Bau der 27 Ziele: 0 Fehler; ctest 24 gruen, 3 rot — genau
    die vorbestehenden tmpnam()-Faelle (d13, dms, do), die VOR jedem
    Spurlesen scheitern ("Wegwerf-Datei fehlgeschlagen").

Am Werkzeug gemessen und berichtigt, bevor es schrieb: die erste Fassung
des Block-Zerteilers setzte in test_pro_gegen_atari800.c:320 ein
Aufraeumen vor das `continue` einer INNEREN Sektorschleife — das haette
die Spur mitten in ihrer Auswertung freigegeben und das `continue`
unbedingt gemacht. Die Vorschau zeigte es, geschrieben wurde es nicht;
die neun zuvor behandelten Dateien sind nachweislich nicht betroffen.

events.title: netplay: lobby fixes (identity fits 31 chars, session keys before caps, LAN members), cold-boot resume reset, digest mutation test, size guard, capability matrix
events.message:
netplay: lobby fixes (identity fits 31 chars, session keys before caps, LAN members), cold-boot resume reset, digest mutation test, size guard, capability matrix

- game_version is '<=18 of the release pin>+<12 hex of exe SHA-256>': the
  lobby carries 31 characters and a longer identity made every join fail
  version_mismatch.
- The engine's widescreen key is registered before the room publishes its
  caps (a first match was refused 'host did not settle widescreen').
- runtime_session_reset clears a pending guest-resume request and the frame
  continuation state: the offline Play after a rematch resumed $8057 on
  zeroed RAM. After the fix it equals a fresh process (RUN_DONE identical).
- NES_RB_PROBE=mutation: one byte per partition flips exactly that
  partition's digest and restores (8/8). _Static_assert on SaveStateData.
- rb_lobby.sh: waits only on the peers, refuses a server that failed to bind.
- docs/NETPLAY.md: capability matrix with measured evidence, open defects.

techniques: shared Atari ST and Amiga regression testing
project.notes: The repository root builds an enhanced Atari ST version from the corrected historical source and a separate native Amiga port, sharing gameplay changes but keeping independent source trees. It also contains an independent preserved-original Atari ST build in src_orig, catalogued separately. The enhanced Atari output uses a TOS launcher and disk image; the Amiga version supplies native bitplanes, input, Paula audio and AmigaDOS handling. The documented Amiga baseline is PAL OCS/MC68000, Kickstart 1.3 and 512 KB Chip plus 512 KB expansion RAM; an explicit 68020-only variant is available. The original build is explicitly not byte-identical; do not infer byte identity for the enhanced versions. Real Amiga hardware remains unverified.

events.title: ci(716.5): WSL2 proved, the /mnt warning measured, and the Linux job given room
events.message:
ci(716.5): WSL2 proved, the /mnt warning measured, and the Linux job given room

WSL2 works. Debian-13 under wsl-version 2, node installed inside it, the package
packed, installed into an empty directory and answering MCP three ways: 29 pass,
0 fail. The job asserts /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop too, so a green run
cannot mean it quietly ran somewhere else.

The /mnt warning is now a number instead of a phrase. Both filesystems run the
full check: 23s on the distribution's own disk, 31s under /mnt, both 29/0. That
is a third slower — not the "great deal" INSTALL.md claimed — so INSTALL.md was
corrected to say what was measured, while noting that this check is not a
file-heavy workload and a disassembly listing is, so the gap widens with the
work. The advice survives; its justification changed from assertion to
measurement. That was the deal this step was built under.

Also raises the Linux job's timeout from 15 to 30 minutes. Spec 716 added two
steps to it and the package one is expensive by nature — a full build through
prepack, a real npm install including a native dependency, three MCP sessions —
which pushed a job that used to finish in ~11 minutes past its own limit. The
first symptom was a bare "The operation was canceled" with no failing step above
it, which reads like a flake and is not one.

events.message:
netplay: session offers from the offline selection, confirmed-frame check, tick cost, rb_sweep.sh

- Session seal: a key may register an OFFER (what the host proposes, e.g.
  read from the offline mod selection -- a match commits no mods) and a game
  may register a finalize rule run after a whole image is applied (SMB:
  co-op excludes widescreen). A peer handed no image (env-driven host, LAN
  room) runs its own offer; the mod-set handshake refuses a mismatch.
- nes_mod_runtime_commit_netplay_c / nes_mod_feature_selected: vanilla
  commit for any netplay launch (launcher or env), and a selection query.
- Environment-driven launches that are refused (scripts, recording, a
  failed start) exit instead of opening a launcher that has no room.
- NES_NET_SHOT_TICK / NET_TICK_DIGEST: the frame and state digest every peer
  confirmed at tick N (rewritten by each replay of N), compared by

  identity's content fingerprint.

  and N64 sweeps run, 3 and 4 seats of co-op at 0 / 200 ms / 2% loss,

events.title: netplay: rollback over recomp-net's episode driver (INCREMENTAL), N seats, shared lobby
events.message:
netplay: rollback over recomp-net's episode driver (INCREMENTAL), N seats, shared lobby

Engine (always built, inert unless netplay or the probe runs):
- src/rollback/nes_rb_state.c: the rollback snapshot is the V7 save-state
  image plus a trailer (logical input seats); the per-tick digest is taken
  over the SAME serialized bytes, partitioned cpu_wram / ppu / apu_io_mods,
  cached until guest code runs. SMB: 167 KB image, save 7 us, load 40 us,
  digest 57 us p50.
- src/rollback/nes_rb_probe.c: NES_RB_PROBE=start:span:count[:gap] -- save,
  run N, load, run N with the recorded rows forced, compare every tick's image
  byte for byte and name the first differing fields; symmetry check after
  every load; NES_RB_PROBE=digest for 'digesting does not perturb the guest'.
- main_runner.c: the rollback tick gate at the top of the OUTERMOST frame
  callback (snapshot/digest/load there, rows applied right before the NMI,
  replayed ticks skip present/pace/audio delivery), and under rollback the
  guest continuation is restarted from (resume PC, charged) at the end of
  EVERY outer callback. The probe found why: SMB's idle JMP $8057 is charged
  3+2 cycles in func_RESET but 3 then 2 per iteration in the resume target
  func_8057_b0, so a resumed timeline fired the next VBlank one CPU cycle off
  (40/40 probes diverged at runtime_blob nes_cycles/ops_count). With the
  restart: 0 divergences in 148 probes (attract, 1P, 4P co-op with deaths).
  Netplay off: 3000-frame smoke, savestate files and 1P/4P scripted runs are
  byte-identical to the pre-change build.
- src/rollback/nes_session_config.c: the session configuration seal (keys a
  match may vary; the host's image is applied before boot, confirmed through
  the driver's mod-set handshake, never persisted).

Netplay (nesrecomp_enable_recomp_net):
- nes_netplay_rb.c binds RNetRbHost (snapshots via rbengine's ring, 1-byte
  pads active high, A|START injector bits, replays_changed evidence).
- nes_netplay.c: N seats (2-4; seat 0 hubs LAN for >2 or the lobby relay),
  spectators on the relay, identity (game_version = version + exe SHA-256,
  ROM SHA-256), pre-boot host-authoritative SRAM barrier + guest sandbox,
  refusal of scripts / recording / --loadstate / TCP execution control
  online, soft return, coordinated drain (SIGUSR1, NES_NET_MATCH_TICKS).
- nes_host_lobby.c: thin adapter over recomp-ui's recomp_netplay_host
  (replaces nes_launcher_netplay.c and the private 1.3k-line lobby client +
  WebSocket copy, which no longer compiled); headless room for harnesses.
- tools/rb_loopback.sh: 2-4 seat two-process soak with exact ledger,
  coordinated drain and a confirmed-frame digest/PNG comparison.

events.title: fix(716.5): a runner environment variable does not cross into WSL
events.message:
fix(716.5): a runner environment variable does not cross into WSL

The gate ran green inside WSL2 on the first try — 29/0, all three start paths
including npx. The step then failed on the line after it: GITHUB_ENV: unbound
variable. setup-wsl gives run steps a shell inside the distribution, and the
runner's own environment is not in it, so carrying the timing from one step to
the next through $GITHUB_ENV could never have worked. $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
would have failed the same way.

Both filesystems are now measured in one step, and nothing reads the runner's
environment. The numbers go to the log instead of a summary table — a table
nobody can write is worth less than two lines that always appear.

WSL2 itself is not the problem and never was: the distribution came up, the
interop check confirmed it really is WSL, node installed, and the package
packed, installed into an empty directory and answered MCP three ways.

events.title: ci(716.5): WSL2, which turns out to be testable after all
events.message:
ci(716.5): WSL2, which turns out to be testable after all

This spec said WSL2 could not be proved on a GitHub runner, because the images
lack nested virtualisation. That was out of date and the claim is withdrawn:
nested virtualisation arrived with the Dadsv5 image in January 2024, WSLv2 works
from windows-2022 onward, and Vampire/setup-wsl defaults to version 2.

A third job asks two different questions.

A — does the package install and run inside the distribution, on its OWN
filesystem? That is the route INSTALL.md tells people to take, and it is the one
that decides whether WSL2 is supported.

B — does it still work from /mnt, and what does that cost? The boundary warning
is the only WSL-specific claim the document makes, and it is a claim about COST,
not correctness. So B gates on the package working in both places and prints the
two wall times into the run summary. If the numbers ever stop supporting the
advice, the advice is what changes rather than the test.

The job also checks it really is under WSL — /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop
exists only there — so a green run cannot mean it quietly ran somewhere else.

Known flaky rather than impossible: actions/runner-images#12321 reports
windows-2022 + WSL hanging after an otherwise successful step.

ncr5380: drop the TT-MFP interrupt line on reset-parity/interrupt, check phase when DMA mode is armed

Two things a 5380 driver can rely on that the emulation did not do on the TT:

- Reading the reset parity/interrupt register (7) cleared scsi->irq but
  left the TT-MFP GPIP7 line high (only the Falcon FDC IRQ was cleared),
  so the next ncr5380_set_irq() produced no edge and the interrupt was
  lost. Drive the line low there, as the Falcon path already clears its
  IRQ source.

- Setting the DMA mode bit in the mode register while the target is
  already in a phase other than the one in the TCR raises the
  phase-mismatch interrupt on the real chip. The emulation only noticed
  the mismatch on the next CPU access to the chip. Run the phase check
  when DMA mode goes from 0 to 1.

Atari System V (UniSoft SVR4) arms DMA after the command phase and sleeps
for exactly that interrupt; with both changes its disk driver completes
its first DMA read instead of waiting forever.

events.title: control: add leftdown/leftup/mousemove fifo events for mouse injection
events.message:
control: add leftdown/leftup/mousemove fifo events for mouse injection

The command fifo could inject key events, doubleclick and the right
mouse button, but not the left button or any pointer motion - leaving
GEM desktops and mouse-only programs undrivable from the fifo.

Add three events to hatari-event:
- leftdown / leftup : left mouse button, mirroring rightdown/rightup
- mousemove <dx> <dy> : relative motion in emulated screen pixels,
  injected the same way host SDL motion is (KeyboardProcessor.Mouse).
  Absolute positioning is achieved by pinning the pointer into a
  screen corner with a large negative move (the OS clamps at the
  edges) and then moving by the wanted coordinates.

Verified by driving the TOS 2.06 desktop headlessly: opening a GEMDOS
drive window, navigating folders and launching a program with clicks
only. Note that VDI drivers may scale mouse deltas (the Nova VDI
applies its ms_speed setting, x4 by default), so absolute targeting
must account for the active driver's scaling.

events.title: fix(716.5): resolve npx the way npm is resolved, not through a quoted shim
events.message:
fix(716.5): resolve npx the way npm is resolved, not through a quoted shim

The Windows run got all the way to the last check: the shim npm wrote runs, does
an MCP initialize and answers a tool call as c64re-mcp.cmd. Only npx failed, and
it died inside its own CJS loader.

Cause: the command was passed to a shell as "npx.cmd" — quoted. Quotes tell
cmd.exe the string is a path, so it stops searching PATH; it found something else
and tried to load it.

Resolved the same way npm already is. npm_execpath points at npm-cli.js and
npx-cli.js sits beside it, so this Node spawns that directly: no shell, no shim,
one code path everywhere. The fallback keeps an unquoted npx.cmd for a run where
nothing set the variable.

--no-install as well, so a missing bin fails instead of quietly reaching for the
registry.

A failing session now prints eight lines of stderr instead of three. Three was
exactly one line short of naming the module that could not be loaded, which cost
a CI round trip.

29 pass, 0 fail locally.

events.title: test(716.5): run the executable the way a harness runs it, not the way a test does
events.message:
test(716.5): run the executable the way a harness runs it, not the way a test does

Every session this gate opened was `node <entry>`. No harness does that — a
harness names the command, and the name is a shim npm wrote. The gate checked
that the shim EXISTED and never ran it, which says nothing about whether it runs:
on Windows it is a .cmd that Node refuses to spawn without a shell, and a config
saying "command": "npx" goes through a second one.

The stdio plumbing is now one session() helper, and the gate completes an MCP
handshake three ways: node <entry> as the baseline, npm's own shim, and
`npx <name>`. On Windows the shim is quoted and run through a shell, because
that is what a harness ends up doing and a temp path is not guaranteed
space-free.

npx gets the install directory as its cwd rather than a temp directory — that is
how it finds a locally installed bin at all, and running it from elsewhere sent
it to the registry for a package that does not exist yet, where it hung. The
other sessions keep running from elsewhere on purpose, to prove the server does
not lean on the cwd.

This is one step short of the documented command: `npx -y @c64re/mcp` adds only
the registry fetch, and that cannot be proved before the package is published.
Verdaccio would close that half, and was weighed and left out — the official
action is a Docker container action and therefore Linux-only, and for a single
package with no internal dependencies it proves dist-tags and resolution we do
not have. The honest way to prove the documented command is a prerelease under
its own dist-tag, which is 716.6 and is the owner's call.

29 pass, 0 fail locally. Also records Windows as proved in the spec: run
36183644245, both jobs green.

"Under Atari System V that made every such call
into a PLT stub - the displacement's low word being the page's first
word - branch to an odd address (BSR.L with displacement $FFFFxxxx
read back as $FFFFFFFF, target PC+1) and the process died with an
address error; XFaceMaker2 was the first program with a PLT call at
exactly that spot.

Keep the deferral for the words ahead, but fault when the word being
returned is the one that never arrived: the instruction is using it."

Third Windows finding, and the first one outside the package gate: the runtime
gate died with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME, 'Received protocol d:'. An
absolute Windows path handed to import() parses as a scheme, and the loader is
right to refuse it. pathToFileURL is the portable way.

The package gate itself PASSED on Windows in that same run, which is the result
this job was added for: pack, install into an empty directory, start the
executable, speak MCP — on a Windows shell, with npm's shims and a drive letter.

Also marks the Intel-Mac cross build proved in the spec: TRX64 run 36174907622
built all six targets green, macos-x86_64 among them, with no tag and nothing
published.

events.title: fix(716.5): run npm through node, not through a shim or a shell
events.message:
fix(716.5): run npm through node, not through a shim or a shell

Second Windows run, second way to fail at the same line: spawnSync npm.cmd
EINVAL. Naming npm.cmd fixed the ENOENT and walked into Node's refusal to spawn
a batch file without a shell — the BatBadBut fix.

Reaching for shell:true there would have traded the problem for quoting. Every
path in this gate comes from mkdtemp, and a temp path containing a space would
have broken silently and later.

npm is now run the way it is already running: npm_execpath is set inside any npm
script and points at npm-cli.js, so this Node spawns that directly. One code path
on every platform, no shell and no shim. The fallback covers a direct
`node scripts/e2e-716-package.mjs`, where nothing set the variable — both ways
proved green locally.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BvAfYUMHmgDKLNXLRwau6B

events.title: fix(716.5): npm is npm.cmd on Windows, and execFileSync does not guess
events.message:
fix(716.5): npm is npm.cmd on Windows, and execFileSync does not guess

The first Windows run died before it packed anything: spawnSync npm ENOENT.
execFileSync looks for a file called exactly "npm" and does not consult PATHEXT,
so the shim npm actually ships as on Windows was never found.

Named per platform rather than passed shell:true, which would hand the whole
argument list to a command interpreter for no benefit.

This is the second thing the Windows job found that the local run could not, and
both were in the gate rather than in the package.

events.title: ci(716.5): run the package gate on Windows, where the claim actually lives
events.message:
ci(716.5): run the package gate on Windows, where the claim actually lives

INSTALL.md claims C64RE installs and runs on Windows with PowerShell, and §5 of
the spec says a route may not be called supported before it is exercised. Until
now that claim was written from the shape of the problem rather than from a run.

A second job on windows-latest runs the package gate and nothing else: pack,
install into an empty directory, start the executable, speak MCP, read the
shipped knowledge base, spawn the pipeline child. That is where every platform
difference actually lives — npm writes .cmd/.ps1 shims instead of a symlink,
paths carry a drive letter and backslashes, and the child is spawned by a
different loader. The runtime gate rides along because it is pure JavaScript.

Writing it found three POSIX assumptions in the gate itself, all mine: two
`mkdir -p` shellouts, and a .bin check that looked for an extensionless file npm
does not write on Windows. Fixed by construction — mkdirSync, and a check that
asks whether npm linked the executable rather than whether one exact filename
exists.

The other 80 steps are deliberately not repeated there. They are
platform-independent logic over temp directories; running them twice buys a
slower signal for the same answer.

No WSL2. GitHub's Windows runners do not offer it, and the third-party actions
that exist install WSL1, which is not what INSTALL.md describes. Proving it with
something adjacent would be worse than leaving it marked unproved.

scripts/gate.sh now reads only the `gates` job, so the local run stays 82 steps
and does not re-run the Windows pair — or its `npm ci`, which would reinstall the
tree underneath the run.

events.title: assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master f1ec64f45a
events.message:
assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master f1ec64f45a

Rebuilt from upstream master at f1ec64f45a (2026-09-25) with no local
patch and no unmerged pull request. Pull request 1179, which the
previous refresh merged on top of master while it was open, was split
up at review and every part has landed in master as its own commit, so
the memory it gives back now comes from upstream: free memory at a
--run program's start is within 800 bytes of the previous ROM (758,624
vs 759,424 bytes on a 1 MB chip-only A500, 1,793,920 vs 1,794,720 on a
2 MB A1200).

The build links .rom at 515,936 and .ext at 508,386 bytes of the
524,288-byte banks. The ext bank had 682 bytes spare before; icon.library
no longer links zlib's deflate into the kickstart (15d1417e3a).

Among the upstream changes that reach the ROM:

- m68k DOS packets and LoadSeg hunks are allocated from the high end of
  free memory (42e43be60a, ed7865194b), keeping the low block contiguous
  for software that updates Copper pointers with 16-bit writes. A --run
  program now loads near the top of memory, which exposed the coverage
  and DAP profiling bugs fixed in the two preceding commits.
- amigavideo programmed DDFSTOP one fetch unit past the last one ($DC
  for a 640-pixel FMODE 0 hires line) while charging that unit in the
  modulo; Agnus stops fetching at $D8, so every line started 4 bytes
  early (66496fd516, AROS issue 1235).
- the level 1-6 interrupt handlers restore INTENA's master bit on exit,
  so a program that enables interrupts itself under Disable() no longer
  freezes at the first vertical blank (8480de989a).
- screen user Copper lists work again (11d17ac37f), cd.device CD32
  playback, cached CD_INFO and Akiko read-stream fixes, OpenLibrary
  matching Kickstart's low-word version check on m68k, afs-handler
  read-ahead limited to free buffers, ATAPI transport hardening, and
  Shell and console.device/handler fixes.

The timing-test golden is re-blessed for the new boot handoff phase, as
on every refresh. Seven rows move by 1 to 6 E-clock ticks and row 31
(beam cck across a DIVU loop in a 6-plane display) by 46; that row is
bistable on the handoff phase, and the previous ROM gives exactly the
new values when the disk is inserted at 14.6 s instead of at power-on.
The other 44 probes are pixel-identical. The DAP hello-one-frame
cpuprofile golden is re-blessed too: the program's functions are
unchanged and the capture now spans from the breakpoint to the first
video frame boundary.

The full unit and integration suites pass. Of the asset-gated --ignored
suite only the hardware- and network-gated tests and the two
pre-existing failures (run_flag_boots_and_runs_a_guest_binary,
mhi_m2_savestate_resume) fail, identically under the previous ROM.

events.title: dap: step until copperline/profile has its frames
events.message:
dap: step until copperline/profile has its frames

copperline/profile {"frames": N} issued one step_frame {"n": N}, but a
step_frame is a CPU-budget quantum, not a video frame. Resumed after a
breakpoint it only finishes the interrupted quantum, which can end
inside the same video frame; the capture then commits no frame and the
report fails with "profile contains no precise sample frames". Whether
it worked depended on where in the quantum the breakpoint landed, and
the refreshed AROS ROM's timing lands it early in a frame.

Step one quantum at a time and poll profile.status until the capture
reports done, stopping early on any stop that is not a step, bounded at
four quanta per requested frame. When the first quantum already crosses
a frame boundary (the case the DAP golden was blessed under) the result
is unchanged.

events.title: coverage: stop counting when the --run program returns
events.message:
coverage: stop counting when the --run program returns

A --coverage run counted every instruction retired inside the program's
code ranges until the boot script's completion marker appeared. That
marker is written by C:Done, which the script loads after the program
returns, so when the loader places Done over the program's freed hunks
its instructions were counted as the program's. AROS master now
allocates m68k LoadSeg hunks from the high end of free memory
(ed7865194b), which makes exactly that reuse the normal case: the hello
probe reported entry() entered twice and scale() four times.

When the arm catches the program, the machine now records the longword
that names its seglist (the CLI's cli_Module, found through the new
OsMemory::process_seglist_slot) and checks it at every retired
instruction. The CLI clears cli_Module when the command returns and
before it unloads it, so the first mismatch closes the collector and the
counts cover exactly the program's lifetime. The lcov file is still
written on the completion marker, so --coverage --exit-on-return keeps
the program's return code.

Under the current bundled ROM the per-line and per-function records are
unchanged; only the "outside the program" total now ends at the
program's return.
