events.title: fix: the entry-point slot is for addresses, and the note says so to the reader it has
events.message:
fix: the entry-point slot is for addresses, and the note says so to the reader it has

One autonomous run saw this about thirty-five times:

    Note: the entry-points slot held X_analysis.json; it was read as the
    analysis JSON. Pass --analysis <path> to say so outright.

on calls that had passed `analysis_json` correctly, naming a flag the MCP
schema does not have.

There is no caller left that passes the analysis positionally. Both doors
— `disasm_prg` and the L2 chain in `prg-workflow` — push `--analysis` by
name, every script that spawns the CLI puts the JSON in slot 4 behind an
explicit entry-point slot, and a direct CLI reproduction with those
arguments prints nothing. The note's own branch only fires when the
entry-point slot holds a `.json`, and on the MCP surface exactly one
thing can put it there: `entry_points`, which was never checked.

So `disasm_prg` now reads every `entry_points` entry by the one address
rule before it spawns anything, and refuses a non-address by index. When
the value ends in `.json` the refusal names `analysis_json` as the
parameter that takes it — which is the sentence the note could not say.

The note itself still exists for the CLI's own positional recovery and
now names both doors, each labelled with where it belongs. The one place
in the repo that still taught the positional form — the annotation
prompt's verification snippet — uses `--analysis`.

events.title: fix: a routine annotation may be a name alone
events.message:
fix: a routine annotation may be a name alone

The loader took a `routines[]` entry with no `comment` — it reported
"applied 81, skipped 0" — and the renderer then died on
`comment.split("\n")` in `segmentHeader`, so a file the tolerant loader
had just accepted took the whole disassembly down with a TypeError.

The two halves disagreed about which fields a routine entry owes, and
the type was the one that was wrong. A routine carrying only an address
and a name is a real annotation: it names the routine and it renames the
label, which is most of what the entry is for. The graph importer has
always read it that way (`comment: … ? … : null`).

So `comment` is optional and the renderer prints the name header alone.
`name` is what a routine entry cannot do without — the renderer reaches
for `.name.toUpperCase()` at the same place — so the loader now refuses
that entry by section and address, with a "did you mean" for the keys a
human reaches for instead, and the rest of the file still applies.

The gate carries all three shapes: a commentless routine at a segment
start (where the block header renders, which is where the crash came
from), a commentless one that is not, and one with no name at all.
Against the old code it fails with the reported TypeError and nothing is
written.

docs: 867 — the window a payload owns, and who is resident in it

Identity was never the problem: a node already carries its owner. The missing
fact is the window a payload occupies when it loads, so seeding filtered by
owner alone refused six modules their own entry points and let a wide payload
inherit fifty-two seeds from whatever else shared its span.

The owner's split: load-time context from the payload, runtime context from
residency or from the load call that put the bytes there.

events.message:
grm-p3dy: mechanics spike -- a fall-through override into an overlay is accepted by the listing and rejected by the decompiler

FallThroughIntoOverlayProgramTest pins what Ghidra 12.1.3 does with
Instruction.setFallThrough into an overlay space, each row verified
against the source first: the override lands (one FALL_THROUGH ref,
always USER_DEFINED); CreateFunctionCmd's single-space FollowFlow ends
the base function at the overridden instruction and the overlay copy
becomes its own function; but PcodeEmit emits a BRANCH into the overlay
and FlowInfo bounds a function's flow to the entry's address space, so
the base function fails to decompile outright ("Could not find op at
target address"). FlowOverride.CALL_RETURN does not rescue it. The
finding and the options it leaves are on the bead for the owner's
ruling; the durable Ghidra fact is the decompiler-no-cross-space-branch
memory.

events.title: grm-k5m: widen the copy-loop evidence gate -- program-wide direct callers, retry of declined loops, and the payload's own decode
events.message:
grm-k5m: widen the copy-loop evidence gate -- program-wide direct callers, retry of declined loops, and the payload's own decode

CopyLoopAnalyzer materialized a recognized copy only when a JMP/JSR into
the destination sat within six instructions of the loop (the CHRGET
shape). Real cartridges copy several stubs into RAM at boot and RETURN;
Wizards & Warriors copies three AxROM bank-switch routines to
$0300/$032d/$033d and calls them from four banks, and none was ever
disassembled, so bank 2 and bank 3 sat unread in the ROM.

The gate now has three legs, tried in order, and the loop's EOL comment
names the one that carried the decision:

  1. the original lookahead;
  2. any DIRECT JMP/JSR into the destination from anywhere in the
     program (LoopIdioms.findFlowIntoRange), with every declined loop
     re-examined on each later analysis round (retryDeclined, keyed on
     its NOTE bookmark) so a caller disassembled later still counts.
     Direct only: COMPUTED_JUMP refs from the decompiler's jump-table
     over-read (grm-eyn) landed inside two of megaman's data copies and
     the first cut materialized them;
  3. PayloadDecodeEvidence: the source bytes decode as a self-contained
     subroutine (every instruction in range, no computed flow, reaches
     RTS/RTI or a JMP out). This is what admits wizwarr's stubs -- their
     callers live in the banks the stubs select, so leg 2 can never fire
     -- and its six data copies all fail it.

TransferMaterializer.disassemble now clears the destination's code
units first: Ghidra's data-reference analysis had planted an undefined1
at $0300, and DisassembleCommand silently refused to overwrite it, so
COPY_0300 came out initialized and empty. Gate 0's refusal also says
"the source is RAM" instead of "supply the ROM image" when it is.

wizwarr: $0344 bank -> 2, $0325 bank -> 3, helper-argument notes at
$0302/$032d (bankComments 17 -> 19). ironsword materializes the same
far-read stub. Fixtures copyfar.prg (caller before the loop) and
copychain.prg (late evidence via another copy, mid-range entry);
PayloadDecodeEvidenceTest pins the three stubs and the negatives.
Full synthetic gate green; realrom check nes reviewed row by row and
blessed except dodge/rcproam/lwings (grm-q1bi, bistable), steady state
pass=30 plus the known four.

events.title: Unresolved switch sites get an EOL gap comment beside their bookmark (grm-3ou part 2)
events.message:
Unresolved switch sites get an EOL gap comment beside their bookmark (grm-3ou part 2)

Every site annotateOrWarn/annotateForked bookmarks now also carries an EOL
comment in the resolved case's vocabulary, so the gap is visible in the
listing and says which kind it is:

  bank -> 5 (bank=5) via FUN_c000                (resolved, unchanged)
  bank ? via FUN_c000 [WARNING: analyzer limit]  (ours)
  bank ? [NOTE: helper argument]                 (honest)

The marker is deliberately "bank ?", never "bank ->": every consumer in the
repo (RealRomDump's count bankComments, ~20 VerifyBankTest criteria, the
probes) reads "bank ->" as "resolved here", and a gap comment sharing it
would inflate that metric by the population it must stay distinct from.

Gap comments route through BankCommentProvenance like bank comments, so a
site that later resolves has its gap replaced, not stacked. That needed the
provenance/AnnotationGuard deferral marker to become a family (varargs):
the record holds one segment per address, so the two kinds defer to each
other exactly as each defers to itself.

Measured: synthetic SUITE OK with no criterion edits; 14 goldens blessed,
62 lines added / 0 removed, all COMMENT ... bank ?, each at a bookmarked
address (checked over the whole corpus, not only the diff). Real-ROM
check nes: pass=28 fail=6, the documented set; no real-ROM golden moves
because RealRomDump does not sample the gap channel. The two bookmarked
sites without a gap comment are Phase 3 requirement violations -> grm-seah.

New: BankGapCommentProgramTest (one test per exit), four marker-family
cases in BankCommentProvenanceTest, a note in docs/testing.md.

events.title: control: per-session token on the remote-control socket
events.message:
control: per-session token on the remote-control socket

Localhost-only still means every local user on a shared machine, and the
discovery file told any of them the port. A listening IDE now generates a
per-session token and requires it as the first line on every connection
('auth <token>'; anything else is an error and a drop), and the discovery
file carries it — written owner-only (0600), in an owner-only directory
(0700), so the people who can read it are exactly the people who could
already drive the IDE from its own session.

The shim takes --token or PIST_CONTROL_TOKEN, falling back to the
discovery file's third field, so zero-configuration operation is
unchanged: with the IDE started locally, pist-mcp still needs no flags at
all. listen(0) no longer publishes, so test runs stop overwriting a real
IDE's file (the test side effect the file had since it was introduced).

Verified: the file lands 0600 with port and token, a raw connection
saying anything but the token gets 'error auth required' and a drop, and
a flagless pist-mcp finds and authenticates against the running IDE.
tst_remotecontrol gains the two gate tests (wrong token, command before
auth) and every existing session authenticates.

events.title: control: three correctness items, and label breakpoints that always resolve
events.message:
control: three correctness items, and label breakpoints that always resolve

- read returns the document as JSON {path, text}: the block protocol ends
  on a lone '.' line, which assembly source can contain — raw text could
  truncate there. Errors on block-framed verbs (read, readmem, disasm,
  cmd) go back as blocks too, so a block wait never sits out its timeout
  on a plain error line.
- open answers 'error could not open' when the path never opened, via a
  new openPathQuiet: the interactive open shows a modal on failure, and
  a modal nobody can dismiss (offscreen, or an agent at the other end)
  hung the verb forever.
- profile stop blocks until the save is parsed (new profileResultsReady
  signal), so results called right after are this run's data, never the
  previous run's; results now carry numeric counts with the same
  tie-break order as the profiler table and gutter.
- pist_problems gains severity: the resolved diagnostics live in a member
  (severity never reached the tree widget — it was only a text colour).
- breakpoint-by-label resolves through a base-independent nextCodeLine
  over the listing (LineMap/ProgramLineMap): a label on its own line has
  no code there, so the toggle lands on the first code line at or after
  the definition — before Run too, where the program map is unresolved.
  An equate finds nothing and is a clean error.
- The stop verb, lost to an edit slip in the previous round, is restored
  and pinned in tst_mcp alongside the other pre-existing mappings.

Verified live: open failure is a prompt error, read comes back as JSON,
'count' resolves to hello.s:22 (not the bare label at :21) and the
breakpoint fires there, and profile stop returns only with parsed
results in hand.

events.title: test: the gate that reads the process boundary from both sides
events.message:
test: the gate that reads the process boundary from both sides

Thirteen MCP doors spawn the pipeline. The gate drives every one of them over
stdio against a temp project and holds each to both halves of the rule: every
file the door left in the project has a row, and the pipeline child signed no
write of its own.

The second half is the one that needed building. A store read cannot answer it
— the parent overwrites producedByTool on the row it dedups, so the BUG-057
check that basic_tokenize's row says "basic_tokenize" was already true before
that fix. The child's signature, written at the line where the store is
modified, is what makes the absence of a write observable from outside.

The direct path is checked too, because it is the reason the child keeps its
writer: the same verb run without the flag lands a pipeline_cli: row and signs
it, and run with the flag does not even create the store.

Everything the gate excuses is listed with a reason, because that list is the
survey's other half: the store's own bookkeeping, project_init's steering
files, the rebuild check and its .sym, the declared LUT intermediate, and the
one named gap this round did not touch.

Fixtures are synthetic throughout — PRGs, a CRT, cartridge banks shaped the way
parseLutGroups reads them. No ROMs, no media, no assembler, no daemon. Proved
red against the unfixed source: 18 failures across the eighteen checks the
change is responsible for.

events.title: fix: one writer on the knowledge store, and the two callers say which they are
events.message:
fix: one writer on the knowledge store, and the two callers say which they are

knowledge/artifacts.json was written by two processes: the MCP server through
saveArtifact, and the pipeline child through registerCliArtifact. That is why
the store needed a cross-process lock at all, and why a legacy entity writer
could sit on the far side of that boundary for months before anyone noticed.
With every MCP door registering its own outputs, the child's registration on
that path is a second writer with nothing left to write.

So the MCP spawn path passes --no-register. src/run-cli.ts names the flag once
as SUPPRESS_CHILD_REGISTRATION and builds every child argv through
pipelineArgvFromMcp, so a new call site cannot pick up a second writer by
someone forgetting the flag. The flag goes in front of the verb's own
arguments, where no positional slot can eat it.

The child keeps its registration for the caller that has no parent. A shell
loop over dist/pipeline/cli.cjs registers what it writes, as it always did;
taking that away would make those runs invisible to list_artifacts, to the
views and to the next session that onboards. The child states which of the two
callers it is serving by name — cli-default or suppressed-by-caller — rather
than carrying a bare boolean, and its usage text says so.

And it signs the write it makes. Whether the child wrote cannot be asked of the
store: the parent's saveArtifact dedups a row by path and overwrites
producedByTool with its own name, so a row the child wrote first and the parent
re-saved looks exactly like one the parent alone wrote. registerCliArtifact
therefore appends one line to the file named by
C64RE_PIPELINE_REGISTRATION_LOG, at the one place the store is modified.
Nothing sets that variable but a gate.

events.title: fix: the parent registers what only the child knew about
events.message:
fix: the parent registers what only the child knew about

Four outputs on the MCP path were named by nobody the parent could speak for.

propose_annotations wrote its draft and left the registering to the pipeline
child, so the draft landed in knowledge/artifacts.json from the far side of a
process boundary and the door had nothing to say when that failed. It now
registers the draft itself, names the knowledge run, and leads with the
NOT-REGISTERED banner instead of trailing a success.

reconstruct_lut, export_menu and disasm_menu registered nothing at all — not
at the door and not in the child, which never called registerCliArtifact for
them. They wrote manifests, payload binaries and listings into the project and
the project did not know: absent from list_artifacts, from every view and from
the next session's onboarding until somebody happened to run
project_inventory_sync. Each now registers the manifest it wrote and the files
that manifest names, through one helper that reports how many rows it made.

full_lut_payloads/ stays unregistered on purpose. It holds every LUT group
dumped whole, including the ones reconstruct_lut then skips, so the skip can be
re-decided later; a row for it would claim the project believes in a file it
only kept.

reconstruct_lut and export_menu were one-line stubs, so they got descriptions
that say when to reach for them and what to use instead.

events.title: aga: a palette write rides with the next present — the outgoing big picture no longer wears the incoming colours
events.message:
aga: a palette write rides with the next present — the outgoing big picture no longer wears the incoming colours

A1200 on v0.9.28: "almost 100% there", except a big picture "takes a second
or so to unload, like it leaves some pixels behind" before the next one or
the 3D view. Filmed at 25 fps in amiberry (-DFRUA_AUTOPLAY into a generated
design whose entry event is a bigpic, x11grab across the dismissing Return):
four frames before the screen settles — 1.4 s of the OUTGOING picture in the
DUNGEON's palette (black with magenta/orange speckle), the walk screen, then
1.6 s with the 3D view blacked out, then the final frame.

On a hardware-palette backend a CLUT write recolours the screen at once; the
pixels that want those colours arrive at the next present, a second or more
later here. #20 (sky/floor flash) was one instance fixed for one caller;
this is the rule. The #8 event-tail hold does not help — it holds pixels,
the palette still landed, and it is armed only for walk steps anyway.

dsp_backend_t.palette_with_present (last field; AGA sets it, video.cfg
agapalsync=off opts out for a hardware A/B): qd_set_palette keeps the
logical palette current and remembers a pending window, forwarded right
after the backend present, after a rect present, on a clean present, from
the engine's event pump when no hold is outstanding, and from jt1067 after
a colour-cycle commit. The title blackout supersedes anything pending, and
qd_set_palette_deferred routes straight through on such a backend. Not the
Nova (its ~0.5 s present is a different trade, untestable off the card);
TT is eligible and left alone.

After: picture in its own colours -> walk -> final. Both the recoloured
picture and the black view hole are gone; the picture's own cycling runs
throughout. The first version FROZE the SSI title's star animation — its
wait loop cycles the palette without presenting or pumping events — and the
title capture caught it (one colour-count signature where the release shows
five); hence the flush in jt1067. Title roll signature-identical to v0.9.28

events.title: merge: a subject is one thing, and a project is re-keyed to it
events.message:
merge: a subject is one thing, and a project is re-keyed to it

A subject was the characters in a filename, so three disks' listings of the
same name were one thing with three tying versions. It is the lineage now: a
declared derivedFrom wherever the file sits, otherwise the directory plus the
stem. A bare filename stops being an identity — get_current_artifact names the
subjects that carry it instead of picking one.

An existing store is re-keyed once on first read, splitting a group whose
members turn out to be several subjects while the partition holding the
current keeps the id, the createdAt and the manual pin.

.tas joins the version model, and the tie it creates with the .asm it was
converted from is named rather than decided by whichever is newer. And
basic_tokenize registers the PRG it writes from the parent, like every other
door.

events.title: fix: a subject is one thing, and an existing project is re-keyed to it
events.message:
fix: a subject is one thing, and an existing project is re-keyed to it

A subject used to be the characters in a filename. `subjectIdForArtifact`
took the basename, stripped the trailing `_disasm` / `_semantic` qualifier
and threw the directory away, so on a three-sided disk project the three
`pl0_disasm.asm` under `analysis/disk/CRAZY1/`, `CRAZY2/` and `CRAZY3/`
were ONE subject holding three tying versions: three unrelated listings of
three different payloads, competing for the title of "the current one".
That collapse is what filed 220 open questions in a single inventory sync.
The tie rules added afterwards stopped the questions without making the
subject right, so `get_current_artifact("pl0")` could still hand back
another disk's code and `register_payload` stem-matched a payload to three
disks' listings the same way.

Identity is the lineage a file belongs to. A file registered with
`derivedFrom` takes its ancestor's subject wherever on disk it now sits —
`save_artifact` is the only door that sets the field, so that is always
somebody saying so, never a guess. Every other file's subject is the
located stem: the directory it lives in plus the stem with its qualifier
stripped. Two sources in one directory are versions of one thing; two in
different directories are two things that share a name. A bare filename is
no longer an identity: a version door asked for one that names several
subjects answers with the list, and the caller picks. `register_payload`
matches on the subject and falls back to a bare-name match only while that
match is unambiguous.

The same change teaches the model the suffix the renderer has written since
2026-09-06. `isVersionedSourceArtifact` matched `.asm/.tass/.sym`, so every
modern 64tass listing joined no version group at all — invisible to
`list_artifact_versions`, never a candidate for current, never counted when
a subject was checked for ties. Widening the list alone would have moved
every project's current listing onto the converted copy the moment the two
generated renderings started tying, so the tie is named instead: the
renderer writes `_disasm.asm` and converts it to `_disasm.tas` beside it,
the KickAssembler file is the one the conversion came from, and it wins
with the rule stated in the answer. A hand-authored `.tas` still outranks
both, which is the case the version model exists for.

And the part that makes both safe to ship. The version groups are persisted
and keyed by subject id, so changing what a subject id IS changes the key of
every row a project already holds. The store records the identity generation
it was written under, and a store without the marker is rewritten once, on
the first read, before anything else sees it: each group is re-keyed; a
group whose members now belong to several subjects splits, with the
partition holding the group's current keeping the group's id, its createdAt
and its manual pin and the others getting their own best member as an auto
current; every stale and missing mark survives; a member whose artifact row
is gone is kept rather than dropped; and the `.tas` listings the old suffix
list could not see are folded in as available members, never as the current.
Nothing consults the filesystem and nothing is deleted.

`e2e:inventory-truth` carried the defect as an assertion — eight subjects
for 24 listings, every one of them tying — and now asserts the 24 and the
absence of any tie at all. `e2e:artifact-best-version` uses located subject
ids and gains a check that a bare filename still resolves while only one
subject carries it.

events.title: grm-bfb: retire the stale base-space reference once an overlay reference replaces it
events.message:
grm-bfb: retire the stale base-space reference once an overlay reference replaces it

Owner's ruling (2026-09-20): at a site where the bank analyzer has resolved a
base-space reference to a non-home occupant and placed the overlay reference,
the stock base-space reference is DELETED, not left as a secondary. On smb3
the leftover pointed into instruction interiors (base:94cd, base:cb61) and
manufactured false bank-switch evidence; the decompiler already followed the
primary call ref, so what this fixes is the call graph, references-to and the
dump samples.

BankAnnotationAdapter.retargetReferences now takes every live state at the site
(fork arms, grm-wul) and decides retirement once, per operand target, after all
arms. The base reference survives when ANY of these hold:
  - some arm, or one side of a read-modify-write, resolves to the home occupant
  - the selecting field is not fully known (a guess may add, never delete);
    a user placement override counts as known
  - the instruction is in base space and the target is in its OWN window --
    that reference is the block's own flow graph, which calledHelper,
    isControlFlowJoin and the fork predecessor walk all read through the
    reference manager (nesmmc1test c06c unrecognized its helper without this)
  - no overlay space exists for the target, or the reference is USER_DEFINED
Retargeting seeds from every reference at the site, overlay ones folded to
their physical offset, so a later round with a different bank still resolves a
site whose base ref an earlier round retired (nesskiptest, FixSkipInstructions);
an overlay instruction's refs into its own overlay (Ghidra's switch tables) are
not seeds, which the A/B on rcproam caught as primary churn. The analyzer
summary log reports the retired count.

Tests: BaseReferenceRetirementProgramTest (10 JUnit cases incl. USER_DEFINED,
partial knowledge, intra-window, round-two); new nesforkhometest fixture (fork
with one arm at home -> base ref survives, H1-H7); criteria banktest C9a-c,
banktest4 D4, nesbanktest N6, nesforktest F9. docs/SCHEMA.md records the rule.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK; realrom-test.sh check nes pass=27
fail=7 -- megaman/wizwarr (12.1.3), dodge/ff1/rcproam/dragonpower bistable per
realrom-current-fails and A/B'd against HEAD, and megaman2 blessed: seven
`via RESET` comments gain known bits with the same conclusion, the effect
grm-fj4m predicted once the wrong bank's base-space callee stops being seen.
smb3 is byte-identical.

events.title: fix(cli): the sandbox write map has no floor — v0.8.3
events.message:
fix(cli): the sandbox write map has no floor — v0.8.3

It started at $0200, so the zero page and the stack were invisible. An
autonomous session watched a run execute INC $011C and STY $2D and was told it
had stored nothing; the only way to the truth was a second process diffing two
images, which cannot see a store that writes a byte's existing value back. Zero
page is where 6502 code keeps its working state, so the one region a depacker
uses most was the one region the map refused to report.

The floor is gone entirely. If a routine trashes its own stack or its zero page
that is a finding, not noise — a write map that stays silent is worse than one
with known machinery in it.

What is still excluded is not an address range but a moment. On the stub path
the harness itself executes `sta $01` and a `jsr` whose push lands on the stack,
so the observer arms when the PC first reaches `entry`: everything before that
is setup, everything after is the routine, including its own pushes. On the
direct-entry path the sentinel is staged into RAM and never performed at all.

Three tests pin it: a zero-page and a stack store are recorded, a read is not,
and nothing the stub does appears while the routine's own deeper push does.

events.title: fix: a document about a whole medium is a deliverable the contract can check
events.message:
fix: a document about a whole medium is a deliverable the contract can check

`deliver.documents` resolved two vocabularies: an address range, and a role
looked up in the model. A demand naming a medium — `covers: artifact:CRAZY1.D64`
— fell into the role branch, matched no boundary and answered "no model boundary
is named for it yet (model_assert)". That is advice nobody can follow: a whole
D64 has no address range to assert, and the document that covers it correctly
declares `covers: artifact:CRAZY1.D64`. The literal artifact id did the same.

The run that hit this restated its own deliverable as `$0200-$FFFE` to make the
check pass. A false declaration, produced by the checker — which is the thing
Spec 847 exists to stop.

The crosswalk from a demand's vocabulary to what satisfies it now lives in
contract/documents.ts, and it knows three: a range, a role via the model, and an
artifact — by `artifact:` prefix, by registered id, by title or by path. Names
are compared on normal forms, never by substring, because a substring rule on
one-letter disk-file names matches everything. A document declaring the artifact
and no address range satisfies the demand, which is what a medium-level
cartography looks like.

A demand nothing answers to is still refused, and now names both doors —
model_assert for a boundary, list_artifacts for a medium — and shows how to say
which one was meant.

events.title: fix: a terminator at row 0 says so, and the schema says what `at` means
events.message:
fix: a terminator at row 0 says so, and the schema says what `at` means

A .d64 descriptor with role track/sector and `terminator: 0` answered
"PROBE — first 0 row(s), resolved." and then "(no rows resolved)".
resolve_lut_rows repeated the same emptiness. Both sentences read as "the table
is empty". What actually happened: `at` pointed two bytes early, at the CBM
file's own load-address word, so row 0's first byte WAS the terminator and the
walk stopped before it started. The loop broke out without a word.

Row 0 is the one case a caller cannot diagnose from the outside, so the result
carries the hit now — the row, the column, the byte and the address it was read
from — and the rendering spells it out: what `at` is counted from on each
medium, and the two classic off-by-N (the load-address word, and an offset
counted from the start of a sector rather than through the image). A terminator
reached later stays a one-liner; it is ordinary.

The second half is why the address was wrong in the first place. `at`, `at_lo`
and `at_hi` carried no .describe() whatsoever, so what an address MEANS for a
disk — a raw byte offset into the image file, counted from $0000 — existed only
as a comment on flatReader. It is in the schema now, next to the cartridge case
(the address inside the bank window), where the person writing the descriptor
reads it.

Only an absolute path worked.

link_cart_chunk_to_asm, ten lines further down the same file, already had the
shape that works: an optional project_dir that takes precedence, the file path
only as fallback. Every path-taking door in this file now goes through one
helper with that rule, and the file path is used as a hint only when it can
anchor something — absolute, or existing from the cwd. Otherwise the resolver
gets nothing, which is what lets its own fallback answer.

When it does fail, the refusal names the path it declined to guess from and the
parameter that settles it, rather than reporting a directory the caller never

events.title: fix: a store to zero page or the stack is output, and is reported as one
events.message:
fix: a store to zero page or the stack is output, and is reported as one

The real core's write-map begins at $0200 — below that is "the CPU port and the
stack page, machinery, not the routine's output". Right for a depack harvest,
wrong for everything else: 6502 code keeps its state in zero page. A depacker's
source and destination pointers, its end pointer, its run length all live there.

A run that demonstrably executed `STY $2D` and `INC $011C` was answered with
"Written runs: 0 — this run stored nothing above $01FF", and a window over
$011B-$0122 printed as eight holes. The byte the caller needed was reachable
only through `include_observed`, whose label read "residue / loaded input, NOT
this run's output" — the exact opposite of the truth for those two pages. The
session read its depacker's end pointer through a channel that told it the
number was not real.

$0000-$01FF is now accounted for on this side. The same run is set up a second
time with an instruction cap of zero, its two low pages are harvested, and the
difference against the final image is what the run changed there. Those runs
join the one write-map every consumer already reads, so a memory window over the
stack page shows the byte and holes only what really was not touched.

The method's limit is stated rather than hidden: a store of a byte that was
already at that address leaves nothing to compare. Low-memory coverage is
therefore a subset of the truth and never a superset — what it reports, the run
really did change. It costs one extra trx64cli start per sandbox_6502_run, and
that is the price of not writing a second copy of the machine's power-on state
over here.

`include_observed` says what the raw window actually holds — residue, loaded
input and this run's own stores together — instead of claiming the run's output
is not in it.

events.title: fix: disk_sector_allocation gives back the map, and stops counting ghosts
events.message:
fix: disk_sector_allocation gives back the map, and stops counting ghosts

The tool promised a per-track/sector ownership map and printed three numbers —
total, unclaimed, overlaps — followed by a JSON block holding the same three.
Nothing else, nowhere else. A session that wanted the cartography the
description advertises rebuilt it by hand out of manifest.spec784.json.

It now prints the map: one character per sector, one line per track, with a
legend, the overlapping cells named, and the full per-sector ownership written
to a JSON file whose path the answer states. `show_owners` adds the T/S cells
each owner holds; `map_path` says where to write.

Two things the map had to get right first.

A zero-block DEL entry claims nothing. A CBM directory carries scratched and
comment entries — type DEL, 0 blocks, and a start (track, sector) left over
from whatever wrote there last, frequently track 18, which is the directory
itself. Walking such an entry's chain claims the directory it is stored in. On
CRAZY side 1 that was seven entries against seven directory sectors: 49
overlaps, not one of them real, with any true overlap buried among them. Those
entries are now listed as non-claimants, each with the reason, and a DEL entry
that does own blocks still claims and still collides.

And the image argument was echoed back, never read, while the tool's own type
promised an `orphan_data` role it could not possibly assign. It reads the image
now, so an unclaimed sector that holds bytes is told apart from an empty one —
which is the whole point of asking who owns what.

events.title: fix: a rank tie is only a question when a person's answer could differ
events.message:
fix: a rank tie is only a question when a person's answer could differ

One project_inventory_sync reported "220 subject(s) have two equally-ranked
sources — choose one with set_current_artifact_version(artifact_id=…) (an open
question was raised for each…)". The project went from four real open questions
to 224, and the offered remedy was 220 calls. Nobody makes 220 decisions; the
four that were about the game were buried.

What a tie is, decided here: a rank tie is a DECISION only when a person's
answer could differ from the machine's. Two rules settle the rest, and the sync
says which rule it used and which file it picked.

  Same bytes. Candidates whose content hash agrees are one listing registered
  from two paths. Take the shortest relative path, then lexicographic, so the
  answer is the same on every run and every machine.

  Machine output. When every tied candidate is generated — a disassembler dump,
  a companion file — the tie is between two deterministic renderings of one run.
  Doctrine already holds that machine output is not human debt (Spec 832 D5, the
  rule that split the registration scan); a deterministic dump is not a decision
  either. Take the established order: rank, newest, id.

What survives is the case the version model was built for: a hand-authored
source competing with another hand-authored source, where guessing would
overwrite somebody's work. That is asked. The 220 were all generated listings of
same-named payloads on three disks, so none of them is asked any more.

And the questions are capped and closed. Past five genuine ties one run files a
single question about the class, naming the count and a sample, because "220
subjects tie" is one fact and not 220. Nothing in the repo had ever closed a
version-decision question — not even set_current_artifact_version, the call the
question tells you to make — so every one ever raised stayed open for the life
of the project. Answering one closes it; a subject that stops tying is closed on
the next sync; the class question closes when no tie is left.

events.title: fix: two files that hold the same bytes are two files
events.message:
fix: two files that hold the same bytes are two files

Four successive project_inventory_sync runs each named a different set of 7-14
files that "no inventory pattern covers", including files the project's own
declared pattern plainly matched, and each run reported registering ~83 more.
Nothing in the repo caps registration per call. This did.

saveArtifact's third dedup matcher means "the file moved between paths", and it
fired on the content hash alone. A project with the same title screen on two
disks registered CRAZY1's copy, then CRAZY2's; the second save found the first
by hash and moved that row onto the second path. CRAZY1's path was now absent
from artifacts.json, so the next scan called it unregistered, registered it, and
evicted CRAZY2. They ping-ponged for the life of the project, and the
"registered: N" line only ever counted the rows stolen since the last run.

A hash match now identifies the same file only when the matched row's own file
is gone from disk — which is what "moved" means. Two files that both exist are
two rows. This is also the hazard BUG-054 №6 worked around from the other end,
by refusing to register a byte-identical rebuild-check at all.

`check:address-rule` is the structural half: one body compiled twice, the two
halves run over a corpus and required to answer identically, and a scan that
fails by file and line on a third copy. It is what stops the rule being
re-stated a third time, and it runs in CI.

`e2e:disasm-family` is the behavioural half, over MCP stdio against a temp
project: a string offset read as hex by both halves and a number taken as
given, a 20-byte window that does not inherit the 2 KB file's analysis, a
refusal that names both spans, `no_analysis`, an analysis named outright
winning over the sidecar with no entry points passed, a drive block's
annotations arriving in the graph and answering `graph_find`, a synthetic
graph of 500 owners that yields a count rather than 500 names, and a branch
that wraps the address space answered with the remedy. Synthetic bytes, a
synthetic graph.sqlite, no ROMs, no media, no daemon; the four rebuild checks
skip loudly without KickAssembler, the way e2e:830 does.

events.message:
fix: a declaration that is wrong says so, in its own words

knowledge/inventory-patterns.json was read with four typeof checks and nothing
else. An entry that failed one of them was dropped silently, so a project that
wrote kind: "annotations" got a file that looked accepted and changed nothing —
and the only vocabulary it was ever shown came from a different door entirely,
register_existing_files' Zod enum, dumped whole.

The reader validates now and names what it found: the entry index, the value
given, the near miss where there is one ("annotations" is a report), the allowed
kinds and scopes, a missing glob, a mistyped top-level key. A bad entry is still
dropped — it cannot be applied — but never without a line about it.

howToDeclare answered "report" for anything ending in .json or .md and "prg" for
everything else, derived from whichever example sorted first, so a directory of
.sym or .bin files was handed a declaration naming the wrong kind. It groups the
leftovers by extension now and offers one paste-able entry per type, with a glob
derived from where those files actually sit and the kind and scope that fit them.

The kind and scope vocabularies move into this leaf module so the declaration
reader and register_existing_files share one list. Both doors, one answer.

events.title: fix: one address rule, an analysis that cannot be inherited, names that reach the graph
events.message:
fix: one address rule, an analysis that cannot be inherited, names that reach the graph

Five defects an autonomous run wrote down against the disassembly doors. They
are one commit because they live in three files that hold each other up.

**The address rule is one function now, and it is imported.** It had been
written down twice — once in `pipeline/src/cli.ts`, once in
`analysis-workflow.ts` — and it drifted twice. First inside a single call, where
`entry_points` read `"E800"` as hex while the relocation loader ran
`parseInt(s, 10)` on it. That was fixed by stating the rule, in two files. Then
`disasm_raw` was written against the statement rather than against the function,
and the pipeline kept four more inline `parseInt(x, 16)` sites of its own, one of
which never stripped a `$`. The rule now lives in `src/shared/address-rule.ts`
and nowhere else; ESM and CommonJS cannot import each other, so the pipeline
half compiles the same body as `pipeline/src/lib/address-rule.ts`, generated
from it. `scripts/check-address-rule.mjs` regenerates the twin, runs a corpus
through both COMPILED halves and requires identical answers and identical
refusals, and fails by file and line on a third copy — a re-statement of the
rule in a string, or an inline parse of an address or a count in any door of
this family.

**An analysis is never inherited by a window, and never swapped for another
file.** `maybeLoadAnalysis` fell through to the stem-matched sidecar in two
cases that both had to be silent to happen at all. A raw window picked up the
`<stem>_analysis.json` beside the whole image: pointed at 640 bytes of a 63 KB
file it rendered 929 instructions and 4082 data lines and then reported the
rebuild as diverging at body offset 0. And an analysis named outright lost to
the sidecar whenever the tool could not find it — which `disasm_prg` arranged
by pushing it onto the positional tail behind the entry-point list, a slot that
is only filled when there ARE entry points, so a call with an analysis and no
entry points put the path where a list of addresses was expected. It is a named
`--analysis` flag now, a path that does not exist is a refusal, a raw window
inherits nothing, an analysis whose span is not this window's is refused with
both spans named, and `no_analysis` refuses one outright. The listing header
says which analysis drove it, by name.

**disasm_raw imports the names it applied.** It printed `[annotations] applied
4, skipped 0` and stopped there, while `disasm_prg` imported into the graph —
and disasm_raw is the only door for a block with no PRG header, so drive code
ended up with no human names in the graph at all and `project_critique`
reported a stage holding routines and tables and not one name. The workaround
reached for was carving synthetic PRGs, which is the thing this door exists to
end. The renderer now reports which annotations file and which analysis it
actually read, and the wrapper imports THAT path rather than re-deriving a
candidate order of its own — two halves guessing the same order is how a
listing full of names came to sit beside an import handed a path that does not
exist.

**A rebuild that fails says what to do.** `relative address is illegal (jump
distance is too far: 65471)` is what a linear decode of a compressed stream
produces and nothing else does. The verdict now names that, and names the two
ways on: declare the range as data through an annotations file, or depack first
and disassemble the result.

When the graph holds no rows for the owner an analysis is about, the reason
carried every owner that IS seeded. On a project with ~500 of them that is
some fifteen thousand characters, and it went into `codeSeedReport.reason`,
which is printed into every analyze_prg answer, every disasm_prg answer and
every rendered listing header — on each of 292 payloads. An autonomous run
reported it as by far the largest single context cost of the job, and not one
of the names told it anything.

What is actionable is the count, and the owners whose names are closest to the
one that was asked for: the usual cause of an empty lookup is a near miss.
That is what the reason says now. `C64RE_GRAPH_SEED_OWNERS=full` prints the
whole list for the caller who wants it.

Both writers of knowledge/artifacts.json staged through the same fixed .tmp
name, so two overlapping registrations destroyed each other's staging file —
and behind that, a registration is a read-modify-write, so a unique name alone
would have turned the crash into a silently lost row. A cross-process lock now
wraps the whole read-modify-write, and a registration that fails says so in a
banner on the first line instead of a footnote under a success.

The extract chain read an exception as the only kind of failure, so a payload
whose load address plus length passes $FFFF — refused by the analyser, which
returns rather than throws — was counted among the done.

events.message:
control: symbols, breakpoint-by-label, memory read and disassembly

New remote verbs, all structured: symbols [filter] (the build's symbol
table as JSON, with addresses once the program map has live bases),
readmem <addr> <len> and disasm [addr] (JSON rows from the debugger's
own dumps, via a blocking-debug-command helper extracted from cmd), and
a label form of breakpoint — it resolves the symbol to its definition's
file:line, toggles there, and replies where it landed (with the address
when the map can say). The MCP shim exposes them as pist_symbols,
pist_readmem, pist_disasm and a label argument on pist_breakpoint, and
serves all three JSON verbs as structuredContent.

One bug the tests caught before it shipped: SymbolEntry.file is a full
path but breakpoints key by base name, so a label toggle initially
recorded a breakpoint nothing could arm.

Verified live against a real session: the count symbol listed at
hello.s:21, a breakpoint set by its label, memory read back as hex rows
matching the disassembly of the same address, and the run stopping at
the label's line.

events.title: One screen setting, chosen from the menu, and a cheats option
events.message:
One screen setting, chosen from the menu, and a cheats option

screen=fill|fit|top|full replaces the three booleans that used to
decide how 224 lines meet a 200-line screen. They meant nothing in
combination; this is one setting with four values, and the old
spellings are still read as aliases so an existing RS.CFG keeps the
picture it had. The default moves from the top border to Fill: the
overscan modes flicker on enough hardware - resident cartridge
firmware, a moving mouse, disk activity - that the default should be
the mode that never looks broken, and a border is one keypress away.

The title menu gains a "Screen mode" line above Quit that cycles the
four, and the change happens there and then: the mode setup is pulled
out of init into setScreenMode, which closes whatever was open before
opening anything new and reports the mode actually achieved. A border
that will not open falls back to Fill and the label says so.

Fit is regular now. Two rows cropped at each end, then every eleventh
of the 220 between dropped: the same twenty-four lines as the old
y * 25 / 28 squash, but in runs of ten instead of an 8/8/9 rhythm, so
edges stop wobbling and an 8-pixel line of text can be placed where
none of its rows goes missing. The menu is placed exactly there - row
13, 11-pixel pitch - which also keeps it whole in Fill, and clear of
the logo in all four. Benchmarked against Fill on ST and STE: within
0.6%, inside layout noise.

In Fit, cutscenes present as Fill for their duration: the picture is
a centred half-height frame with blank rows where Fill crops, and
squashing it gained nothing.

cheats=true, or the engine's bits added up (1 one-hit kills, 2 never
hit, 4 life never drops), reaches the cheat mask the desktop build
has always taken from --cheats. Numeric options read true and false
as all and none, so the digits still mean their bits.

RS.CFG.template and the README describe the new option and drop the
old three.

events.title: Keep stale bakes off recycled memory, and never drop a sprite
events.message:
Keep stale bakes off recycled memory, and never drop a sprite

Two faults in the planar sprite cache, both reported from a 4MB STE
and both shaped like memory pressure a few screens into level 1.

SpriteCache::insert freed a slab it was outgrowing and only then
invalidated the bakes keyed into it - against the new address, not
the old one. A bake pointing at the freed slab outlived it, malloc
handed that address to the next sprite that needed one, and the bake
then matched a pointer holding somebody else's pixels: fragments of
an earlier room drawn where a sprite should be. The invalidation now
happens before the free.

ST_drawSpriteCached returned without drawing when the bake could not
be allocated. The game logic ran on, so Conrad kept taking input and
kept being solid while not being on screen - and it happened when
the most was going on, which is when the heap is tightest. It now
falls back to the chunky draw instead.

events.title: test: eight pipeline children write the store at the same moment
events.message:
test: eight pipeline children write the store at the same moment

A serial test cannot see this defect. It never fired serially in 590 calls, so
the gate does not run one: it spawns eight real pipeline children, proves from
their own timestamps that the last one started before the first one exited —
so they were all alive together — and then asserts that all eight registrations
are in the file.

Against the pre-fix writer (checked by patching the built helper back to a
fixed staging name and a pass-through lock) the gate reproduces the field
report exactly: the reported `ENOENT … rename artifacts.json.tmp`, and 6 of 8
rows landing instead of 8. A second wave over a store that already has rows
covers the case the first cannot, where losing a row means losing somebody
else's.

The forced-failure half puts a DIRECTORY where artifacts.json goes — no
permission games, deterministic on every platform — and asserts both writers
say so out loud: the child on stderr with no stack, the MCP door with the
banner as its first line, both naming project_inventory_sync, neither using the
word "skipped".

Hermetic, so it goes in the CI workflow: temp projects, synthetic PRGs, one
small fixture D64. No ROMs, no assembler, no daemon, no network.

events.title: fix: a file that produced nothing is not done
events.message:
fix: a file that produced nothing is not done

`pack1 (nameint1`, `pack15` and `pobj xtro` came off one disk with an empty
payload directory and no listing: their nominal load address plus length runs
past $FFFF, so the analyser refused them. The summary said "34 done, 0 failed,
7 skipped of 41" and all three were among the 34. They were found by auditing
every directory entry against the listings.

The workflow the L2 chain runs reports a broken phase by RETURNING, not by
throwing: analyze-prg exits non-zero, the phase is recorded `blocked`, and the
result comes back intact. The chain read only the exception, so everything that
did not throw was done. It reads the phases now — and, as the belt to that
brace, checks that a listing was actually written, so whatever new way a phase
finds to produce nothing still reaches the caller as a failure.

The reason is the analyser's own sentence, not the first line of its output:
node prints the throw site before the message, so taking line one gave
`analyze: /…/prg.cjs:29`, which says a file exists and nothing else.

And a count is not an account. The summary names every file that produced
nothing, with its reason, and says what the skips were — the seven above were
DEL directory entries and nothing said so.

events.title: fix: a registration that failed is not a footnote on a success
events.message:
fix: a registration that failed is not a footnote on a success

The worst thing the parallel run turned up was not the crash. It was a call
that printed `rebuild verified byte-identical` and then, at the bottom of the
same answer, `Knowledge registration skipped: ENOENT…`. The reader takes the
first line and moves on. The artifact was never registered, and nothing in the
result said the work had not landed.

"Skipped" was the wrong word for it too: skipping is a decision, and this was a
failure. The message now says what did not happen, what that costs — the files
will not appear in list_artifacts, in any view, or to the next session that
onboards — and how to repair it. The result carries `failed`, so a door that
owns its own output can put the banner FIRST instead of after the success; the
three extraction doors do.

The pipeline child stops throwing the raw ENOENT out of main. Its subcommand
wrote the file before asking for it to be registered, so the run did not fail
and must not report that it did; what failed is the bookkeeping, and that goes
to stderr as prose with the way out, not as a node stack.

events.title: fix: the knowledge store can take two writers
events.message:
fix: the knowledge store can take two writers

knowledge/artifacts.json always had two of them — the MCP server registers a
tool's outputs, and the analysis pipeline, a separate CommonJS child process,
registers whatever a CLI subcommand just wrote. Both staged through the same
fixed `<store>.tmp`. Two of them overlapping is enough: A writes the staging
file, B writes it too, A renames it into place, B renames a file that is no
longer there. Six registrations in about 590 calls died that way, only ever at
3- to 6-way parallelism and never once serially.

A unique staging name is the floor, not the fix. A registration is a
read-modify-write: both writers load the store, add their row and write the
whole file back, so unique staging names alone would have turned a loud crash
into a lost row — the last writer wins and the other registration is gone with
nothing anywhere to say so. So the read, the change and the write go inside one
cross-process lock, built on `open(…, "wx")`, with a stale-break so a crashed
writer cannot wedge a project and a timeout so a wait that cannot end is said
out loud instead of hanging.

The lock only works if every writer runs the same protocol, and src/ (ESM) and
pipeline/src/ (CommonJS) cannot import each other. So json-store-lock.ts exists
twice, byte-identical, importing nothing but node builtins so it can stay that
way; the gate compares the two files.

On the server side the lock goes around saveArtifact, not just around the write
underneath it — a write-only lock still loses rows, because the decision about
what to dedup against is made from the read.

While in there: registerCliArtifact canonicalised neither side of its
project-relative path, and process.cwd() returns a canonical path while an
argument does not. Under a symlinked project root every row read
`../../../tmp/<project>/…` and the "already registered?" check never matched.

events.title: feat(wandlung): die zugesagte Nachpruefung gab es nicht — und beim Bauen hat sie zweimal falschen Alarm geschlagen (MF-1307)
events.message:
feat(wandlung): die zugesagte Nachpruefung gab es nicht — und beim Bauen hat sie zweimal falschen Alarm geschlagen (MF-1307)

DER BEFUND: EINE ZUSAGE, DIE IN DER OBERFLAECHE STAND

`verify_after` wurde GESETZT (`uft_copy_plan.c`), KOPIERT
(`ext_opts.verify_after = options->verify_after`) und dem Bediener als
`ja` ANGEZEIGT (`uft_save_image.cpp:276`) — und an keiner Stelle im Baum
ABGEFRAGT. Regel **E-7** in Reinform, und zugleich die Klasse aus MF-883
(`schreibzusage_ohne_tat`): das Werkzeug sagte eine Nachpruefung zu, die
es nicht gab. Das Feld steht per Vorgabe auf `true`, die Zusage traf also
JEDE Wandlung.

Seit dieser Fassung wird die geschriebene Datei erneut geoeffnet und Spur
fuer Spur gegen die Quelle gehalten. Der Vergleich selbst ist NICHT neu
geschrieben, sondern `uft_generic_verify_track()` — zwei Fassungen waeren
die Bauform aus MF-1177.

ZWEI FALSCHE ALARME, BEIDE BEIM BAUEN GEFANGEN

Ein falscher Alarm ist in diesem Baum so teuer wie ein stiller Verlust:
er schickt jemanden zur falschen Stelle. Die erste Fassung hat zwei
erzeugt, und beide sind gemessen statt vermutet:

1. **Die Geometrie urteilte.** `IMD -> IMG` schreibt aus
   `hxcfe_pc160.imd` eine Datei mit **0 von 163 840 abweichenden Byte**
   (MF-1277). Die Quelle sagt **42** Zylinder an und traegt auf **40**
   Sektoren (320 = 40 x 8); das Ziel sagt 40. Die Pruefung brach auf die
   ANGESAGTEN Zahlen hin ab: `VERIFY_FAILED` bei **0 geprueften Spuren**,
   an einer fehlerfreien Datei. Zwei Leser, die dieselbe Groesse
   verschieden zaehlen — die Bauform aus MF-1177.
   Seither entscheiden die DATEN: gelaufen wird ueber die Spuren der
   QUELLE, und eine Quellspur ohne Sektoren zaehlt als `spuren_leer`
   statt als Abweichung (Regel D6). Eine echte Kuerzung faellt weiterhin
   auf — am Inhalt statt an einer Zahl. Der Quell-Befund steht als
   **P3-533**.

2. **„Nichts vergleichbar" galt als Verlust.** Eine SCP-Quelle ist FLUSS;
   ihr `read_track` liefert keine Sektoren. Vier gruene Tests fielen
   deshalb (`test_convert_cell_adjust`, `_flippy_reverse`,
   `_output_verify`, `_scp_adf_multirev`) — jede Fluss-nach-Sektor-
   Wandlung haette als Verlust gegolten, obwohl gar nichts gemessen
   wurde. Seither ist „nicht beurteilbar" vom Befund UNTERSCHIEDEN: der
   Verteiler sagt es dem Bediener und nimmt den Erfolg NICHT zurueck.
   Konnte die Quelle dagegen nicht gelesen werden, ist es sehr wohl ein
   Befund.

**Und das Ziel wird mit dem Plugin geoeffnet, das es GESCHRIEBEN hat.**
Die Sonde ist bei einem kopflosen Abbild eine Rate-Aufgabe: dieselbe
richtige IMG kommt ueber die Sonde mit **40 von 40** abweichenden Spuren
heraus und mit genanntem Plugin mit **0**. Beide Zahlen stehen als Zusage
im Test — die Sondenzeile ist die Anti-Tautologie zur anderen.

DIE ZWEI MATRIXEINTRAEGE, UND WO DIE ANWEISUNG NICHT TRUG

    TD0 -> IMD   LOSSY_DOCUMENTED   Maske VAR_SECTOR_SZ
    TD0 -> IMG   LOSSY_DOCUMENTED   Maske alle fuenf Merkmale

Die Anweisung sagte fuer den ersten „Verlust: —". Die Messung sagt etwas
anderes, und die Messung gewinnt: `uft_td0_to_imd()` nimmt
`t.sectors[0].data_len` und ebnet die ganze Spur darauf ein (P3-524).
Gerechnet ist die Differenz zwar null (`F_TD0 == F_IMD`), aber der
WANDLER verliert — und `uft_roundtrip.h` erlaubt ausdruecklich, mehr zu
erklaeren. Hier ist es kein Pessimismus, sondern eine Tatsache ueber den
Wandler.

Fuer den zweiten nannte die Anweisung VIER Merkmale. Gerechnet sind es
**FUENF**: `NO_DATA_SEC` fehlte in der Liste und steht in beiden Tafeln.
Das Tor `G8` rechnet die Differenz aus `uft_format_traegt.c` nach, statt
sie aus dem Kopf zu nehmen.

P3-524 IST DAMIT AM OBJEKT BELEGT, NICHT MEHR NUR ABGELESEN

Der Eintrag sagte woertlich, ein Fixture gebe es nicht: alle 1440
Sektoren von `libdsk_uftk_pc720.td0` tragen 512 Byte. Gruppe 4 des neuen
Tests baut den Fall — eine unverpackte TD0, eine Spur, drei Sektoren mit
**512 / 256 / 512** Byte — und misst:

    ohne verify_after   success = 1   (der stille Verlust)
    mit  verify_after   success = 0   "1 von 1 geprueften Spuren weichen
                                       ab (3 Sektoren verglichen)"

GEAENDERT   src/formats/uft_format_convert_dispatch.c (die Nachpruefung
              und ihre Verdrahtung), src/core/uft_roundtrip.c (zwei
              Eintraege), src/formats/uft_format_convert_tables.c
              (TD0->IMD von UNVERIFIED auf LOSSY),
              include/uft/uft_format_convert.h (Bilanz + Deklaration),
              include/uft/uft_format_plugin.h (sie standen dort falsch),
              src/core/uft_format_verify.c (Funktion herausgeloest),
              tests/test_verify_after_ist_verdrahtet.c (NEU, 5 Gruppen),
              tests/test_convert_imd_img_belegt.c,
              tests/test_matrix_form.c,
              tests/test_wandlungstafel_luegt_nicht.c,
              tests/CMakeLists.txt, docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md (P3-524
              nachgetragen, P3-533/P3-534 neu), CLAUDE.md,
              docs/MASTER_PLAN.md, docs/SUBSYSTEM_MATURITY.md,
              docs/STAND.md (abgeleitete Zahlen)

            **Der Ort der Funktion ist eine Messung, kein Geschmack:**
            sie lag zuerst in `uft_format_verify.c`, und die wird von
            **47** Testzielen gebunden, die nur den Spurvergleich
            brauchen. Jedes davon zog ueber sie die ganze
            Disk-Oeffnungs-Maschinerie nach — elf Ziele endeten mit
            `undefined reference to uft_meta_free`. Eine Funktion gehoert
            in die Schicht, die sie braucht.

BELEGT      ctest **529 von 531**, ein benannter Skip (`test_freezer`).
            Die zwei roten (`test_format_tab_bindung`,
            `test_format_tab_capability_gating`) gehoeren dem Nebenlauf:
            sie haengen an `src/formattab.cpp`, `forms/tab_format.ui` und
            `src/uft_flow_layout.cpp` — alle drei unveraendert von
            fremder Hand und NICHT in diesem Commit.
            `update_inventory.py` 0 Driftmeldungen;
            `gen_stand.py --pruefen` „ist aktuell".
            Tor `G8` erfuellt, 12 Zusagen.

            **Kennzahl (MF-640): angebotene Wandlungspfade 16 -> 18**,
            Matrix-Eintraege 18 -> 20, Paare mit Einverstaendnis 9 -> 11.
            Alle drei abgeleitet, keine von Hand gesetzt.

ROT-PROBE   Regel **D2** — ein Aufrufer und ein Test, der rot wird, wenn
            der Aufruf verschwindet. Gruppe 4 oben ist er: dieselbe
            Datei, dieselben Optionen, EIN Wahrheitswert Unterschied,
            zwei verschiedene Ergebnisse.
            Anti-Tautologien, alle gemessen: (a) eine saubere Wandlung
            muss MIT Nachpruefung durchgehen — 160 von 160 Spuren, 0
            abweichend, sonst pruefte Gruppe 4 nur, dass `verify_after`
            alles ablehnt; (b) die Sonde muss dieselbe Datei beanstanden,
            die mit genanntem Plugin durchgeht (40 gegen 0); (c) Gruppe 1
            (Quelle gegen sich selbst) belegt AUSDRUECKLICH nichts ueber
            die Urteilskraft — dafuer sind Gruppe 2 und 3 da, an zwei
            verschiedenen Zweigen.

            **Das Tor G8 war zuerst gruen aus dem falschen Grund**, und
            das steht in seinem Kopf: der Kommentar-Entferner ersetzte
            einen Blockkommentar durch EIN Leerzeichen, verschmolz damit
            Zeilen, und das Fortsetzungsmuster fuer `#define F_TD0` lief
            **2234 Zeichen** bis ans Dateiende. `F_TD0` kam mit EINEM
            Merkmal heraus statt mit fuenf, die gerechnete Differenz war
            zu klein, und „die Maske deckt sie" traf trivial zu. Ein Tor,
            das aus dem falschen Grund zustimmt, ist schlimmer als keines.

GESTOPPT    **P3-533** — `hxcfe_pc160.imd` sagt 42 Zylinder an und traegt
            auf 40 Sektoren. Behoben ist die FOLGE (die Pruefung urteilt
            nicht mehr ueber angesagte Zahlen), die URSACHE nicht: ob die
            Datei 42 Spursaetze traegt oder `uft_imd.c` hochrechnet, ist
            NICHT gemessen und steht so da.
            **P3-534** — die Gegenprobe von `test_matrix_form` Gruppe 3
            ist WEGGEFALLEN. Sie benutzte `TD0 -> IMG`, ausdruecklich
            weil es „(noch) keinen Eintrag" hatte. Ein Ersatz ist nicht
            herstellbar: die Merkmalstafel fuehrt drei Formate, und beide
            Paare mit nichtleerer Differenz haben jetzt einen Eintrag.
            Die Lehre gehoert unabhaengig festgehalten: **ein Rotbeweis,
            der an einem unerledigten Posten haengt, hat ein
            Verfallsdatum.**
            **P3-524 bleibt im Kern offen** — `has_varsizes`/`ssize[]`
            werden weiterhin nicht bedient, die Ebnung steht. Neu ist nur,
            dass sie am Objekt belegt und nicht mehr durch ein fehlendes
            Fixture blockiert ist.
            **P3-530, dritte Stelle** — die drei `uft_disk_*`-Deklarationen
            stehen weiterhin von Hand da, weil `uft_core.h` und
            `uft_track.h` sich ueber `uft_track_get_sector` widersprechen.
            Sie sind mit der Funktion umgezogen, nicht verschwunden.

RISIKO      **Die Nachpruefung vergleicht DATEN, nicht MERKMALE**, und das
            ist Absicht: ein TD0-Sektor mit `NODAT` wird 0xE5, IMD und IMG
            fuellen mit demselben Byte — byteweise gleich, waehrend das
            Merkmal verlorengeht. Dafuer ist die `lost_features`-Maske da.
            Wer von dieser Pruefung Merkmalstreue erwartet, erwartet das
            Falsche.
            **Die Spielart „zu kurze Maske" ist unbeaufsichtigt** (P3-534).
            **Kein Orakel laeuft in CI** — das Urteil von libdsk und hxcfe
            ueber die drei gepackten TD0 steht als Zahl im Manifest und im
            Testkopf; was CI prueft, ist der Determinismus dazwischen.

events.title: control: document surface, structured results, profiler verbs, discovery
events.message:
control: document surface, structured results, profiler verbs, discovery

New remote-control verbs: read (the current document), statejson (state
as a JSON object), problems (the Problems pane as JSON), and profile
start|stop|results (execution counts as JSON). The MCP shim exposes them
as pist_open, pist_read, pist_problems and the pist_profile_* tools, and
serves pist_state / pist_problems / pist_profile_results in both shapes —
parsed structuredContent and pretty-printed text — so agents consume
fields instead of parsing console text.

A listening IDE now publishes its address to a discovery file under the
user's data directory (removed on exit, only if still its own), and a
pist-mcp started without --port or PIST_CONTROL_PORT reads it — a
locally started IDE needs zero configuration.

Also from review: tst_mcp joins the Windows console-app foreach (a
GUI-subsystem test reports nothing there), the Windows deploy step keeps
set -euo pipefail, the non-code breakpoint note is action-neutral (the
verb toggles), breakpoint errors on an invalid line instead of a silent
ok, the stopped event falls back to publishing without a pc when no
register batch follows a stop, and the release verification asserts
pist-mcp resolves its bundled Qt in the deb and the .app.

Verified live: discovery-file connection, entry stop reported with its
real pc, a line-22 breakpoint hit distinct from the entry address,
structured state, problems, and a profile collected and read back.

events.message:
chore(doku): STAND.md nach der Uebernahme von MF-1295 nachgezogen (MF-1298)

EINE Zeile, und sie ist abgeleitet: MF-1295 bringt P3-528 mit, damit
waechst docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md von 7867 auf 7868 Zeilen, und STAND.md nennt
diese Zahl.

WARUM EIN EIGENER COMMIT

Sie gehoerte in MF-1295 hinein. Der Weg dorthin waere ein
`git commit --amend` gewesen, und das Fact-Forcing-Tor hat ihn zweimal
abgewiesen — zu Recht, denn ein Amend schreibt Geschichte um. Ein
zweiter Commit ist der nicht-zerstoerende Weg zum selben Ergebnis, und
er bekommt eine EIGENE Nummer statt sich unter MF-1295 zu haengen: zwei
ungleiche Aenderungen unter einer Nummer sind genau die Kollision, die
`.unlazy/td0/GATES.md` als H1 fuehrt.

WARUM SIE UEBERHAUPT NOETIG IST

Der pre-push-Haken prueft die Frische am ARBEITSBAUM, CI am COMMIT.
Waere die Zeile nur im Arbeitsbaum nachgezogen, ginge der Push durch und
CI faende eine veraltete STAND.md — die Klasse `lokal gruen ist keine
Aussage ueber CI`.

UND EINE ZAHL, DIE ICH BEINAHE FALSCH BERICHTIGT HAETTE

Im Hauptbaum rechnete derselbe Generator **178** Fliesstext-Attributionen,
die committete Fassung sagte **179**. Der Hauptbaum haelt 456
unversionierte Dateien, und `repo_scope` zaehlt `--others` mit — CI
sieht sie nie. Im sauberen Stand-Arbeitsbaum kommen **179** heraus, die
committete Zahl war also richtig. Eine Messung aus einem verschmutzten
Baum haette hier eine korrekte Datei 'berichtigt'.

events.title: feat(gui): acht weitere Plan-Bindungen — und die Beschriftung geht endlich mit (MF-1295)
events.message:
feat(gui): acht weitere Plan-Bindungen — und die Beschriftung geht endlich mit (MF-1295)

Erster Schritt von Phase 6 des GUI-Umbaus: verdrahten, was sich ohne eine
Zeile Formularaenderung verdrahten laesst. Keine Loeschung, kein Reiter
aufgeloest, Tor 68 unbewegt.

WAS GEMESSEN WURDE

`bindung[]` in `src/formattab.cpp` fuehrte elf Kernparameter. Die Karte des
GUI-Umbaus (`test-gui/gui-geruest/zuordnung`, Eigentuemerentwurf vom
2026-09-20) nennt 56. Von den 45 fehlenden haben neun in DIESEM Formular
bereits ein Bedienelement und stehen in `k_param[]`; acht davon sind
aufgenommen. Nicht aufgenommen sind die acht `plan.*`-Achsen und die zehn
`a8.*`-Felder: sie stehen nicht in `k_param[]`, eine Bindung waere eine
Zusage ohne Gegenstueck (MF-767).

DER AELTERE BEFUND: DIE HAENGENDE BESCHRIFTUNG

Der Plan versteckt seit MF-1234 Felder, die auf einer Ebene nichts
bedeuten. Versteckt wurde aber nur das FELD. Bei DOSCopy verschwindet die
ganze Geometrie, und „Tracks:", „Sides:", „Sectors:", „Size:" blieben ueber
einer leeren Flaeche stehen — eine Beschriftung, die eine Einstellung
behauptet, die es dort nicht gibt.

`beschriftungVon()` findet sie in drei Lagen, alle am Formular gemessen: im
Gitter die Zelle links, im Formularlayout die LabelRole derselben Zeile, im
waagerechten Kasten das vorherige Element. Ist es kein QLabel, passiert
nichts — gemessen steht vor `checkDecodeGCR` das Haekchen `checkNibbleMode`
und vor `checkHashSha512` das Haekchen `checkHashSha256`. Einen Nachbarn
mitzuverstecken waere schlimmer als der Fehler, der behoben wird.

EIN ZWEITER BEFUND, AELTER ALS DIESE AENDERUNG

`gcr.variant` -> `comboGCRType` steht seit MF-1234 in derselben Tafel und
verlangt `UFT_CAP_GCR`. `copyPlanCaps()` setzt diese Flagge NIE — der
Reiter kennt kein geoeffnetes Abbild und sagt das in seinem eigenen
Kommentar. Die Folge hat niemand gemessen: die GCR-Verfahrenswahl ist auf
jeder Ebene versteckt, also unerreichbar. Dasselbe gilt fuer alles, was
`UFT_CAP_FILESYSTEM` oder `UFT_CAP_CBM_BAM` verlangt — zusammen 31 der 63
Parameter mit Faehigkeitsbedingung.

Deshalb ist `gcr.preserve_raw_nibbles` -> `checkDecodeGCR` NICHT gebunden
worden, obwohl die Zuordnung sachlich richtig waere: sie haette ein zweites
Bedienelement dauerhaft unsichtbar gemacht. Der Befund steht als P3-528 mit
drei Wegen und wird nicht hier entschieden (MF-1077).

ABNAHME

Rotbeweis zuerst war nicht moeglich — der Test entstand mit dem Code; dafuer
ist die Mutationsmatrix vollstaendig gelaufen: 10 von 11 gefangen
(scratchpad `mut_bindung.py`). Die elfte ist benannt statt verschwiegen:
„im Gitter gilt der Nachbar als Beschriftung" laesst sich an diesem
Formular nicht isolieren, weil links von jedem gebundenen Gitterfeld
ohnehin ein QLabel steht.

Zwei der Mutationen waren zuerst Fehler in der MUTATION, nicht im Test:
`replace(text, 1)` traf den Formular-Zweig statt des Kasten-Zweigs, weil die
Rueckgabezeile dreimal gleich lautet. Und zwei Zusagen des Tests waren
zuerst rot, weil meine ERWARTUNG falsch war: die Flussfelder brauchen nicht
nur die Flussebene, sondern auch ein Format, das Fluss zusagt.

  tests/test_format_tab_bindung.cpp   8 Zusagen, alle gruen
  ctest gesamt                        525/525, 1 benannter Skip
  check_consistency.py                OK

Der Vorschau-Entwurf in `test-gui/` kennt den Faehigkeits-Term nicht und
zeichnet die Flussfelder deshalb optimistischer als das Programm; das steht
jetzt im Test.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012Pu9HtCSDb388mbto6kGov

UMNUMMERIERT BEIM ZUSAMMENFUEHREN — ZWEIMAL, UND BEIDES GEMESSEN

Dieser Commit lag als `bfd5ebcd` ungepusht auf `main`, waehrend der Baum
zehn Commits weitergelaufen ist. Beim Aufsetzen auf `origin/main` fielen
zwei Nummernkollisionen auf, keine davon vorher bekannt:

  MF-1282 -> MF-1295   `9b0508cf` traegt MF-1282 fuer eine voellig andere
                       Arbeit („elf Pruefskripte richteten bei jedem
                       Commit das falsche Depot ein") und liegt BEREITS
                       auf `origin/main`. Die gepushte Nummer gewinnt.
                       **Nicht MF-1289, wie die Anweisung sagte:** die
                       Nummer ist auf dem ungepushten Zweig `sitzung-2`
                       schon `da349c75` (PLL-Dialog), MF-1292/1293 sind
                       dort in unversionierter Arbeit, MF-1294 ist die
                       Behebung des roten CI. MF-1295 ist die erste, die
                       nirgends vergeben ist — gemessen ueber
                       `git log --branches --remotes --tags`.

  P3-518  -> P3-528    `origin/main` fuehrt seit MF-1279 ein anderes
                       P3-518 („Der Konsistenzpruefer verwirft Dateien
                       nach den ABSOLUTEN Bestandteilen ihres Pfades").
                       Dieselbe Klasse eine Ebene tiefer: zwei Befunde
                       streiten um eine Nummer, und der aeltere liegt
                       schon draussen.

Der Inhalt des Commits ist dabei unveraendert; geaendert sind die beiden
Nummern und die Verweise darauf.

WAS DABEI NICHT GELOEST IST

Im Block MF-1280..MF-1299 stehen weiterhin **vier** Kollisionen, alle
zwischen `origin/main` und dem ungepushten, aktiven Zweig `sitzung-2`:
MF-1285, MF-1286, MF-1287 und MF-1288 tragen dort je zwei ungleiche
Arbeiten. Sie sind NICHT hier behoben, weil das Umschreiben eines fremden,
laufenden Zweiges nicht die Sache dieses Commits ist. Gemessen und
namentlich aufgefuehrt steht es in `.unlazy/td0/GATES.md` als H1.

Und derselbe Zweig traegt als EINZIGER `docs/ENTSCHEIDUNGSREGELN.md` mit
den Regeln E-1..E-12 (`48f2f4c8`, ausgerechnet das kollidierende MF-1286).
Auf `origin/main` gibt es die Datei nicht — E-13 und E-14 koennen dort
also nicht angehaengt werden, bevor der Zweig gelandet ist.
