events.title: feat(td0): UFT schreibt gepackte TD0 — und die Praemisse, warum es das muss, war nur zur Haelfte richtig (MF-1297)
events.message:
feat(td0): UFT schreibt gepackte TD0 — und die Praemisse, warum es das muss, war nur zur Haelfte richtig (MF-1297)

DIE PRAEMISSE, NACHGEMESSEN

Der Auftrag sagte: „Kein fremdes Werkzeug schreibt gepackte TD0. Also
schreibt UFT sie." Das stimmt — aber nicht aus dem Grund, den der Satz
nahelegt, und die Unterscheidung halbiert den Aufwand:

    fluxfox `src/file_parsers/compression/lzhuf/lzhuf.rs:215`
        pub fn compress<R, W>(...)          <- ein LZHUF-PACKER, MIT,
                                               aus dfgordons retrocompressor
    fluxfox `src/file_parsers/td0.rs:228`
        can_write() -> UnsupportedFormat    <- kein TD0-BEHAELTER

Die Kompression hat also sehr wohl eine fremde, lizenzvertraegliche
Umsetzung; was fehlt, ist der Behaelter. `P3-520` ist damit behoben, und
sein alter Wortlaut bleibt zitiert stehen.

EINE BAUVORSCHRIFT, GEFUNDEN BEVOR EINE ZEILE STAND

Vor dem Bauen wurde der PRUEFSTAND gemessen: koennen die beiden Orakel
ueberhaupt eine gepackte TD0 lesen? Beide koennen — aber sie
widersprachen sich an fluxfox' eigener Datei:

    hxcfe   40 x 2 x 9    richtig
    libdsk  40 x 1 x 8    163 840 statt 368 640 Byte

Ursache gemessen: `lib/drvtele.c` hat **kein `tele_getgeom`**. libdsk
nimmt die TD0-Geometrie aus dem **BPB des Bootsektors** — und fluxfox'
Bootsektor ist **0 von 512 Byte ungleich null**. An
`libdsk_uftk_pc720.td0`, deren Bootsektor einen echten BPB traegt,
meldet libdsk 80 x 2 x 9, richtig.

**Daraus die Vorschrift: wer eine TD0 baut, die libdsk beurteilen soll,
legt einen gueltigen FAT-BPB hinein.** Sie steht im Kopf des Schreibers,
und die beiden neuen Korpusdateien halten sie. Als eigener Befund ueber
das ORAKEL steht sie als **P3-532** — fuer TD0-Inhalte ohne FAT (Amiga,
CP/M, Apple) ist libdsk als zweite Hand ungeeignet.

WAS GEBAUT WURDE

`uft_td0_lzhuf_packen()` steht in DERSELBEN Datei wie der Entpacker und
teilt mit ihm Baumaufbau und Baumumbau — waeren es zwei Fassungen,
drifteten sie, und der Bruch faende erst ein fremder Leser (MF-1177).

**Was er nicht tut, steht im Header:** er gibt nur Literale aus, nie
einen LZ-Treffer. Der Strom ist gueltig, weil der adaptive Huffman-Baum
auf beiden Seiten identisch waechst; er ist nur schlechter gepackt. Das
kostet wenig, weil TD0 seine Wiederholungen eine Schicht frueher
abfaengt: Verfahren 1 macht aus einem gleichfoermigen 512-Byte-Sektor
fuenf Byte.

`uft_td0_schreibe_gepackt()` baut den Behaelter und setzt ALLE DREI
Pruefsummen — seit MF-1296 rechnet UFTs eigener Leser sie nach, und eine
Pruefdatei, die ihre eigene Zusage nicht halten kann, ist keine.

DER BELEG SIND ZWEI FREMDE LESER, NICHT DER EIGENE

Ein Rundlauf durch den eigenen Entpacker waere die Gestalt von MF-1009
(`apridisk`), wo Packer und Entpacker Spiegelbilder derselben Erfindung
waren. Gemessen, beide Werkzeuge ausgefuehrt:

                          libdsk 1.5              hxcfe 2.x
    720K   Geometrie      80 x 2 x 9              80 Spuren, 2 Seiten
           Ausgabe        737 280 Byte            1440 Sektoren (IMD)
           Marken         1439 von 1439           1439 von 1439
    1.2M   Geometrie      80 x 2 x 15             80 Spuren, 2 Seiten
           Ausgabe        1 228 800 Byte          2400 Sektoren (IMD)
           Marken         2399 von 2399           2399 von 2399

Null falsch in allen vier Laeufen. Der jeweils fehlende Sektor ist der
Bootsektor — er traegt den BPB statt einer Marke. hxcfe meldet dabei
500 000 bit/s fuer die 1.2M gegen 250 000 fuer die 720K: die Datenrate
kommt wirklich aus der Datei.

**Die Bruecke vom Orakel-Urteil zu den committeten Bytes ist der
Determinismus.** `test_td0_schreiber` baut dasselbe Abbild neu, schreibt
es und vergleicht BYTEWEISE mit der Korpusdatei — 367 290 gegen
367 290, 608 535 gegen 608 535. Ohne diese Zusage bezoege sich das
Urteil oben auf Bytes, die niemand mehr nachbauen kann.

KORPUS >= 3, UND EINER DAVON VON FREMDER HAND

    fluxfox_sector_test_360k.td0    4 680 B   FREMD, MIT
    uft_gepackt_pc720.td0         367 290 B   eigen, von beiden bestaetigt
    uft_gepackt_pc1200.td0        608 535 B   eigen, von beiden bestaetigt

Die fremde ist Pflicht, sonst waere der Korpus ein Selbstgespraech; das
Tor `G7` prueft genau das.

DIE LIZENZ WURDE GELESEN, NICHT ENTSCHIEDEN

`tools/uft-scout/work/fluxfox/LICENSE` sagt MIT, `Copyright (c) 2024
Daniel Balsom`. Aber eine MIT-Lizenz auf ein Depot macht fremden Inhalt
darin nicht MIT, und der Urheber hat selbst unterschieden:
`tests/images/transylvania/` traegt eine EIGENE LICENSE.txt (Polarware/
Penguin, Weitergabe nur unentgeltlich) und ist NICHT benutzbar.

Der Fremdcode-Befund fuer die uebernommene Datei ist gemessen, nicht
behauptet: `CREDITS.md` nennt einen Bootsektor von 1991 — im Abbild
steckt er nicht, der Bootsektor ist **0 von 512 Byte ungleich null**.
fluxfox' `--sector_test` laesst ihn ausdruecklich aus
(`create/mod.rs:88`, `chsn_iter().skip(1)`).

**Und der Baum wusste das Meiste schon:** der Orakel-Eintrag `fluxfox`
traegt seit MF-1071 `licence="MIT (Daniel Balsom, 2024)"` und benennt
die Transylvania-Grenze woertlich. Neu ist allein der Bootsektor-Befund.

GEAENDERT   src/formats/td0/uft_td0_lzss.c (+131 Z., der Packer),
            src/formats/td0/uft_td0_schreiber.c (NEU, der Behaelter),
            include/uft/formats/uft_td0.h (`uft_td0_lzhuf_packen`,
              `uft_td0_schreibsatz_t`, `uft_td0_schreibe_gepackt`),
            tests/test_td0_schreiber.c (NEU, 5 Gruppen),
            tests/corpus_free/uft_gepackt_pc720.td0 (NEU),
            tests/corpus_free/uft_gepackt_pc1200.td0 (NEU),
            tests/corpus_free/fluxfox_sector_test_360k.td0 (NEU, fremd),
            tests/corpus_manifest/manifest.json (drei Eintraege),
            tests/CMakeLists.txt, UnifiedFloppyTool.pro,
            docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md (P3-520 behoben, P3-532 neu), docs/STAND.md

BELEGT      `test_td0_schreiber` 5 von 5 Gruppen · beide Orakel wie oben ·
            Tor `Korpus-Herkunft` 0 Befunde bei 86 cross-tool-Eintraegen ·
            `verify_build_sources.py` ohne neue Abweichung ·
            Basisname `uft_td0_schreiber.c` einmalig geprueft (zwingend
            vor jeder neuen `.c`) · `git check-attr text` meldet fuer
            beide neuen Korpusdateien `unset` (H6: ohne `-text` haette
            derselbe Beleg auf zwei Rechnern zwei Summen).
            Packrate gemessen: 720K 49,8 %, 1.2M 49,5 %.

ROT-PROBE   Der Packer wurde ZUERST gegen den vorhandenen Entpacker
            gefahren, fuenf Faelle, alle byteidentisch zurueck: ein Byte,
            256 verschiedene Werte (108,6 % — der schlechteste Fall fuer
            einen Huffman), 8192 x 0xE5 (13,0 %), 16 384 Zufall (100,7 %),
            200 000 gemischt (23,7 %). **Das ist die
            Entwicklungsschleife, NICHT der Beweis** — dieselbe Hand auf
            beiden Seiten. Der Beweis steht oben.
            Die Gegenprobe gegen die Identitaet steht IM Test: die
            Kennung muss klein geschrieben sein (`td`, nicht `TD`), und
            die Datei muss kleiner sein als das Sektorabbild. Ohne sie
            waere ein Schreiber, der gar nicht packt, gruen.

GESTOPPT    **P3-532** — libdsk nimmt die TD0-Geometrie aus dem
            Dateisystem. `docs/ORACLES.md` fuehrt es ohne diese
            Einschraenkung; sie gehoert dorthin, damit der naechste Lauf
            sie nicht neu misst.
            **Der Schreiber hat keinen Produktivaufrufer.** Er ist ein
            Korpus-Werkzeug, kein Weg fuer den Bediener — dieselbe Lage
            wie bei den elf Schreibern aus P3-204, nur von Anfang an
            benannt statt nachtraeglich gemessen.

RISIKO      **Der Packer gibt nur Literale aus.** Gueltig, aber ein
            fremder Leser, der LZ-Treffer erwartet, bekommt hier nie
            welche — geprueft ist also, dass beide Orakel einen
            literal-only-Strom nehmen, NICHT dass sie jeden gueltigen
            LZHUF-Strom nehmen. Wer spaeter Treffer ergaenzt, braucht
            denselben Orakel-Lauf noch einmal.
            **Drei Testziele binden weiterhin nicht**
            (`test_format_tab_*`, `UftFlowLayout` aus unverfolgten
            Dateien des Nebenlaufs). Der Zustand ist aelter als dieser
            Commit und liegt ausserhalb seiner Reichweite.
            **Und keines der beiden Orakel laeuft in CI.** Ihr Urteil
            steht als Zahl im Manifest und im Testkopf; was CI prueft,
            ist der Determinismus, der beides verbindet.

events.title: fix(td0): drei Pruefsummen lagen in der Datei und keine wurde gerechnet — und die vierte gibt es gar nicht (MF-1296)
events.message:
fix(td0): drei Pruefsummen lagen in der Datei und keine wurde gerechnet — und die vierte gibt es gar nicht (MF-1296)

DER AUFTRAG UND WAS DIE MESSUNG DARAN BERICHTIGT HAT

Der Auftrag lautete: „TD0 traegt eine CRC im Spurkopf, eine im
Sektorkopf und eine ueber die Daten. Der Baum rechnet keine nach.
`sec_hdr[5]` ist laut eigenem Header die Sektorkopf-CRC und wird null
Mal gelesen."

Die zweite Haelfte stimmt. Die erste nicht — **und der eigene Header
irrt.** `include/uft/formats/uft_td0.h` nannte `sec_hdr[5]` „Sector
header CRC-8". Zwei unabhaengige Haende im Baum sagen, dass das Feld
die DATEN deckt:

    SAMdisk td0.cpp:53   uint8_t data_crc;
                         // Low 8-bits of sector data CRC
    SAMdisk td0.cpp:277  CrcTd0Block(data, size) & 0xff  gegen  data_crc
    libdsk drvtele.c:133 „buf[5] is the CRC, ignored on load"
    libdsk drvtele.c:138 Formatflag 0x02 -> ST2 0x20,
                         „Data Error in Data Field"

**Und es ist AM OBJEKT bewiesen, nicht an einer zweiten Beschreibung.**
Ein Bit gekippt, je Ort einmal:

    Dateikopf       CRC 0x6EDD -> 0x84CC          gefangen
    Spurkopf        CRC 0x34   -> 0xBD            gefangen
    Sektordaten     1439 von 1440 bleiben gut     gefangen
    SEKTORKOPF      nichts faellt                 UNGEDECKT

TD0 schuetzt seine Sektor-IDENTITAET durch nichts. Zylinder, Kopf,
Nummer und Groesse eines Sektors koennen still verfaelscht werden, und
keine Pruefsumme der Datei bemerkt es. Das steht als **P3-529**.

Folge fuer das Zentrum, und sie ist eine Absage: `id_crc_known` bleibt
fuer TD0 **false**. Das Feld bedeutet dort woertlich „false = das Format
traegt keine Angabe"; etwas anderes einzutragen waere eine erfundene
Zusage. Aus „drei CRCs, drei Befunde" werden damit **drei Pruefsummen
und ein vierter Befund**.

WAS DER SPURKOPF HAETTE VERHINDERN KOENNEN

MF-1284 kamen aus einem falsch gelesenen Strom 188 Zylinder und null
Sektoren heraus. `trk_hdr[3]` ist die Pruefsumme ueber die drei Byte
davor und stand im Code als blosser Kommentar. Sie sagt es beim ERSTEN
falschen Byte, nicht beim 255. Muellzylinder. Seit MF-1296 beendet ein
Spurkopf mit falscher Pruefsumme die Spur mit `UFT_TRACK_HDR_CRC`,
statt hinter ihm weiterzusuchen — denn hinter einem Kopf, dessen Zahlen
nicht stimmen, ist die Sektorzahl unbrauchbar.

**Eine gespeicherte NULL heisst dabei „keine Angabe", nicht „die CRC
ist 0"** — so sagt es SAMdisks `if (tt.crc && crc != tt.crc)`.

ZWEI AUSSAGEN, NICHT EINE

`crc_ok` je Sektor kam bisher aus `sec_flags & UFT_TD0_SEC_CRC`, also
aus dem, was der Erzeuger BEHAUPTET. Jetzt steht daneben, was GEMESSEN
wurde. Beide gelten: eine Flagge, die einen Fehler behauptet, wird von
einer stimmenden Pruefsumme nicht ueberstimmt, und umgekehrt.

Gerechnet wird ueber die volle Sektorgroesse, nicht ueber das, was der
eigene Entpacker erzeugt hat. Bleibt er kurz, faellt die Pruefsumme —
das ist kein Nachteil, sondern eine unabhaengige Probe auf den EIGENEN
Dekoder.

EINE NEUE FLAGGE, UND IHR ANLASS IST GEMESSEN

`UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED` sagt, **ob** nachgerechnet wurde — nicht, was
herauskam. Ohne sie ist `crc_ok` zweideutig zwischen „geprueft und gut"
und „niemand hat nachgesehen", weil `uft_format_add_sector()`
unbedingt `UFT_SECTOR_OK` setzt (MF-980).

Der Anlass ist kein Gedankenspiel: die Bruecke ins Zentrum leitete
`data_crc_known` aus `crc_stored != 0 || crc_calculated != 0` ab. Ein
Sektor, dessen Pruefsumme 0x00 ist und STIMMT, haette damit „nicht
gemessen" gemeldet. In `libdsk_uftk_pc720.td0` trifft das **2 von 1440**
Sektoren.

GEAENDERT   include/uft/formats/uft_td0.h — `uft_td0_crc()` deklariert;
              die beiden falschen Feldbeschreibungen berichtigt (die
              alte Fassung bleibt ZITIERT stehen),
            include/uft/uft_types.h — `UFT_TRACK_HDR_CRC = (1 << 6)`,
              `UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED = (1 << 7)`, beide mit
              ausdruecklichem Zahlenwert,
            src/formats/td0/uft_td0.c — `uft_td0_crc()`, Spurkopf-
              Pruefung, gemessene Sektorpruefsumme, `id.crc = 0` mit
              Begruendung,
            src/core/uft_disk2_bridge.c — `data_crc_known` fragt zuerst
              die Flagge,
            tests/test_td0_pruefsummen.c (NEU, 5 Gruppen),
            tests/test_td0_error_marks.c und
            tests/test_td0_erfindet_keine_sektoren.c — ihre Pruefdateien
              trugen erfundene Pruefsummen, siehe ROT-PROBE,
            tests/CMakeLists.txt, docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md (P3-529/530/531),
            docs/STAND.md

BELEGT      **Die Rechnung ist an einer FREMDEN Hand geeicht**, nicht an
            sich selbst: `tests/corpus_free/libdsk_uftk_pc720.td0` ist
            von libdsk geschrieben, und darin gehen **1602 Pruefsummen**
            auf — Dateikopf 0x6EDD, Kommentar 0xFEF2, 160 Spurkoepfe,
            1440 Sektoren, **0 abweichend**.
            Polynom 0xA097, Anfangswert 0, MSB zuerst; aus der
            Parameterangabe neu geschrieben, keine Zeile uebernommen
            (Kanal *Spec*, MF-695).
            `test_td0_pruefsummen` 5 von 5 Gruppen · volle Suite
            **526 von 529 bestanden**, 1 benannter Skip (`test_freezer`).
            Die drei uebrigen sind `test_format_tab_*` und binden nicht —
            **aus fremder Ursache**, siehe RISIKO.
            Vollbau der TD0-Ziele **0 Fehler, 0 Warnungen**; die drei
            Warnungen in `uft_td0.c` sind vorbestehend (gemessen: 3 vor
            der Aenderung, 3 danach).

ROT-PROBE   Vier Bytes gekippt, je eines, und die Tafel oben ist das
            Ergebnis. Gruppe 5 des neuen Tests ist die
            **Anti-Tautologie**: ein Test, bei dem JEDE Aenderung rot
            wird, misst nicht die Pruefsumme, sondern nur, dass sich
            etwas geaendert hat.
            **Und die Suite hat zwei eigene Tests rot gemacht — zu
            Recht.** `test_td0_error_marks` und
            `test_td0_erfindet_keine_sektoren` bauen ihre Pruefdateien
            selbst und schrieben dort Pruefsummenbyte **0**, einen Wert,
            den keine ihrer Nutzlasten hat. Solange niemand nachrechnete,
            fiel das nicht auf. Sie tragen jetzt die richtigen Werte,
            und die sind mit einer UNABHAENGIGEN Python-Umsetzung
            gerechnet und als Zahlen festgenagelt (`crc_anker_haelt()`):
            0xA1 -> 0x2D, 0xB2 -> 0x27, 0xC3 -> 0x8E, 0xD4 -> 0x00.
            Ohne diesen zweiten Anker waeren Pruefdatei und Pruefling
            Spiegelbilder derselben Rechnung — die Gestalt von MF-1009
            (`apridisk`).
            **Ein zweiter Defekt kam dabei heraus:**
            `ASSERT(status == UFT_SECTOR_OK)` ist Gleichheit auf einem
            FLAGGENFELD. Jede additive Flagge laesst es fallen, auch
            wenn nichts kaputt ist. Drei solcher Stellen fragen jetzt
            nach Fehlerbits statt nach Gleichheit mit 0.

GESTOPPT    **P3-529** — TD0s Sektoridentitaet ist ungedeckt. Der Leser
            tut das Richtige; was fehlt, ist der Weg zum Bediener,
            dieselbe Lage wie bei `P3-429` und `P3-525`.
            **P3-530** — `uft_track.h` und `uft_format_plugin.h`
            deklarieren `uft_track_get_sector` unvereinbar; die beiden
            Header sind nicht zusammen einbindbar. Kein neuer Befund:
            `audit_decl_conflicts.py` nennt ihn woertlich und fuehrt ihn
            unter den 35 der Grundlinie — das Tor schlaegt selbst vor,
            auf 15 zu senken.
            **P3-531** — `uft_track_free()` ruft `free()` auf sein
            Argument; auf einer Stapelspur endet der Lauf (gemessen:
            rc 127). Der Schwestertest `test_td0_gepackt.c` umgeht das,
            indem er GAR NICHT befreit.

RISIKO      **Drei Testziele binden nicht, und die Ursache liegt
            ausserhalb dieses Commits.** `src/formattab.cpp:769` ruft
            `UftFlowLayout::UftFlowLayout(QWidget*, int, int, int)`;
            die Klasse liegt als `src/uft_flow_layout.{h,cpp}` im
            Hauptbaum und ist **unverfolgt**, im Bau steht sie nirgends
            (`grep -c uft_flow_layout build.ninja` = 0). Der Aufruf
            kommt aus einer unversionierten Aenderung — im Commit steht
            er 0 Mal. Das Nachtragen einer CMake-Zeile auf eine
            unverfolgte Datei wuerde CI brechen, also bleibt es liegen.
            Der Zustand ist AELTER als dieser Commit.
            **Zweitens:** die Spurkopf-Absage beendet die GANZE
            Spurwanderung, nicht nur die betroffene Spur. Gemessen
            melden nach einem gekippten Kopf an Position 0 alle 160
            angefragten Spuren `UFT_TRACK_HDR_CRC` und liefern 0
            Sektoren. Das ist die wahrheitsgemaesse Folge und keine
            Ueberreaktion — aber wer eine Datei mit EINEM kaputten
            Spurkopf teilweise retten will, bekommt heute nichts. Ein
            Wiederaufsetzen hinter dem Schaden waere Arbeit mit eigenem
            Beleg, keine Zeile.

events.title: fix(864): the device verb asks the host what it has — v0.8.2
events.message:
fix(864): the device verb asks the host what it has — v0.8.2

The second host found this the day it built against the trait. `device`
compared its argument against the literals "c64" and "drive8", so a host that
offered a third device could never be switched to it: their `device fw`
answered the usage line, and `devices()` was called by nothing at all.

The gate under it was keyed on the same literal, and that is the half that
mattered. A device that is not the C64 is read-inspect — but the check asked
"is this drive8" rather than "is this the C64", so a host device would have
fallen through and let every write land on the C64 instead. A refused write is
loud. A write that lands on the wrong machine is silent.

Now the list a host offers is the list the verb accepts, the list it prints and
the list a refusal names, and `Device::is_read_inspect` answers the question the
gate was actually asking. Three tests on a host with a device of its own: it can
be selected, an unknown one is refused with what this host has, and a write
under it is blocked.

The daemon's own output did not change — the transcript gained the device block
and altered no existing line.

events.title: docs: 865 closed, including the acceptance item that was wrong
events.message:
docs: 865 closed, including the acceptance item that was wrong

Rule 9, before the commit and not after it. The spec's status line, its §8
as-built, its row on the board and its row in the archive, all in one place.

§8 records the two things worth carrying forward. The first is that this was
not a second disassembler and the diff proves it: `disassemblePrgToKickAsm`
gained one branch at the top, because the header was only ever where the
{loadAddress, data} pair came from. The second is what fell out of doing it
honestly — the linear renderer had been accepting entry points and throwing
them away, so `disasm_prg --entry-points` without an analysis JSON changed
nothing at all, and fixing that retired a guessed default seed that would
otherwise have started splitting real instructions.

§8.1 records an acceptance item that describes a failure this renderer does
not have. §6.2 asked for a data-filled range to report a divergence with its
offset; it does not, because unknown opcodes render as `.byte`, undocumented
ones as their bytes, and an absolute instruction with a zero-page operand is
forced wide — 256 bytes of pseudo-random data rebuilt byte-identically, and so
did a branch into the middle of another instruction. Data misread as code is
precisely what a rebuild proof cannot see, which is the argument for reporting
the verdict rather than refusing the listing. The negative fixture is a real
one instead: a relative branch whose target wrapped below $0000, which the
assembler refuses by name. A closed spec that still asserted the other thing
would be worse than no spec.

docs/tools/analysis.md gains the raw-bytes section a reader needs, and the
gate goes into the hermetic CI workflow.

events.title: test: eight acceptance items, one hermetic gate
events.message:
test: eight acceptance items, one hermetic gate

A headerless block disassembles and emits no load-address word. It
round-trips, and a range that cannot is reported rather than claimed. A window
of a 16 KB file yields the window's nine instructions and a provenance that
names the range. An entry point at +3 recovers code a blind linear decode
swallows, and without the entry point the tool does not pretend to have found
it. The same annotations file through disasm_prg and disasm_raw produces two
listings that match line for line. Drive code at $0300 renders and
round-trips. The input's hash is unchanged and no .prg is left anywhere the
tool touched. The listing is registered, its provenance reads back, and a
second identical run returns the same artifact id with a one-entry lineage.

Hermetic: temp projects, synthetic bytes, no ROMs, no media, no daemon. 55/55
with KickAssembler, 47 pass and 4 loud skips without it, the way e2e:830
behaves.

The negative half of acceptance item 2 is not the fixture the spec asked for,
and the gate says so in a comment. "A deliberately data-filled range reports
the divergence with its offset" does not happen: this renderer emits unknown
opcodes as .byte and forces exact operand widths, so 256 bytes of pseudo-random
data rebuild byte-identically — data misread as code is exactly the failure the
rebuild proof cannot see, which is why the verdict is reported rather than the
listing refused. What genuinely cannot round-trip is a relative branch whose
target wrapped below $0000: the decoder wraps at 16 bits, KickAssembler
refuses the distance, and that is the fixture.

events.title: feat: disasm_raw — the door for bytes at an address
events.message:
feat: disasm_raw — the door for bytes at an address

Two autonomous runs hit the same wall on the same day, and both climbed it in
the shell. One wrote its own disassembler and called it 180 times. The other
wrote a script that bolts a 2-byte header onto .bin blocks — its own words,
"so the MCP disassembler can eat them" — and made 308 PRGs that were never
PRGs. Both then held listings the project knew nothing about.

disasm_raw is that door. A file path or an artifact id, an optional byte
window, and the address the bytes run at; it renders through the same decoder,
renderer and annotation handling as disasm_prg, proves the listing by
reassembling it against the input range header-free on both sides, and
registers it.

What the project keeps is the point. The artifact row carries the provenance
in prose — which file, which byte range, which address, what seeded it — the
tool run records every argument, and re-running with the same arguments
updates that row instead of minting a second one. Where the bytes belong to a
payload the listing links to it through the shared payload predicate, so a
payload extract_disk created is not invisible to it.

One rule for every number, and it is the rule this repo already settled: an
address is hex, $ and 0x are decoration, a JSON number is taken as given.
offset and length are counted rather than addressed, which is exactly why the
rule may not fork for them — so they follow it too, and every answer prints
the window in both notations. A refusal quotes the rule and names the field: an
offset past the end, a length that runs off it, an entry point outside the span
it claims to be inside.

Annotations can be named outright. loadAnnotations has always accepted an
explicit path and nothing ever passed one; a raw block needs it, because its
bytes usually live under a name no annotations file was going to be named
after. The same file through both doors now yields the same listing, line for
line.

It is not an analysis pass. Handed an analysis JSON it is segment-aware;
without one the listing says it read every byte as code, in its own header,
where a reader will see it.

events.title: fix: the rebuild verdict can hold a window, and says why it failed
events.message:
fix: the rebuild verdict can hold a window, and says why it failed

Three small things the one verifier needed before a headerless listing could
use it, and disasm_prg is better for two of them.

A block lifted out of a bigger file must be compared with the bytes it was
rendered from, not with the whole file — otherwise every window reports a
length divergence at the first byte past its end, which is a false alarm and
worse than silence. `compareRange` says which window, `compareLabel` says what
to call it in the verdict.

An exit code is not a reason. "rebuild assembler exited 1" sends the caller
back to run the assembler by hand to find out that a branch target wrapped
below $0000 or a symbol was never defined — and a refused listing is the
commonest way a round trip actually fails, because this renderer emits unknown
opcodes as .byte and forces exact operand widths, so arbitrary data comes back
byte-for-byte. The assembler's first complaint now rides along with the
verdict.

And a verified rebuild check can be discarded. It is a byte-for-byte copy of
bytes already on disk plus the load header the assembler insists on; beside a
PRG that is unremarkable, but beside a headerless listing it is precisely the
stray .prg the raw path exists to stop producing. Opt-in, so disasm_prg keeps
its own behaviour. A divergence is always kept: then it is evidence.

events.title: feat: the renderer reads bytes, not only a PRG
events.message:
feat: the renderer reads bytes, not only a PRG

The disassembler only ever needed a load address and a buffer. The 2-byte PRG
header was simply where it read the address from, and that single detail is why
every door into a listing wanted a PRG — so a session holding a depacked chunk,
a relocated overlay or a block lifted out of a track had nothing to knock on.

So the header becomes one way of getting {loadAddress, data} and `raw` becomes
the other, and the branch is one line at the top of disassemblePrgToKickAsm.
Everything past it — the decoder, the segment-aware path, the annotations, the
.asm/.tas pair — is the same code. Nothing is prepended to the bytes and
nothing on disk is rewritten. A window outside the file is named rather than
clamped, and the listing carries its own provenance: which file, which byte
range, which address, what seeded it, whether it had an analysis.

Two shared changes come with it, and disasm_prg gets both.

The linear renderer now honours its entry points. It took the list and dropped
it — collectLabels still names the parameter `_entryPoints` — so
`disasm_prg --entry-points` on a file with no analysis JSON changed nothing at
all. A seed that falls strictly inside a decoded instruction now breaks it: the
bytes up to the seed render as data and the walk resumes at the seed. Same
bytes, differently spelled, and it is the rule the analysis path already
applies to an entry hidden in an operand. It is not code discovery and does not
pretend to be; an analysis JSON is still what finds code.

That makes the pipeline's `[0x0827]` default dangerous instead of merely inert
— a guessed SYS target would split a real instruction in any PRG that does not
load at $0801 — so disasm-prg now defaults to no seed at all. Today that
changes nothing: the default only ever reached the two renderers that ignored
it.

`disasm-raw` is the new CLI verb, reading every number by the one address rule
already in this file, and the renderer now returns what it emitted so a caller
can say how many instructions came out.

events.title: fix(864): three shapes the build proved wrong, and an honest as-built
events.message:
fix(864): three shapes the build proved wrong, and an honest as-built

The effect fires BEFORE the verb, not after. `g` is a mutator that appends
timeline anchors while it runs, so truncating afterwards cuts the anchors the
command just made — and nothing in the golden transcript would ever have shown
it, because a timeline is not text.

Reset has no working default. The spec gave it the machine-level reset; the
daemon's warm reset also clears the keyboard, runs five million cycles, resets
the flow stack and marks the machine running, and its cold reset is a whole-host
power cycle. A default doing the weaker thing is worse than none: the machine
then looks reset without being reset. It refuses instead.

Step and resume cannot drive the machine from a default either, and this one is
a shape rather than a detail. The daemon's step classifies what it stepped and
pushes a frame on the flow tracker — which is the library's own state,
unreachable from a `&mut self` host method. So the host reports what it retired
and the library keeps its own books: StopInfo carries the step classifications.
Passing the library's session into the host method would have made every host
import library state to implement a run loop, which is the coupling this spec
exists to prevent.

A second method was needed and is now in: a write reports the bank lens it went
through, because the daemon latches injected and io_injected separately.

§9.1 records what actually moved, what did not, and why — the extraction stopped
where moving would have meant inventing a service instead of extracting one.

events.title: fix: the SFX probe claims what it showed, not what it hoped
events.message:
fix: the SFX probe claims what it showed, not what it hoped

  {"format":"exomizer_sfx","confidence":0.93,
   "reason":"Exomizer self-extracting wrapper decrunch succeeded structurally."}

on a payload whose real codec is a $B3-escape RLE. A 0.93 with "succeeded
structurally" as its reason is a trap: it reads as identification and is not one.

What the probe does is emulate the file's OWN 6502 code from a prologue it picked by
pattern score — SEI / LDA #imm / STA $01 and friends — and watch it write memory. Every
C64 depacker stub on earth passes that. Nothing Exomizer-specific is verified: not the
decrunch table, not the bit stream, not the literal encoding. The honest reading of
that evidence is "this file is self-extracting", which is a fact about the wrapper and
says nothing about the codec.

So the confidence matches the evidence: 0.5 at most, below the probes that actually
consume a declared stream and terminate (byteboozer 0.9, lykia 0.88, rle 0.85), and
0.2 when the expansion ratio is implausible. The BASIC SYS bonus that pushed it to 0.93
is gone — every packed executable has one. The reason states the entry point, the
bytes written, where they went, and what was not checked; the notes name the two codecs
that reach the same result. And `analyze_prg` stops printing "NEXT: this PRG is likely
Exomizer-packed" for any top hint under 0.6, printing each hint's reason instead so the
number can be judged.

(`delta.unregistered.slice(0, 10)`), so the header number was always 10 — a number that
is always the same is not a number. The sample stays a sample; the count is the truth.

`analysis/disk/*/manifest.spec784.json`, `analysis/reloc/*.prg` and
`analysis/rebuild/verify-*.json` came back as "Remaining problems" on every single run
with no way to say they were intentional — advice nobody can act on, which is the
failure Spec 832 D5 already fixed for tool output. The extraction manifest is ours and
gets a shipped pattern. The other two are the project's own, so a project can declare
them in `knowledge/inventory-patterns.json` — `patterns` registers them, `intentional`
merely silences them — and the report prints the shape to write.

Writing that found a third thing: `matchesGlob` compiled `**/` to `.*` with the slash
kept, so `docs/**/*.md` never matched `docs/index.md`. Every shipped pattern was
missing the files at the top of its own directory, and the declaration did not work
either, for the same reason. `**/` matches zero or more directories now, as it does in
every other glob dialect.

And `agent_record_step` recommended `bulk_import_analysis_reports`, which is
advanced-tier and therefore not on the surface the session was reading — ToolSearch
found nothing by that name. `project_inventory_sync` is the facade built for exactly
this and was simply missing the phase; it back-fills the analysis runs itself now,
reports how many, and the four sites that recommended the invisible tool name it

events.title: fix: project_slots reports a number work can move, and stops contradicting itself
events.message:
fix: project_slots reports a number work can move, and stops contradicting itself

Three faults in one report.

`Coverage: 13514 / 1184478 bytes = 1.1 %`. The denominator summed every registered
loadable artifact — 252 extracts, 271 cart chunks, the depacked copy of each — so the
same content was counted five and six times, while the numerator is a per-owner address
union inside a 64 KB space. No amount of work could move that ratio; a percentage
nobody can reach is worse than no percentage. Each distinct piece of content is counted
once now — by the content hash the store already records, else the lineage root, else
the path, which is the rule the UI applies when it shows one artifact per lineage — and
the line says how many artifacts its denominator is made of and how many copies were
left out.

`✓ S5 Runtime count  finding "One resident image per phase, five in all…"` and three
lines below it `· S6 Runtime linkage  S5 has not stated a runtime count yet`. S5 was
answered; its wording simply carries no number `parseRuntimeCount` can read, which is a
different problem with a different fix. S6 now says which of the two it is and what
would settle it.

`Slots: 1/12 filled, 11 open` and later `Slots: 10/14 filled, 4 open`, over a list of
15. Both are internally consistent — the denominator MOVES as conditional slots become
applicable — and nothing said so, which is what made it read as a contradiction. The
header states the not-applicable count and the total.

Also: a slot answer that needs a sentence became the finding's title, and there was no
other field, so the agent had to re-save through `save_finding` with the same id to
repair it. `slot_record` takes an optional `title`, derives a headline from the answer's
first sentence when it is omitted, and keeps the whole answer in the finding's body —
where the readers that parse a slot claim already look.

events.title: fix: the L2 chain verifies what it disassembled
events.message:
fix: the L2 chain verifies what it disassembled

The doctrine says "extract ⇒ always disasm + analyse". `extract_disk` ran both on 245
files and not one of the resulting listings carried the `rebuild verified
byte-identical` line that `disasm_prg` emits on its own — the verification half simply
did not exist on this path. The agent had to drive `assemble_source` itself, 245 times,
to learn whether any of those listings was a faithful rendering of its bytes.

`disasm_prg` and the auto-chain reach the renderer by different routes: the tool
wrapper verified, `runPrgReverseWorkflow` called the pipeline and stopped. The verifier
now lives in `src/lib/rebuild-verify.ts` and both use it. The chain's summary states
how many rebuilt byte-identical, how many diverged and names the diverged ones, and
gives up after the first failure to start the assembler rather than spawning it 245
more times to learn the same thing.

A raw blob is compared past the two-byte load header KickAssembler adds to its output;
otherwise every extracted raw payload would have reported a divergence at offset 0,
which is a false alarm and worse than silence.

Turning verification on exposed a hazard that had been sitting in `disasm_prg`
unobserved: `saveArtifact` dedups by content hash, and a rebuild-check that VERIFIED is
by definition byte-identical to the file it was compared against — so registering it
overwrote the source artifact's own row, and the payload entity pointing at it went
internal. A verified rebuild-check is no longer registered; a diverged one still is,
and says so in its title. Blanket globs were already kept off it.

events.title: fix: a document refusal says everything at once, and the rule reaches its moment
events.message:
fix: a document refusal says everything at once, and the rule reaches its moment

21 of 46 `doc_register` calls were refused in one run, and five separate subagents each
rediscovered the same four-step ladder: kind, then status, then a `covers` entry with a
parenthetical, then a quoted one. `parseFrontmatter` returned on the first problem, so
a document with four things wrong cost four calls — a refusal that reports one problem
teaches the shape of the next refusal, not the shape of the contract. It accumulates
now, numbered, and the covers message says what a valid entry looks like instead of
only that this one is not.

Worse, `- "$C820-$CFFF"` was rejected outright: block-list and inline-list items never
passed through `unquote()` — only the scalar branch did — and the message came back as
`covers entry ""$C820-$CFFF"" is neither $XXXX-$YYYY nor artifact:<name>`, with the
doubled quotes being the bug showing itself while the text blamed the author's syntax.
Both list branches unquote now.

Second half of the same defect: the rule that would have prevented all of it could not
be delivered. `documents-declare-themselves` bound itself to `doc_template` and
`render_docs`, not to `doc_register` — and `doc_template` took only {kind, title}, so
`ruleFooterHandler` resolved no directory and `ruleFooterForTool` returned early. It
was absent from `rules-delivered.json` after four `doc_template` calls. The tool takes
`project_dir` now, `doc_register` carries the rule too, and the rule text spells out
the block and the one-entry-per-line requirement the refusals kept re-teaching.

events.title: fix: the chain guard only fires where the two lengths are the same quantity
events.message:
fix: the chain guard only fires where the two lengths are the same quantity

`register_payloads_from_manifest` warned 232 times in one run:

  CRAZY1:04_pack2@$E000: extracted blob is 8002 bytes but its 26 declared sector
  span(s) cover only 6472 — the block chain looks incomplete (start-only?)

The chain was complete. The blob is bigger because it was decompressed, and comparing
blob length against sector coverage only holds for a payload stored raw. Every packed
payload on the disk produced one of these, and 232 unactionable warnings hide the one
real defect the check exists to find — the Pawn 168/1329 start-only bug it was written
for.

So the guard steps aside when the payload says it is packed: a declared `packer`, or a
`format` among the compressed ones, or `unknown` — which is not permission to assume
raw. A payload declared `prg`/`raw`, or declaring nothing, is still measured, so Pawn
still trips it. And the warning now names its own escape, because a caller reading it
about a packed payload had no way to know what to change.

events.title: fix: one rule for every address disasm_prg takes, and a bad relocation is a refusal
events.message:
fix: one rule for every address disasm_prg takes, and a bad relocation is a refusal

`{"fileStart":"E800","fileEnd":"ECFF","runtimeAddr":"2000"}` came back as
`relocation has invalid range: {"fileStart":null,"fileEnd":null,"runtimeAddr":2000,…}`.
"E800" became null; "2000" was read as decimal 2000, i.e. $07D0. `$`-prefixing worked.
In the same call, `entry_points` accepts a bare "E800" as hex.

Two readings of one notation, decided by which field the value landed in: the
relocation loader in the pipeline CLI fell back to `parseInt(s, 10)` for a bare string.
An address is HEX, `$` and `0x` are optional decoration, a JSON number is taken as-is —
stated once as ADDRESS_RULE, applied to entry_points, relocations and their
subSegments, and quoted in every refusal, which now names the field it is about.

While there: a relocation outside the PRG threw out of `prg-disasm` and arrived as a
full node stack trace in the tool result — four times in one run, once for a zero-page
entry that was a typo. The list is parsed and held against the PRG's own span in the
tool now, so an out-of-range, reversed or overlapping region is a refusal that says
what the span is and what the fields mean. The renderer never sees a bad map, and the
graph import gets the same parsed list the listing was rendered with instead of parsing
the raw input a second time.

`e2e:741` covers this flow end to end and has been red on master since the onboarding
gate landed, for want of one `agent_onboard` call. It is green again.

events.title: fix: a payload door sees every payload that is one
events.message:
fix: a payload door sees every payload that is one

`link_payload_to_lut_row` answered "No payload with id
crazy-news:ram/pack1_nameint1:payload:0000" while the graph's nodes table held 758
payload rows and `list_payloads` showed 269. Two real LUT rows were left unlinkable
purely because of which door created the payload.

The reported cause was `entityKindOf` letting `attrs.legacy_kind` win over the node's
own kind. It is not: `save_entity({kind:"disk-file"})` stores that kind and reads it
back, which is round-tripping and correct — make the node kind win and
`list_entities({kind:"disk-file"})` returns nothing. The wrong code was the READER.
Five doors filtered `listEntities({kind:"payload"})` while `list_loader_models`, ten
lines above one of them, counted `payload | disk-file | cart-chunk | chip` and listed
them fine. Two views of one store.

So there is one predicate now, in `project-knowledge/payload-kinds.ts`, and every door
imports it: the payload tools, the phase gate's payload_id resolver, and the analysis
importer's payload stamp — which had the same filter and therefore never linked an
analysis to a disk-file payload either. A door that refuses now says what it DID find,
because "no payload with id X" cannot be told from a typo.

Second half of the same report: the tool demanded `project_dir` even in an onboarded
session, and omitting it resolved from the cwd — for a globally configured server, the
MCP repo — and died with "Resolved to the MCP repo itself". Onboarding is the session
saying which project it is in; asking again is asking a question already answered. With
exactly one onboarded root, that root is the default. Two is genuine ambiguity and the
old error stands.

events.title: test(864): a host with only a machine, and the two defaults that were missing
events.message:
test(864): a host with only a machine, and the two defaults that were missing

Spec 864 §11.4 wants a second host in the test suite, and writing it found the
trait claiming something it did not do: `machine()` was described as the one
method with no default, but `cpu`, `resume` and `step` had none either, so a
host with only a machine did not compile. `cpu` now defaults to `None` — the
verbs that have moved reach both 6502s through `machine()` and
`machine().drive8`, and a view is what a host adds when it has a CPU those
cannot reach.

`resume` and `step` default to the same sentence every absent service gets,
and NOT, as §3 drew it, to driving the machine. The reason is worth having in
the code: the daemon's step is `step_one_with_flow`, which classifies the step
and pushes or pops a frame on the FlowTracker — and the FlowTracker lives in
MonitorSession, the library's state, which a `&mut self` host method cannot
reach. A default that drove the machine would leave the `flow` panel quietly
wrong on every host that took it.

The test host is a `Machine` and two vectors. It proves the verbs that only
need a machine work against any host that has one — registers, a write read
back, disassembly, the breakpoint and flow surfaces, the help text — that the
absent services answer instead of failing, that the assemble mode and the
device gate are the library's (including over a verb the library does not own),
and that the effect classification is a property of the parse rather than of a
verb list.

Golden transcript unchanged; trx64-monitor 21 + 6 passed.

events.title: refactor(864): the effect classification, and six more verbs
events.message:
refactor(864): the effect classification, and six more verbs

Spec 808's rule stops being a verb list inlined at the top of the dispatch.
The library classifies the command — Observes, Mutates, Replaces — and the
daemon's host acts on it: truncate the future on a mutation, discard the
timeline on a reset. The classification has to live in the library because it
is a property of the parse: `r` alone reads the registers, `r a=$42` writes
one, and the difference is a `=`. A host holding its own verb list would hold
a stale one within a release.

One thing the trait's wording got wrong and the code settled: on_effect is
documented as "what a verb did, AFTER it ran". On this host it must fire
BEFORE. `g` is a mutator and it appends anchors while it runs, so truncating
afterwards would cut the anchors the command just made. The ordering is now
stated on the daemon's impl where it is load-bearing.

`transport_discard_timeline` and `transport_truncate_on_intervention` are
split into functions of the pieces they touch, so the daemon's own call sites
and the host's `on_effect` run the same code rather than two copies.

Six more verbs cross: `df`, `whowrote`, `revdepth`, `reu`/`georam` and `uci`,
with the expansion-port and UCI reports they render through. `cdiff` was in
that group until it turned out to read the checkpoint ring; it stays until the
timeline service exists.

Also repaired: cutting the arms at their `"verb" =>` lines left every leading
comment block one arm behind in both files, so a comment about `bitmap` was
sitting above `f`. Every block is put back against the verb it describes, from
the pre-move revision — including the two the original itself had misattached,
which are reproduced as they were rather than quietly fixed.

Golden transcript unchanged.

events.title: refactor(864): the first half of the verbs, and the daemon as their host
events.message:
refactor(864): the first half of the verbs, and the daemon as their host

About 1300 lines of verb bodies move into the crate's `verbs` module and run
against `&mut MonitorSession` plus `&mut dyn MonitorHost`: the registers, the
memory and disassembly verbs, the fill/transfer/compare/hunt block, `a` with
its assemble mode, `bank`, `sidefx`, the breakpoint and observer surfaces,
`flow`, `focus`, `bt`, `io`, `iec`, `screen`, `triage` and `help`. With them go
the helpers they share — the hex and glob parsers, the screen-code decode, the
control-flow classifier, the help text, the trap-rule rendering, the one-line
assembler's call path.

The library sees every line first, because the monitor is modal: it owns the
pending prompt, the assemble cursor and the selected device, and it applies the
drive8 read-inspect gate to verbs it does not own before handing them back. A
verb it does not own answers `None` and the daemon's dispatch takes it — the
half-moved state the extraction is allowed to sit in, and the shape §6 keeps
afterwards for a host's own verbs.

The daemon's `DaemonHost` is the first host impl. It is deliberately thin: the
machine, and the one thing the library cannot know. `cpu()` answers `None` and
`resume`/`step` refuse, because run control has not moved and a host method
answering something it does not do would be a lie the transcript cannot see.

One trait method was added under contact with the real code:
`on_machine_write(lens)`. The write itself is the library's — it is the
machine's own memory — but the daemon's bus-selection gate latches `injected`
and `io_injected` SEPARATELY, and `on_effect` fires once per command, before
the verb runs, so it cannot carry which lens a write went through. One flag for
both would drop a booted, `wr io`-poked machine onto the isolated core, which
is the 2026-08-12 observers-wreck-everything bug arriving by a new road.

Golden transcript unchanged.

events.title: fix(tor): CI konnte eine eigene Datei nicht zerlegen — zwei f-Strings, die es erst ab Python 3.12 gibt (MF-1294)
events.message:
fix(tor): CI konnte eine eigene Datei nicht zerlegen — zwei f-Strings, die es erst ab Python 3.12 gibt (MF-1294)

DER BEFUND

CI war auf `5d569c41` rot. Von 87 Kategorien des Konsistenz-Tores stand
genau EINE auf 1:

    [git-Umgebung]
      tools/uft-nachbau/scripts/kontamination.py:260
      NICHT ZERLEGBAR: unterminated string literal (detected at line 260)

Das Tor hat dabei genau getan, wofuer es gebaut ist. `pruefe_datei()` in
`scripts/audit_git_umgebung.py` erklaert eine unzerlegbare Datei
ausdruecklich zum BEFUND, mit Begruendung im Kopf: eine fruehere Fassung
meldete „0 Befunde" — gruen, WEIL die Dateien kaputt waren (Klasse
MF-1000/Tor 64). Der rote Lauf ist also kein Torfehler.

DIE URSACHE IST EINE GRAMMATIK, KEIN TIPPFEHLER

Die beiden Stellen sahen so aus:

    f"{'Hintergrund aus ' + baum if baum else 'OHNE Hintergrundbaum '
       '— jeder geteilte Name gilt als beweiskraeftig'})"

Ein f-String-Ausdruck, der ueber einen Zeilenumbruch laeuft. Das erlaubt
**PEP 701 — und PEP 701 ist Python 3.12**. Vorher ist es ein
`SyntaxError`.

Damit ist der eigentliche Treiber benannt, und er ist gemessen:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:47-48` ruft blank `python3` unter
`runs-on: ubuntu-22.04`, und der `consistency`-Auftrag hat **keinen**
`setup-python`-Schritt — die Fassung ist dort **3.10**, waehrend hier
**3.13.14** laeuft. Drei Ablaeufe nennen ihre Fassung (`audit.yml:49`
= `3.x`, `teilstring.yml` dreimal = `3.11`); `ci.yml` nennt keine. Die
Schranke, gegen die jedes Pruefskript geschrieben werden muss, war fuer
den Autor nicht lesbar. Das steht als **P3-527**.

ZWEI STELLEN, UND CI KONNTE NUR EINE NENNEN

Das ist die teuerste Haelfte. `ast.parse` bricht beim ERSTEN
`SyntaxError` ab, also meldete CI Zeile 260 — und schwieg ueber Zeile
302, wo dasselbe Konstrukt ein zweites Mal steht. Wer nur die gemeldete
Zeile repariert, pusht wieder rot.

Gefunden hat die zweite Stelle nicht der Zerleger, sondern der
**Tokenizer**: er laeuft weiter, wo der Zerleger aufgibt, und nennt
ALLE Vorkommen. Der Umfang kam dabei aus
`git ls-files` und nicht aus einer Liste bekannter Dateien (MF-636).

EIN RUECKFALL, DER NICHT TRAEGT

`ast.parse(..., feature_version=(3,10))` sieht aus wie das Messwerkzeug
fuer genau diese Frage. Es ist keines: gemessen **akzeptiert** es das
Konstrukt weiterhin — `feature_version` steuert den Zerleger, nicht den
Tokenizer. Die Abnahme laeuft deshalb gegen einen **echten** 3.10.20
(`uv python install 3.10`), nicht gegen einen Stellvertreter.

GEAENDERT   tools/uft-nachbau/scripts/kontamination.py — zwei Stellen
              (`bericht()` und `selbsttest()`): der Bedingungsausdruck
              steht jetzt VOR dem f-String statt darin, mit einer Zeile
              Begruendung an Ort und Stelle,
            docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md (P3-527),
            docs/STAND.md (abgeleitet: 7862 -> 7863 Zeilen; genau
              eine Zeile, keine weitere Drift aus dem Arbeitsbaum)

BELEGT      Gegen einen echten Python **3.10.20**, also die Fassung, die
            CI fuehrt:
              Vorzustand : 235 verfolgte .py, **1 NICHT ZERLEGBAR**
                           (`kontamination.py:260`, woertlich die
                           CI-Meldung)
              Nachher    : 237 verfolgte .py, **0 NICHT ZERLEGBAR**
            `audit_git_umgebung.py` unter 3.10: „OK (0 Abweichungen)",
            Selbsttest OK, `git init ohne bereinigte Umgebung: 0`.
            `scripts/verify_build_sources.py` unter 3.10: rc 0, „no new
            divergence beyond the accepted baseline".
            **Und die Ausgabe ist byteweise dieselbe** — das ist hier die
            eigentliche Zusage, weil eine Umformulierung genau die stille
            Veraenderung waere, die dieser Baum verbietet:
              `--selbsttest`            : 0 Byte Unterschied, 0
                                          Abweichung(en) bei 3 Faellen
              `bericht()` MIT Baum      : 0 Byte Unterschied
              `bericht()` OHNE Baum     : 0 Byte Unterschied
            Beide Zweige des Bedingungsausdrucks sind einzeln aufgerufen
            worden, nicht nur der, den der Selbsttest trifft.

ROT-PROBE   Der Vorzustand IST die Rotprobe, und sie ist nicht
            nachgestellt: derselbe Zerleger, dieselbe Datei, dieselbe
            Zeile, derselbe Wortlaut wie im CI-Protokoll.
            **Anti-Tautologie:** eine Zaehlung „0 nicht zerlegbar" ist
            gruen, sobald sie null liefert — auch wenn sie am falschen
            Baum zaehlt. Genau das ist beim Bau passiert: der erste Lauf
            meldete fuer BEIDE Baeume 2 Befunde, weil das Messskript auf
            eine fest verdrahtete Wurzel zeigte und den geaenderten Baum
            gar nicht ansah. Die Messung gilt erst, seit sie die beiden
            Baeume UNTERSCHEIDET: Stand 0, Hauptbaum 2.

GESTOPPT    **P3-527** — die Python-Fassung von CI steht nirgends, und
            lokal ist sie eine andere. Drei Wege sind benannt (Tokenizer-
            Tor mit fallender Grundlinie · Fassung in `ci.yml`
            ausdruecklich setzen · pre-push ueber `uv` gegen einen echten
            3.10), und einer ist ausdruecklich ausgeschlossen: CI auf
            >= 3.12 heben wuerde die Klasse verschwinden lassen, ohne
            dass irgendetwas gemessen waere — die Zahl als Motiv
            (MF-1077).
            **Kein Tor in diesem Commit.** „Ein Tor wird allein und
            zuerst committet"; der rote Lauf brauchte zuerst eine gruene
            Antwort.

RISIKO      **Der Baum ist heute allein durch CI gegen diese Klasse
            geschuetzt — also erst NACH einem Push, und dann nur gegen
            die jeweils erste Fundstelle.** Der Tokenizer-Melder, der
            beide Stellen gefunden hat, liegt im Arbeitsverzeichnis der
            Sitzung und nicht im Baum. Das ist der Inhalt von P3-527 (a)
            und steht hier, damit niemand die gruene CI fuer eine
            Absicherung haelt.
            **Zweitens, und das ist keine Vermutung:** dieselbe Datei ist
            im Zweig `sitzung-2` (bis `d26e991a`) und in der
            Arbeitskopie des Hauptbaums unveraendert. Beide erben die
            Behebung, sobald sie `origin/main` aufnehmen — ein Push von
            `sitzung-2` OHNE diese Aufnahme faerbt CI erneut rot.

events.title: refactor(864): the five loose fields become one MonitorSession
events.message:
refactor(864): the five loose fields become one MonitorSession

The daemon's State carried the monitor's memory as five separate fields among
sixty: the cursors and the selected device, the breakpoint surfaces, the
observer registry with its DSL registrations beside it, the interrupt-flow
tracker, and the project's trap rules. Nothing about any of them is about
being a daemon — they are what a monitor remembers between two commands, and a
second host needs every one.

They move to trx64-monitor's `session` module and are gathered into
MonitorSession, which State now holds as a single field. The types keep their
names, so the verb bodies read as they did; the split-borrow destructurings
(`let State { breakpoints, observers: reg, .. }`) reach into the session
instead, and the one that straddles both worlds takes the machine from State
and the registry from the session.

One field deliberately did not come: fs_cwd. Spec 864 §10.1 argues it is shell
state of a filesystem rather than monitor state, and a host without a
filesystem would be carrying a directory it cannot use. It stays on the
daemon's State, beside the paths it resolves against.

Golden transcript unchanged; daemon suite 186 passed.

events.title: feat(864): the crate, the host trait, and the tee where it belongs
events.message:
feat(864): the crate, the host trait, and the tee where it belongs

The trait is the whole design: one method with no default (the C64), and every
other answer a sentence rather than a panic, so a host that cannot rewind says
so and the verb still exists.

Three shapes in it were decided by the second host rather than by ours, which is
why it was worth having them read it. A CpuView carries its address width, not
just its register list, because their firmware CPU is 32-bit and a u16 in the
shared path would leave that device unable to address anything it has. Flags are
an option, because a RISC-V has none. And the debug gates are declared a
capability, because a 64 KB watch table is a 6502 shape and watching the wrong
64 KB silently is worse than refusing by name.

TeeObserver moves to core. It is a pure combinator over core's own Observer
trait, it was private to the daemon for no reason beyond where it was written,
and it is exactly the mechanism a second host needs to chain its observer with
the one the monitor arms.

The verb table has not moved yet; the door says so rather than pretending to be
finished. Golden transcript unchanged, core suite green (587).

events.message:
docs: 862 closed, with what it found out on the way

The spec moves to the archive with an as-built §9, its board row flips to BUILT
with the link retargeted, and the archive register gains its row and its count.

§9 records two things the spec said that did not survive contact with the
machine, because a closed spec that still asserts them is worse than no spec.

The tail call saves 9 cycles and not 6: a `jsr` is 6, an `rts` is 6, a `jmp`
is 3, and the callee's own `rts` costs the same either way. Nothing in the
implementation ever read that number — every Δ comes from the cycle table —
and the gate asserts 9.

And there is no `sax` rule. §4 names SAX among the opcodes to rewrite into,
and a stock 6502 cannot compute `A & X` without a scratch cell: the sequence
SAX would replace writes that cell, SAX does not, so the two differ on a
memory location and every match would be dropped. Where A and X are already
equal, SAX and STA cost the same. The undocumented class is LAX and the six
read-modify-write fusions instead, and the opt-in gate is satisfied by those.

§9 also records the correction the gates forced — `count-down` was asking what
is live after the BRANCH, which always contains the counter because the back
edge reads it, so the rule could never fire; the question is what is live on
the way out — and the one place the acceptance had to be split: ranking by
frequency needs a measurement, a CI runner has no machine, so the hermetic
gate puts synthesised rows through 861's own evaluator and the real capture is
a local gate. Both agree, and on the real machine to the cycle: 13 656 of page
crossing measured, 13 656 reported.

The rules gate also asserts what §5 asks and nothing had checked: every
candidate carries the impact walk's summary, and it is a real walk.

events.title: test: a fixture per rule, the three refusals, and the two things it may never do
events.message:
test: a fixture per rule, the three refusals, and the two things it may never do

Three gates, split by what they need.

`e2e:862-rules` (73/73, hermetic, in CI) builds its own project through the
product's doors — project_init, agent_onboard, analyze_prg, disasm_prg with an
annotations file, save_finding for the free-RAM slot — and runs a positive and
a negative fixture for every one of the eleven rules. The positive yields its
candidate with the verdict and the exact delta; the negative yields none, and
where the rule fired it is counted: the callee that reads its own return
address, the flags that are live and differ, the branch whose final target is
out of reach, the loop body that reads its index, the cell touched once, the
two reads of $D012 that are two reads on purpose.

It also runs the three kinds of code that must be left alone, and each of them
holds a store/load pair that would be a candidate anywhere else. None is
proposed; all three are in the exclusion list with their own reason.

And the two things the tool may never do. Nothing is applied: every file in
the project is byte-for-byte what it was, and the graph's write-ahead log is
empty afterwards, which is the sharper claim — the scan opened the database
and did not write to it. Undocumented opcodes are opt-in: off, the class is
not even counted; on, the LAX and DCP candidates appear with the same verdict
every other rule gets.

`e2e:862-rank` (23/23, hermetic, in CI) is the half that needs a measurement.
The rows are synthesised and put through 861's own evaluator, so the
arithmetic under test is the real one and only the store is not. The page
crossings are known by construction — the index values say 24 of 40 — so the
gate compares two independent answers instead of one implementation with
itself. With the capture, two cycles in code that runs often outranks nine in
code that runs once; without it, the order flips, which is the whole reason
for having the measurement.

`smoke:862` (19/19, local) is the same two questions on a real C64: a sandbox
of its own, a reader daemon of its own, and the shared machine never
addressed. 13656 cycles of page crossing measured, 13656 reported. The cold
routine ran exactly once, the hot one 5690 times, and the list is in that
order. The tool itself is driven over MCP against the store the gate recorded.

The 861 program library exports its assembler shorthand and its setup rather
than having a second copy of them.

events.message:
fix(wandlung): „verlustfrei" stand da, wo niemand nachsehen konnte — TD0->IMD auf UNVERIFIED, und eine Ratsche fuer die anderen sieben (MF-1288)

DIE ZEILE

`src/formats/uft_format_convert_tables.c` fuehrte

    { .source = UFT_FORMAT_TD0, .target = UFT_FORMAT_IMD,
      .quality = UFT_CONV_LOSSLESS,        // „No data loss"
      .description = "TD0 to IMD (preserves metadata)" },

ohne Messung. Inzwischen gibt es eine GEGEN sie: MF-1287 hat gemessen,
dass `uft_td0_to_imd()` die Sektorgroessen einer Spur auf die des ersten
ebnet (P3-524). Die Zeile war also nicht nur unbelegt, sondern falsch.

ES IST KEIN EINZELFALL

Gemessen ueber die ganze Tafel, zur Laufzeit mit `uft_roundtrip_status()`
statt mit einem Regex: **13 Pfade behaupteten LOSSLESS, acht davon ohne
jeden Eintrag in der Rundlauf-Matrix** — also ohne eine Stelle, an der
jemand haette nachsehen koennen.

  SCP -> G64      KRYOFLUX -> SCP   G64 -> HFE    ADF -> IMG
  IMG -> IMD      TD0 -> IMD        NBZ -> D64    NBZ -> G64

`SCP -> G64` ist der auffaelligste: Fluss nach Bitstrom, und `CLAUDE.md`
sagt woertlich „Flux->Sektor verliert Timing+WeakBits". Eine Wandlung,
die Zeitverhalten und schwache Bits nicht mitnehmen KANN, stand dort als
verlustfrei.

UND DIE SPALTE HATTE KEINEN LESER

Das ist der Grund, warum so etwas stehen bleibt.
`uft_conversion_path_t.quality` wird ausserhalb der Tafel genau zweimal
gelesen, und beide Leser sind unerreichbar:

  uft_convert_can()          2 Fundstellen — Deklaration und Definition.
                             NULL Aufrufer.
  uft_convert_print_matrix() 1 Fundstelle — nur die Definition. Es gibt
                             nicht einmal eine Deklaration in einem Header.

46 Guete-Angaben, Dokumentation in C-Syntax. Bestand, nicht Faehigkeit —
wie der Kopierschutz-Katalog (P0-2) und die Merkmalstafel (MF-1176). Der
neue Test ist der **erste Leser** dieser Spalte.

„NICHT GEMESSEN" WAR NICHT SAGBAR

Die Aufzaehlung kannte vier Werte: LOSSLESS, LOSSY, SYNTHETIC,
IMPOSSIBLE. Jeder Pfad MUSSTE also eine Behauptung aufstellen, und im
Zweifel stand dort die freundlichste. `UFT_CONV_UNVERIFIED` ist
ANGEHAENGT — nicht eingefuegt —, und die Werte tragen jetzt
ausdrueckliche Zahlen: eine Aufzaehlung ohne sie ist eine ABI-Bombe, bei
der ein eingefuegter Wert alle folgenden verschiebt und kein Uebersetzer
warnt. Dieselbe Regel wie bei `UFT_RT_NO_ROUNDTRIP` (MF-1283).

UNVERIFIED und nicht LOSSY fuer `TD0 -> IMD`, weil genau EIN Verlust
gemessen ist und nicht die Bilanz. Die kommt aus Schritt 4 des
Umbauplans: Vorwaertspruefung gegen hxcfe, Korpus >= 3.

DIE RATSCHE

`tests/test_wandlungstafel_luegt_nicht.c` haelt seit diesem Commit die
Regel: **kein Pfad darf LOSSLESS behaupten, ohne dass die Matrix etwas
ueber ihn sagt.** Grundlinie **7** — sie darf nur fallen, und sie sinkt
auf zwei Arten, die beide Arbeit sind: einen Matrixeintrag mit Beleg
anlegen, oder die Behauptung zuruecknehmen. Bauform von Tor 57 (MF-883)
und der Sondendoktrin (MF-1153); der Zweck ist der Rand — ein NEUER Pfad
kann gar nicht mehr unbelegt „verlustfrei" behaupten.

GEAENDERT   include/uft/uft_format_convert.h (ausdrueckliche Zahlen,
              UNVERIFIED angehaengt),
            src/formats/uft_format_convert_tables.c (TD0 -> IMD, mit
              Warnung fuer den gemessenen Verlust),
            src/formats/uft_format_convert_dispatch.c (UNVERIFIED und
              IMPOSSIBLE bekommen eigene Zeichenketten statt `???`),
            tests/test_wandlungstafel_luegt_nicht.c (NEU, 3 Gruppen),
            tests/CMakeLists.txt, docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md (P3-525, P3-526),
            docs/STAND.md, .claude/AUFGABEN.md
BELEGT      test_wandlungstafel_luegt_nicht 3/3 · volle Suite 528/528 mit
            einem benannten Skip (test_freezer) · Vollbau 0 Fehler ·
            **0 enum- und 0 switch-Warnungen** trotz des neuen Werts
            (gemessen: `grep -c 'enumeration value'` und `Wswitch` je 0).
            Die 26 Warnungen des Laufs betreffen ALLE `uft_core.h` und
            sind vorbestehend; sie sind nur sichtbarer geworden, weil der
            Header-Umbau 13 weitere Uebersetzungseinheiten neu uebersetzt
            hat — dieselbe Erscheinung wie in MF-1285
ROT-PROBE   Gegen den Vorzustand gemessen: `TD0 -> IMD` auf LOSSLESS
            zurueckgesetzt, gebaut, gelaufen — **3 Zusagen fallen**:
              „behauptet weiterhin LOSSLESS"      Gruppe 1
              „steht nicht auf UNVERIFIED"        Gruppe 1
              „mehr unbelegte als die Grundlinie" Gruppe 2 (8 > 7)
            Danach byteidentisch wiederhergestellt, Nachlauf GRUEN.
            **Die Anti-Tautologie steht IM Test, nicht daneben:** Gruppe 2
            zaehlt, und eine Zaehlung ist gruen, sobald sie null liefert —
            auch wenn sie am falschen Feld zaehlt. Gruppe 1 belegt
            deshalb, dass `uft_roundtrip_status()` fuer ein ungeprueftes
            Paar UNTESTED sagt, und Gruppe 3, dass sie es fuer ein
            belegtes NICHT sagt. Erst beide zusammen zeigen, dass die
            Abfrage ueberhaupt unterscheidet.
GESTOPPT    **P3-525** — die Guete-Spalte erreicht weiterhin keinen
            Bediener; ihr einziger Leser ist jetzt ein Test. Ob sie aus
            der Matrix ABGELEITET werden soll (dann verschwindet sie als
            eigene Wahrheit, Bauform MF-541), ob `uft_convert_can()`
            verdrahtet wird, oder ob es bleibt wie es ist, ist eine
            Entwurfsfrage und keine Zeile.
            **P3-526** — die sieben verbliebenen unbelegten
            LOSSLESS-Behauptungen, namentlich aufgefuehrt. Vorschlag zur
            Reihenfolge: `SCP -> G64` zuerst, weil dort die eigene
            Dokumentation der Angabe widerspricht.
RISIKO      **Die Ratsche faengt das Senken, nicht das Heben.** Wer die
            Grundlinie in der Testdatei von 7 auf 8 setzt, macht den Test
            gruen und die Regel wertlos — das sieht nur ein Leser des
            Diffs, kein Lauf. Dieselbe Schwaeche haben Tor 57 und die
            Sondendoktrin; sie steht hier, damit niemand die Zahl fuer
            eine mechanische Garantie haelt.
            Der Test bindet bewusst KLEIN — nur die beiden Tafeln, kein
            Verteiler — und sucht seine Pfade deshalb selbst, statt
            `uft_convert_get_path()` zu rufen. Das ist ein zweiter WEG
            zum selben Feld, keine zweite REGEL; wer daraus eine Regel
            macht, hat die Doppelung wieder.

events.title: feat: optimisation_candidates, on the surface a session can actually reach
events.message:
feat: optimisation_candidates, on the surface a session can actually reach

One tool over the rule table: a scope (a PRG, a payload, a routine, a range),
optionally a capture to rank against, and the rule classes to use. It answers
with where it looked and why, what it refused to touch and why, the candidates
in gain order with a verdict and its assumptions on each, and a counter per
rule. `show_rules` prints the table itself.

The undocumented class is off unless it is asked for, because using LAX and
DCP is a decision about which machines the result has to run on, not a fact
about the code.

It reads bytes and writes none. The graph opens read-only, no record is
written, no file is touched — turning a candidate into a patch is a separate
and deliberate act with its own door, and the report says so every time.

On the DEFAULT surface, beside the three cost tools, for the reason they are
there: reading a listing for redundant loads, dead `clc`s and page crossings
is exactly the work a session does slowly and badly, and a tool nobody can see
is a tool nobody uses. In the change/patch/crack/port flow it goes at the
front with them — where the goal is speed rather than a specific edit, "what
is even worth changing" comes before "what does this change break".

check:mcp-product-surface green: tool-surface 19/19, matrix 17/17, playbooks
12/12, and the eight end-to-end surface gates behind them.

events.title: feat: the rules that find an optimisation, and the verdict that keeps them honest
events.message:
feat: the rules that find an optimisation, and the verdict that keeps them honest

Finding is a heuristic; the verdict is not. `src/optimise/` is that sentence,
built.

`rules.ts` is the table. Eleven rows, each with an id, a class, the pattern it
looks for, the preconditions it needs, the rewrite and why that is cheaper —
and a matcher underneath it. Adding a rule is adding a row. Nothing in that
file decides whether a rewrite is CORRECT: the matchers propose and are often
wrong about whether they apply, which is the point.

`verdict.ts` is where every proposal goes to be judged, and it judges in three
ways because the rules need three.

  equivalence   both versions executed symbolically and their effects compared
                over the registers, the stack, every memory cell, the flags
                that are LIVE at that point in that routine, and every access
                to $D000-$DFFF in order. NOT EQUIVALENT ends the candidate;
                UNKNOWN is shown, marked and counted, because "could not
                decide" must never read as "fine".

  control-flow  a `jsr`, a `jmp` and an `rts` are not straight-line code, so
                symbolic execution cannot compare them — and `jsr x / rts`
                against `jmp x` is decidable all the same, once the one thing
                that can differ is checked: how deep the stack is while x runs.
                So the callee's own bytes are read, and a `tsx`, a `txs`, an
                `rti`, an unbalanced pull or an exit the graph cannot follow
                stops the rewrite with that instruction named. The obligations
                are printed with the candidate; not one of them is assumed.

  measurement   the structural rules, where the answer is a count and says so:
                page crossings the trace recorded, accesses in the code,
                iterations a resolved loop makes.

`exclusions.ts` is what must never be made faster, and why. A delay loop is
its cycle count; a raster wait ends when the beam arrives; a byte-ready `bvc`
takes exactly as long as the hardware does; and bytes that modify themselves,
an indirect jump or a stack trick cannot be reasoned about at all. Each is a
span with a reason, and the reason is printed — a scan that quietly skipped
the hot routine looks exactly like one that found nothing there.

`free-zp.ts` is where `zp-promote` is allowed to move a variable TO, and the
answer is never a guess: the project's own free-RAM slot, with the distinction
it carries between a claim a run confirmed and one somebody read off a
listing. No slot, no destination, no candidate — and the rule says that is why.

`candidates.ts` looks at hot code first, at routines in raster lines whose
budget is nearly spent second, at everything else last, and ranks what it
finds by gain per frame, then static gain, then address. Without a trace it
says outright that it has no frequency to go on. `format.ts` prints all of it,
counters included: proposed, dropped NOT EQUIVALENT, not formed, UNKNOWN, per
rule, so a rule that is often wrong is visible as such.

events.title: feat: the cost engine can be told what is already true
events.message:
feat: the cost engine can be told what is already true

Three small extensions to the static-cost engine, each of them something the
candidate scan cannot do without.

An entry seed. A window taken out of the middle of a block does not start on
an unknown machine: the instructions before it may already have put a constant
in a register or decided a flag. `SymOptions.known` seeds those facts into both
versions of a comparison, and `compareCost` carries them into the assumption
list, because the verdict holds only under them. `nzFollow` is the one fact
that is a relation rather than a constant — the instruction before the window
loaded the register, so N and Z already say what a reload would say. Without
it a redundant `clc` and a second `lda #$01` are UNKNOWN forever; with it they
are decided.

`factsOf` and `nzFollows` read those facts back off a state, which is how they
are derived: run the block's prefix from a fully symbolic entry and keep what
comes out constant. Anything that does is a constant for every way into the
block, and a prefix the engine cannot model yields nothing rather than a guess.

The six stable undocumented read-modify-writes. `dcp`, `isc`, `slo`, `sre`,
`rla` and `rra` are each modelled as the two halves they ARE — the RMW, then
the ALU op on the value it just wrote — so a fused opcode and the documented
pair it replaces reach the same expression for every cell, register and flag,
and an equivalence over the rewrite comes out EQUIVALENT because it is, not
because something decided to allow it. The add/subtract and the compare are
extracted into pieces for that, and the documented opcodes go through the same
pieces, so there is one implementation of each.

And an empty range is straight-line code that costs nothing. It was reported as
"nothing decoded" with no cycle total, which is the wrong answer to a question
nobody had asked yet: "these bytes go away" is one side of every candidate that
removes an instruction.

release: 0.6.2

A feature release: profiler, panels, and packaging.

- CPU profiler: per-instruction counts and cycles in a results dock, a
  per-source-line hot view, and a gutter heatmap in the editor.
- New docks: a symbols browser fed from the build's listing, and a 68000
  instruction reference that follows the cursor.
- Debugger: step out and run to cursor join step/step-over; the console
  takes typed commands with history and completion. Two prompt-framing
  races in the transport are fixed — a stale stderr prompt is chopped at
  dispatch, and the dispatch watermark now moves as the buffer drains;
  either could leave a session looking like it never stopped.
- Editor: Ctrl+click opens includes and jumps to labels; F4/Shift+F4
  tour the Problems pane; File > Open Recent.
- Sprite editor: one-key bitplane re-export with the last export's
  settings.
- Remote control publishes watch events; a pist-mcp shim (source-only)
  exposes the IDE over MCP stdio.
- Packaging: every archive bundles vlink, and the Windows archive also
  bundles the hrdb-main Hatari fork built with MSYS2 ucrt64
  (experimental — stock Windows Hatari never enters the debugger over
  pipes, so Windows CI unit-tests only).
- CI now exercises the emulator suites on macOS too, which flushed out
  the transport fixes above plus a macOS sun_path overflow for session
  control sockets under the deep system temp directory.
